q.en: Which of the following best describes the project manager’s responsibility within the project feasibility study, which documents the business needs and the cost-benefit analysis that justifies the project?

en: The project manager may make recommendations to keep the project business case in alignment with the goals and objectives of the organization.
Making changes on the business case if necessary
Update the business case at the end of each phase
Development of the project business case

x.en:
A very important exam question:
The project manager does not update or modify business documents because they are not project documents; however, the project manager may provide recommendations to maintain their status.

q.en: Which of the following would be a result of a sprint planning meeting

en: A prioritized list of backlog items
A sprint goal as agreed upon by the product owner and the team members
An increment of the product
A sprint toolbox with the storyboard, code repository.

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

A sprint goal includes a description of what the product owner and the team have agreed to accomplish during the sprint. 

A sprint goal is among the artifacts produced during the sprint planning meeting. 

The product owner then presents the updated backlog items during the sprint planning meeting. 

Agile Practice Guide - First Edition, Page(s) 154

q.en: A project manager already has a good understanding of the expectations of the project stakeholders. What action should the project manager take next to effectively plan the project.

en: Assess required competencies against resource availability.
Determine the project budget and funding sources.
Discover needs and decomposes them into requirements
Conduct a kick-off meeting with the team.

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

We can ask the question with another way to be easy, what is the next process after developing the project charter and identify stakeholders?..... The answer is to collect requirements..... The project’s success is directly influenced by active stakeholder involvement in the discovery and decomposition of needs into the project and product requirements and by the care taken in determining, documenting, and managing the requirements of the product, service, or result of the project.

 
 In project planning, after identifying stakeholders and resources, the PM should focus on collecting requirements. This involves determining what stakeholders need and breaking those needs into actionable requirements to define project scope and guide all future planning activities.
 

🔑 Keywords

Requirements Gathering – Stakeholders – Scope – Planning

📚 PMI References 

 
 PMBOK® 6th Ed: Section 5.2 – Collect Requirements (p.137–143)
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Ed: Planning Domain – Requirements Management
 
 
 PMBOK 6th edition Page, 140.

q.en: In which of the following types of contracts does the buyer have the maximum cost risk

en: Cost Plus Incentive Fee
Cost Reimbursable
Time and Material
Fixed Price

x.en:
Domain : Business Environment 

In a cost-reimbursable type of contract, the buyer has the maximum risk because the total cost of the project remains unknown. This is usually used when the buyer is not able to come up with a complete contract statement of work and has limited understanding.

🔑 Keywords 

Procurement – Contract Risk – Buyer/Seller Risk – Cost Contract

📚 PMI References 

 
 PMBOK® 6th Ed: Section 12.1.3.2 – Contract Types (p.471–474)
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Ed: Procurement Models & Tailoring – Business Domain

q.en: A buyer sent the proposal (RFP) to the potential vendors. After a few days, some potential vendors have questions about the terms and conditions. As a project manager, to ensure that all vendors have a clear and common understanding, what should you do?

en: Conduct one- to-one meeting with vendors.
Send a clarification to the vendors via email.
Allow each vendor to submit their own clarification document separately.
Conduct a bidder conferences

x.en:
Domain : Business Environment 

After receiving a request for proposal (RFP) and prior to proposal submittal , some potential vendors have questions about the terms and conditions. SO the project manager should conduct a Bidder conference (also called contractor conferences, vendor conferences, and pre-bid conferences) this meeting between the buyer and prospective sellers prior to proposal submittal. They are used to ensure that all prospective bidders have a clear and common understanding of the procurement and no bidders receive preferential treatment. 

🔑 Keywords 

Procurement – RFP – Bidder Conference – Vendor Selection

📚 PMI References

 
 PMBOK® 6th Ed: Section 12.2.2.2 – Bidder Conferences (p.479)
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Ed: Procurement Practices – Tailoring Guidance
 
 
 PMBOK 6th edition page, 477.

q.en: A project manager is assigned to an agile software development project for a large banking corporation. With the project just getting underway, the project manager has learned about new hacking tactics that present a potential threat to regulatory compliance for the project. What should the project manager do next.

en: Submit a change request to update the risk management plan.
Submit a change request to update the risk report
Analyze the consequences of non-compliance
Review the risks during the project retrospective

x.en:
Very Important question in Real Exam 

Agile practitioners often view compliance as unnecessary overhead that does not deliver value to the customer. Therefore, the project manager may consider 'minimizing' resources (time, money, team members) allocated for compliance. However, to understand the appropriate amount of resources to invest in compliance activities, the project manager should first analyze the consequences of non-compliance.

🔑 Keywords :

Agile – Risk Report – Non-compliance – Team Behavior
 

📚 PMI References 

 
 PMBOK® 6th Ed: Section 11.7 – Monitor Risks (p.453–459)
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Ed: Delivery & Team Performance Domain (Agile Behavior Guidance)

q.en: You are the Project Manager of a project in which team members have a dual reporting structure. In addition to reporting to you, they also report to their functional manager. Also, the team members are expected to do the project work along with department work. You are working in which form of organization.

en: Functional
Complex
Matrix
Projectized

x.en: These are the characteristics of a matrix organization where team members have dual reporting structure, and the teams work in their respective functional areas while performing project work. It simply denotes keeping the project team in the vicinity. Please refer to PMBOK® Guide - Sixth Edition, page 47.

q.en: An agile team is using a Kanban board to track their work. Which of the following is considered an example of WIP

en: User stories that are awaiting selection by the team
User stories that have been fully tested and released to production
Deployed user stories that contain code that has already been integrated
User stories that contain code that is waiting for customer feedback

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

In Agile, and specifically in Kanban, Work In Progress (WIP) includes any item that has been started but not yet finished. This includes coding, testing, review, or feedback states. Items waiting for feedback are actively in progress and are still occupying team bandwidth and system flow.

User stories that contain code that is waiting for customer feedback are considered WIP. A user story awaiting feedback implies that work has begun on the story but has yet to be completed and deployed; therefore, it is still considered WIP .

📚 Official References 

✅ PMBOK® 6th Edition:

 
 📖 Section 6.6 – Control Schedule (focus on progress tracking)
 
 
 📖 Agile Practice Guide (Annex to PMBOK 6):
  → Chapter 5: "Delivering in an Agile Environment" – WIP limits and Kanban use (pages 58–61)
 

✅ PMBOK® 7th Edition:

 
 📖 Delivery Performance Domain
  → Page 28–31 – Discusses flow-based work and WIP limits
 
 
 📖 Tailoring Considerations for Agile: Transparency and flow
 

✅ Agile Practice Guide (1st Edition):

 
 📖 Chapter 5 – Kanban boards and WIP management (p. 58–60)
 
 
 📖 Appendix X3 – Agile Practices Glossary (WIP and Flow)

q.en: Your team has finished identifying risks for your project and is now analyzing the quality of risk data. What should be done next.

en: Applying a probability and impact matrix
Creating a response plan
Running a Monte Carlo simulation
Conducting a reserve analysis

x.en: After identifying the risks and assessing the quality of risk data the project team should discuss the probability and impact of the identified risks, and assign a priority level using a probability and impact matrix – a technique used in the Perform Qualitative Analysis process. By completing this step, the project team can determine which of the identified risks have the highest priority and require further analysis and action.

q.en: In your organization, a project management team has subcontracted work to a service company. The process of ensuring that this service company's performance meets contractual requirements is called

en: Control Procurements
Risk Management Plan
Close Procurements
Plan Procurement Management

x.en: Control procurements is the process of managing procurement relationships, monitoring contract performance, and making changes and/or corrections as needed.

q.en: An agile project is running its fifth iteration out of ten. After the last iteration review, the team members receive feedback from the security department about regulations with which the project must comply with requirements. Which two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two)

en: Ask the stakeholders about the priority of this regulation
Ask the product owner to include the requirements in the product backlog
Ask the team members to include the requirements in the next iteration
Ask the security department for details about regulations
Ask the team members to analyze the impact of including this regulation

x.en:
1- Ask the security department for details about regulations.

 

2-Ask the team members to analyze the impact of including this regulation

q.en: While reviewing and working on the product backlog, who is responsible to represent the interests of the stakeholders, and ensures the value of the work completed

en: Scrum Master
Product owner
The Team
Sponsor

x.en: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product resulting from work of the Development Team. How this is done may vary widely across organizations, Scrum Teams, and individuals.

q.en: A project manager notifies the project sponsor that the mitigation strategy for a major risk did not work. The sponsor states that the same risk response was implemented a few months ago on a similar project with the same result. How might this situation have been avoided

en: The project manager should have researched the lessons learned repository for knowledge gained throughout similar past projects
The project manager should have researched the lessons learned register for knowledge gained throughout similar past projects
The project manager should have applied the avoidance risk response strategy because the risk had been seen before in past projects
The project manager could not have avoided this situation since it is impossible to determine in advance the effectiveness of a risk response

x.en: In this situation, a risk response was implemented and found to be ineffective for the current project. As it turns out, the same risk response was applied during a similar past project and experienced the same result. It is not enough to select a risk response strategy; the project manager also needs to validate the strategy by talking with experts, researching historical data, looking for analogous projects, reviewing lessons learned, etc. While it is not possible, with complete accuracy, to determine in advance the effectiveness of a risk response, past experience is the best guide. Failing to take into account the lessons learned from the past will likely lead to a repetition of the same mistakes. Knowledge gained from past projects should be captured in the lessons learned repository, and reviewing the information in the lessons learned repository might have prevented the same failed risk response from being selected for the current project.

q.en: During the implementation phase, the project manager identifies a new project activity that will not affect the project end date. What should the project manager do next.

en: Update the change log and update the schedule baseline
Update the schedule baseline and Begin working on the new task immediately
Ask the sponsor to approve the new activity.
Create a change request.

x.en: Although the new project activity does not affect the end date of the project, but it may affect the scope baseline and the other project constraints, therefore the project manager should submit the change request first and take approval from CCB

q.en: A project is terminated early, and the project manager sends the final project report to relevant stakeholders. A finance manager is interested in understanding the impact and requests a copy of the report. What should the project manager do.

en: Review the stakeholder engagement plan and act accordingly.
Don’t send the report since the project was prematurely terminated.
Send the report to the finance manager.
Check the communication management plan and act accordingly.

x.en: The project manager should Check the communication management plan and act accordingly because it contains Stakeholder communication requirements and Persons or groups who will receive the information.PMBOK 377.

q.en: During the Sprint Planning Meeting, the amount of work necessary for fulfilling the items requested by the Product Owner seems greater than the Development Team's capacity. Which action makes more sense

en: The Product Owner demands that the Development Team work overtime just for this Sprint, provided this doesn't happen again.
The Development Team and Product Owner collaborate, with a view to removing or modifying items.
Cancel the Sprint.
Increasing the number of Sprints.

x.en: The Development Team and Product Owner collaborate, with a view to removing or modifying items.

q.en: As a project manager, which of the following processes is responsible for verifying that the project deliverables are ready for inspection and acceptance by the customer

en: Validate scope
Direct and Manage Project Work
Manage Quality
Control Quality

x.en: A goal of the Control Quality process is to determine the correctness of deliverables. The results of performing the Control Quality process are verified deliverables that become an input to the Validate Scope process for formalized acceptance. PMBOK 6th edition, page, 305

q.en: You are the project manager of a large IT project. Your Agile team wants to develop quality standards for a project. How should you coach the team

en: Inform the team that user acceptance testing is required to ensure that the product owner accepts the solution.
Insist that test-driven development is implemented along with automated testing.
Ensure that the definition of done DOD is provided when the product owner agrees that all acceptance criteria have been met for the user story.
Determine the tool and techniques suitable for the project and ensure that testing is done early and continuously.

x.en: Definition of Done is A team's checklist of all the criteria required to be met so that a deliverable can be considered ready for customer use. if the team wants to develop quality standards, the project manager should ensure that the definition of done DOD is provided when the product owner agrees that all acceptance criteria have been met for the user story.

q.en: You are using a methodology that calculates the amount of float on various paths in the network diagram to determine the minimum project duration. What tool or technique are you using.

en: Critical path method
Parametric estimating
Three-point estimating
Critical chain method

x.en: The critical path method is used to estimate the minimum project duration and determine the amount of schedule flexibility on the logical network paths within the schedule model. A critical path is normally characterized by zero total floats on the critical path. [PMBOK 6th edition, Page 210].

q.en: An agile team is tasked with the development of a robot. The project manager wants to ensure that before the actual robot is built, the team receives early feedback on requirements and adapts the design accordingly. Which of the following should the project manager use to achieve that goal

en: Prototyping
Design review
Business case
Checklists

x.en: Prototyping supports the concept of progressive elaboration in iterative cycles, such as those used on agile projects described in the scenario. When enough feedback cycles have been performed, the requirements obtained from the prototype are sufficiently complete to move to the design or build phase. PMBOk 6th edition Page, 147

q.en: During a retrospective meeting, an agile team identified a recurring problem that has been causing a delay in their development cycle, consequently increasing the cost of the product. What specific tool or technique should the team members use to get to the root cause of the problem

en: Root causes analysis
Value Stream Mapping
Cost of delay
Five Whys

x.en: The 'five whys' technique is commonly used by agile teams to get to the root cause of a problem.

q.en: Working software over comprehensive documentation? is one of the key Agile Manifesto values. Which of the following Agile approaches helps in achieving this value

en: Daily standups
Chartering the project and the team
Agile measurements
Demonstrations and reviews

x.en:
Agile teams use prototypes, demonstrations and reviews to understand and refine project scope which enables rapid delivery of a working product.
[Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 97]

q.en: At the end of an iteration, the product owner rejects the work items developed and provides feedback. What should an agile team do to avoid this situation in the future

en: Schedule frequent backlog refinement sessions with the product owner to clarify acceptance criteria
Document the product owners’ feedback in the retrospective session.
Ensure the product owner attends daily standups to understand the current status
Ensure the product owner is part of daily agile team activities and provides feedback.

x.en: The agile team should document the product owners’ feedback in the retrospective session. Retrospectives occur after every iteration and at the end of every project. Conducting a retrospective encourages the team to review what went well and what could have been done better. This assessment includes the work on the product, but also the processes, team dynamics, and other areas that influence the effectiveness of the team.

q.en: Which of the following Agile terms means an agreed-upon condition, when satisfied, means a feature is complete

en: Definition of done
Acceptance constraints
Test case
Triple constraints

x.en: Definition of done (DoD) is a checklist of all the criteria required to be met so that a deliverable can be considered ready for customer use. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 151]

q.en: The sprint began two days ago. The team did not reach a consensus on how to address a feature of a product under construction. As a project manager, what should you do

en: Increase Team Velocity
Decrease WIP and increase Throughput
Increase WIP and Throughput
Decrease WIP and Throughput

x.en:
Very Important Question in Real Exam 

When a team cannot reach agreement and work is stalled, the best agile practice is to limit Work in Progress (WIP).
This allows the team to focus on fewer items, collaborate better, resolve blockers, and increase flow efficiency and throughput.
 

📚 References 

 
 PMBOK 6 (Agile Practice Guide)
  → p. 58–61: "Limiting Work in Progress"
  → p. 67: "Improving flow and reducing delays"
 
 
 PMBOK 7
  → Delivery Performance Domain – Flow-based metrics (velocity, WIP, throughput)

q.en: What agile concept is used to empower the team to make decisions and stay accountable

en: Lean Thinking
Self-Organization
Incremental development
Performance Management

x.en: Self-organizing Teams: ** Not command and control. ** Responsibility delegated to the team. ** The team must be organized to deliver what is expected. ** The focus is on the overall team goal. ** Empower the team to make decisions and stay accountable.

q.en: Scrum users must frequently review Scrum artifacts and progress toward a Sprint Goal to detect undesirable variances. Which pillar of Scrum does this represent

en: Transparency
Sprint
Inspection
Adaptation

x.en:
Scrum has 3 Pillars.

1- Transparency Significant aspects of the process must be visible to those responsible for the outcome. Transparency requires those aspects be defined by a common standard so observers share a common understanding of what is being seen. For example: A common language referring to the process must be shared by all participants; and, Those performing the work and those inspecting the resulting increment must share a common definition of "Done".

2- Inspection Scrum users must frequently inspect Scrum artifacts and progress toward a Sprint Goal to detect undesirable variances. Their inspection should not be so frequent that inspection gets in the way of the work. Inspections are most beneficial when diligently performed by skilled inspectors at the point of work. 

3- Adaptation If an inspector determines that one or more aspects of a process deviate outside acceptable limits and that the resulting product will be unacceptable, the process or the material being processed must be adjusted. An adjustment must be made as soon as possible to minimize further deviation.

q.en: An agile team has completed 9 out of 10 stories for the sprint. During the retrospective, a few team members pointed out that they finished all of their stories. However, one team member failed to finish a story. What should the agile leader do

en: Suggest that the team assign stories at the beginning of the sprint based on each person's strengths to maximize performance
Ask the team to address this at the next sprint planning instead of at the retrospective
Emphasize to the team that each member is responsible for their story, but the team is collectively responsible for finishing the sprint
Work with the product owner to remove the story from the sprint

x.en: Emphasize to the team that each member is responsible for their story, but the team is collectively responsible for finishing the sprint

q.en: In the iteration review of an agile project, the team receives feedback from the stakeholders that could result in a change in the product. What two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two)

en: Ask the stakeholders about the priority of this change
Ask the sponsor to approve the change request
Ask the team members to include the change in the next iteration
Ask the team members to analyze the impact of this change
Ask the product owner to review the product backlog

x.en:
1- Ask the product owner to review the product backlog

2- Ask the stakeholders about the priority of this change

q.en: A project started 11 months ago and is currently on iteration 12 of 15. The team has performed well and completed all deliverables on time. However, some team members are starting to complain about the length of the project, creating a risk for lack of performance at this critical stage. What should the project manager do as a servant leader to mitigate this risk

en: Contact the functional manager to ensure that team motivation remains high until the end of the project.
Apply additional controls to the project deliverables to ensure that all milestones are achieved on time.
Meet with the team to reinforce their responsibilities and the consequences if the project deliverables are not completed on time.
Schedule a team event with the project sponsor to highlight the importance of the project and recognize the work of the team.

x.en: Schedule a team event with the project sponsor to highlight the importance of the project and recognize the work of the team.

q.en: A project manager is leading the development of a mobile banking application using hybrid approach. The team has been holding daily standup meetings each workday morning. Due to an unexpected issue 50 % of the team has to work from home. The bank’s management directed the team not to have in –person daily standups. Various team members are complaining about this, stating that there is a lack of information sharing among the team. What should the project manager do

en: Ask senior management for permission to hold in –person team meeting once each week
Postpone the daily standups and ask the team members to update the project manager daily via messaging.
Hold virtual daily standups each workday morning and use collaboration tools to manage project updates
Delegate authority to the team members and ask them to submit weekly status reports instead

x.en: Daily standup meetings are required even if the team is not located in one geographical area

q.en: Regardless of the size and complexity of a project, which of the following provides a platform to an Agile team to learn about, improve, and adapt its processes

en: Sprints
Servant-leader
Retrospectives
Product owner

x.en: Retrospectives allow Agile teams to learn about, improve, and adapt their processes. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 50]

q.en: A project manager was asked to provide an indication of the time remaining on an agile project. What tools can be used to provide this information?

en: Analysis of the business requirements document
A release burndown chart
Story points for the remaining user stories
Pareto chart

x.en:
A burndown chart is a simple tool that tracks a team’s work progress against the amount of time remaining to complete the work. The chart shows the ideal rate of effort needed to reach work completion by a set date. Using a burndown chart helps you:

Communicate progress
Track remaining work
Plan for future events
Reach work completion on time

q.en: Due to the complexity and the number of requirements, you need someone to provide the guiding direction and requirements prioritization. Ideally, this role should work with the project team and provide product feedback, and set direction on the next piece of functionality to be delivered. In Agile, this role is called

en: Servant leader
Product owner
Scrum master
Cross -functional team member

x.en: The product owner is responsible for guiding the direction of the product. Product owners rank the work based on its business value. Product owners work with their teams by providing product feedback and setting direction on the next piece of functionality to be delivered. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 41]

q.en: In an agile project, the project manager finds that the team members are involved in several Different projects due to budget constraints. As a project manager, what should you do.

en: Brainstorm with the team members on how they can deliver on multiple projects within the given budget
Request the project sponsor prioritize and if necessary, allocate additional budget so the team can work on a single project
Instruct the team members to spread evenly across projects so mistakes will not occur within the current budget
Provide an incentive plan so the team members will work more unaccounted hours on multiple projects

x.en: The agile team should work on a single project. SO the project manager should Request the project sponsor to prioritize and if necessary, allocate additional budget so the team can work on a single project.

q.en: Which of the following is an organizational construct that focuses on the flow of value to customers through the delivery of specific products or services

en: Business Value
Kano Model
Pareto Chart
Value Stream

x.en: Value Stream is an organizational construct that focuses on the flow of value to customers through the delivery of specific products or services. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 154]

q.en: Agile team members are estimating how long it would take to develop features for a new application without being overly concerned about accuracy. A new team member is concerned that a lack of planning now would cause scheduling problems later on. What is the best advice that the agile practitioner can give to this new team member on agile sizing and estimating the project duration

en: Project duration is determined using bottom-up estimating by adding up the duration of the tasks comprising the user stories
Once the velocity is established, the total amount of story points divided by velocity will determine the project duration
The project duration can be determined by adding the number of story points completed by the team in each iteration.
To determine the project duration , velocity should be calculated prior to the start of the first iteration.

x.en: Hint: In Agile, project duration cannot be accurately estimated up front. Rather, it can be derived from observing the team performance and knowing the total amount of story points. "The duration of a project is not estimated as much as it is derived by taking the total number of story points and dividing it by the velocity of the team." Velocity can be roughly estimated at the beginning of the project if the project uses the same team, same (or similar) technologies, and other team and project attributes that are same or similar to the previously completed projects. If the velocity cannot be estimated based on those factors, it should be observed during the first two to three iterations. Once the velocity is established and the total amount of the story points is known, this amount can be divided by the current team's velocity to arrive at how many iterations it will take for the team to complete the project work. Iterations are time-boxed intervals, for example, two weeks. Knowing the number of the iterations, the team will be able to tell how long the project will take. For example, with ten 2-week iterations, the project duration will be 20 weeks. . Velocity is usually known after the team has run a few iterations (typically two to three). Dividing the total amount of story points by velocity would result in the number of iterations required to complete the project. With a time-boxed iteration length (for example 2 weeks), an estimated project duration can then be calculated.

q.en: When is a sprint finished?

en: When all the items in the Product Backlog achieve the Definition of Done.
When the Product Owner determines that the Sprint is finished.
When the fixed time allocated to the Sprint runs out.
When all tasks in the Sprint Backlog are complete.

x.en: When the fixed time allocated to the Sprint runs out.

q.en: Which of the following methods provides guidance on the use of a product backlog, sprint planning, daily scrum, sprint review and sprint retrospective sessions.

en: Sprint
Kanban
Scrum
XP

x.en: The scrum method provides guidance on the use of a product backlog, a product owner, scrum master, and a cross-functional development team, including sprint planning, daily scrum, sprint review and sprint retrospective sessions. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 31]

q.en: You are currently managing a complex project that requires a lot of knowledge work. You want some sort of visual management system that can help you visualize the flow of work, make impediments easily visible, and allow flow to be managed by adjusting the work-in-process limits. Which of the following tools can help you in this regard

en: Product backlog
Kanban board
Sprint retrospective
5S

x.en: A Kanban board provides a means to visualize the flow of work, make impediments easily visible, and allow flow to be managed by adjusting the work-in-process limits. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 31]

q.en: Which of the following Agile concepts implies “smallest possible deliverable that meets customer requirements.

en: User story
Epic
Minimum viable product
Theme

x.en: A minimum viable product (MVP) is a product or a project outcome that contains sufficient features to satisfy project stakeholders. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 23]

q.en: Although the team delivered the required features, they encountered several issues and conflicts during the sprint. Team members were upset about this experience and are now showing a lack of motivation due to what has occurred. What can the project manager do to help increase the team’s motivation and engagement with the project

en: Review sprint planning procedures with the project team members
Set up one-on-one meetings with the project team members
Review sprint progress with the project team members
Perform a sprint retrospective with the project team members

x.en: Keyword ( Team encountered several issues and conflicts during the sprint) The correct answer is: Perform a sprint retrospective with the project team members. In order to determine the cause of an issue, it is appropriate to engage the team in determining what could be causing the issue. Discussing with the team during the iteration retrospective is an appropriate way to look for causes and remedies. An iteration retrospective is an excellent venue for discussing both what is and isn't working.

q.en: The team is negotiating the commitment with a product owner during the Sprint planning meeting. Identify the steps that are part of the Sprint Planning: (select two)

en: Team prioritizes the backlog items and discusses what can be delivered as an increment.
Scrum master defines the Sprint goals and set the objectives for the Sprint.
Team review the backlog, latest product Increment, projected capacity and past performance of the Development Team
The product owner helps to clarify the selected product backlog items and make trade-offs.

x.en:
1- Team prioritizes the backlog items and discusses what can be delivered as an increment.

2- Team review the backlog, latest product Increment, projected capacity and past performance of the Development Team.

q.en: A project manager is using a hybrid approach for project delivery. The development team was sized but is not yet fully resourced. The project manager is working on defining the project schedule. What should the project manager do to address the issue of developer availability?

en: Ask the sponsor to provide the desired completion date for project activities and complete the schedule.
Ask the resource manager when the new contractor is available to start and change the delivery date for the project schedule.
Organize a planning session with the development team and use their estimations to complete the schedule.
Use expert judgment to estimate all of the tasks and complete the schedule in the allocated time.

x.en:
Organize a planning session with the development team and use their estimations to complete the schedule.

The activities should be estimated by the team who are working on the task based on their velocity to be more accurate and reliable.

q.en: What are some objectives of running a Retrospective? (Choose two.)

en: Provide the stakeholders access to the team.
Lessons learned and opportunities for improvement
Plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.
Get feedback on the product.

x.en: The objectives of running a Retrospective is Lessons learned and opportunities for improvement and Plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness.

q.en: An experienced project manager is managing a multi-million dollar agile project. The project manager communicates the ground rules to the team but after 12 iterations, the project manager starts noticing that some team members are not following the ground rules. What should the project manager do first to ensure team adherence to the ground rules.

en: Schedule a meeting with the project team to reinforce the ground rules.
Notify the project sponsor about this behavior and ask the sponsor to take disciplinary action
Contact human resources to request a written warning letter be sent to team members not following the ground rules
Ask the functional manager to replace team members not following the ground rules

x.en: Before replacing team members or escalate this situation, the project manager should schedule a meeting with the project team to reinforce the ground rules.

q.en: What should the scrum master mention at the next retrospective if the product owner said that the last sprint failed to deliver value to the project.

en: Cost Saving during the sprint
Issues which were solved
The way of communication during the sprint
Issues that arose

x.en: Issues which come and happen during that sprint needs to be discussed and present on the table during the retrospective meeting. .

q.en: During the middle of the iteration process, a stakeholder wants to delay the iteration's completion date so that the features they requested can be implemented. How should the team respond?

en: Continue working at their sustainable pace and not extend the iteration.
Work extra hours on the project
Delay the iteration completion date
Bring additional developers on the team for this iteration only.

x.en: The team works within a fixed iteration length and must not extend it. The team must also maintain a sustainable pace. (Agile Practice Guide – 1st Edition, p. 9)

q.en: During the daily stand-up meeting some of the team members are frequently taking calls on their mobile. Having a ground rule of no mobile phones during daily stand-up can enhance effectiveness of daily stand-up, who should create and enforce this rule

en: Product owner
Scrum Master
Sponsor
The Team

x.en: Team is responsible for managing and putting the ground rules, which they agreed on it.

q.en: A Scrum team has completed Its first iteration for an important project. A burndown chart indicates that the project is behind schedule. Which two actions should the project manager take to manage Impediments and improve the team’s velocity

en: Move the items with high complexity to the last iterations
Empower the learn to make decisions to remove impediments
Assign the items with high complexity lo senior developers
Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility
Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible

x.en:
1- Look for processes that cause bottlenecks and slow down the team's agility

2- Work with the team to remove impediments as quickly as possible

q.en: A project manager is working in a hybrid environment using both waterfall and agile frameworks Which causes some confusion about who does what throughout the project. What can the project manager do to help clear the confusion?

en: Invite the project sponsor to the project kick-off meeting
Send out an email to the project team to clarify who is responsible for what as it arises
Develop the resource management plan by defining the roles and responsibilities.
Detail the roles and responsibilities in the project charter.

x.en:
CORRECT ANSWER IS :

Develop the resource management plan by defining the roles and responsibilities.

q.en: An agile team is developing a product for a customer. In the last few iterations, the team members spent extra hours creating product documentation and reviewing the contracts with the customer. How would the team's time been better spent.

en: Building features according to the initial project management plan
Developing functionality as requested by the project sponsor
Reporting the extra hours in the company's time and attendance tools
Creating the product increment and working with the product owner

x.en: Creating the product increment and working with the product owner : is the best answer among the choices given, as it represents value to the customer and is aligned with the Agile Manifesto values of creating working software and collaborating with the customer (or with the product owner who is the voice of the customer).

q.en: In Agile communities, people with expertise in one domain, less-developed skills in associated areas and good collaboration skills are known as

en: U-shaped people
H-shaped people
T-shaped people
I-shaped people

x.en: In Agile communities, people with expertise in one domain, less-developed skills in associated areas and good collaboration skills are known as T-shaped people. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 42]

q.en: Responding to change over following a plan” is one of the key Agile Manifesto values. Which of the following Agile approaches helps in achieving this value

en: Kanban boards
Servant-leader
Self-organizing teams
Backlog refinement

x.en: Backlog refinement allows the product owner to change project priorities in line with evolving business needs. This changes the focus from following a predefined plan to responding to change. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 97]

q.en: An Agile team measures story points without completing the actual feature or story. What is the problem with this approach

en: Decrease of team’s velocity.
Increased response time.
Violation of Agile Principles
Ineffective use of a Kanban board

x.en: Measuring story points is not the same as measuring completed stories or features. Some teams attempt to measure story points without completing the actual feature or story. When teams measure only story points, they measure capacity not finished work which violates the Agile Principle of “the primary measure of progress is working software”. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 66]

q.en: An agile team finished coding for the current iteration. Which of the following is a continuous process improvement ceremony that the team will now attend

en: Iteration retrospective meeting
Product demonstration meeting
Iteration Planning meeting
Release Planning meeting

x.en: The iteration retrospective meeting is an example of a continuous process improvement ceremony on an agile project.

q.en: A project team is engaging a development team in another country to develop software. During progress reviews, the project manager identified completion date delays due to rework because there were different interpretations of the client’s needs. What should the project manager do

en: Escalate to the project steering committee and request additional time
Set up a meeting with key stakeholders to clarify requirements
Travel to the development team's office to push the schedule
Create prototypes with the development team to confirm requirements

x.en: Set up a meeting with key stakeholders to clarify requirements

q.en: An agile practitioner was explaining the differences and similarities between agile and traditional project management approaches to a senior manager. After the conversation, the practitioner realized that she had misstated one important point. Which of the following points would that likely be

en: Both traditional and agile methods allow for changes throughout the project
Too much Planning on agile projects introduce risks
Both traditional and agile methods are value driven
Scrum Agile methods are iteration and non- increment

x.en: Agile methods are iterative and incremental. Agile delivers in increments to focus on the important features first and to deliver these features to the customer sooner. Saying that agile methods are 'non-incremental' is wrong. Therefore, this answer choice represents the point that the practitioner had misstated.

q.en: An Agile team is currently working on a complex ERP customization and deployment project. The team is currently facing an issue with deploying a couple of features as the recipient department is not yet ready for the changeover. Which Scrum role is responsible for removing this impediment

en: Product Owner
Development team
Scrum Master
Business Analyst

x.en: The scrum master is responsible for ensuring the Scrum process is upheld and works to ensure the Scrum team adheres to the practices and rules as well as coaches the team on removing impediments. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 101]

q.en: A key customer stakeholder asks the project team to include new tasks in the backlog and begin analyzing new requests. The customer expects results as soon as possible and pressures the team to attend noncritical meetings. The team is frustrated by this situation . How should the project manager approach this situation

en: Understand the customer's perspective and provide mentoring on agile mindsets.
Call for an internal team retrospective and create an improvement action plan.
Work with the team to receive customer directions and improve the process.
Ask the customer to work with the product owner to prioritize all requests.

x.en: One of the tasks of the agile project manager is that he acts as a servant leader and removes obstacles that confront the team and prevent it from concentrating on executing the tasks. In this scenario , one of these obstacles is the customer's requests for unimportant meetings , so the project manager must direct the customer to work with the product owner and prioritize his requests.

q.en: The on-demand scheduling approach used in agile environments is based on the theory-of-constraints and pull-based scheduling concepts from lean manufacturing to limit a team’s work in progress. This is also called

en: 5S
Andon
Gemba
Kanban

x.en:
The on-demand scheduling approach used in agile environments is based on the theory-of-constraints and pull-based scheduling concepts from lean manufacturing to limit a team’s work in progress. This is also called Kanban system.
Kanban Board is Pull System and Visual management to identify the status of Requirements.

q.en: A project for a new product launch is in a very initial stage and the requirements are evolving Due to stiff competition in the market, the customer would like to launch the product keeping the scope flexible. The project team intends to start the work based on the forecast of a similar project delivered last year Which project approach suits the scenario

en: Execute it as a predictive project
Execute it using the same approach as the reference project
Execute it as a Scrum project
Execute it as a project with stage gates

x.en: Because the requirements are evolving and the customer would like to launch the product keeping the scope flexible. SO the team should Execute it as a Scrum project. Note: Scrum is one of the most popular agile methods.

q.en: You are a project manager for an important project. The project is delayed due to the high amount of major changes requested by different stakeholders at different stages of the project. If the project continues on the same path, it will consume twice the time and budget planned. What two actions can the project manager take to be more cost-effective? (Choose two)

en: Conduct a stakeholder analysis
Adopt an incremental approach
Update the project management plan with the new timeline
Leverage work between team members
Reinforce team communication

x.en: Keyword ( high amount of major changes requested by different stakeholders ) SO the incremental approach is best for this project. Also, the project manager should conduct a stakeholder analysis to identify: The interests of all stakeholders, who may affect or be affected by the project. Groups that should be encouraged to participate in different stages of the project. Ways to reduce potential negative impacts and manage negative stakeholders.

q.en: An agile team has been struggling to keep up with the planned pace, which is frequently resulting in sprint failures What should the project manager do to help avoid this situation in the future

en: Switch to a Kanban approach, implementing features on a first-come, first-serve basis, fostering a sustainable pace
Ask the project sponsor to approve overtime to compensate for the lack of performance while adjusting the plan
Replace junior team members with more experienced ones and negotiate the project scope to compensate for the budget gap
Review the velocity of the team over the last several sprints and adjust the plan accordingly

x.en: Review the velocity of the team over the last several sprints and adjust the plan accordingly

q.en: T-shaped people are more suitable for Agile teams than I-shaped people. All of the following are benefits of having T-shaped people on the team EXCEPT

en: This removes the risk from the project.
This helps in forming smaller teams.
This allows teams to self-organize.
This helps in creating a cross-functional team.

x.en: In Agile communities, people with expertise in one domain, less-developed skills in associated areas and good collaboration skills are known as T-shaped people. For Agile projects, it is preferred to have a team of self-organizing, T-shaped, cross-functional team generalists. However, having T-shaped people doesn’t remove the project risk. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 42]

q.en: During a project’s third iteration, a planned activity becomes more complex. The work should be delivered in the shortest time possible. What approach should be used in this situation

en: The team member brings SMEs to help them.
The team should request support from external team members.
The product owner should remove the complex activities from the product backlog.
The cross-functional team members work together to complete the activity.

x.en: Cross-functional teams consist of team members with all the skills necessary to produce a working product. In software development, cross-functional teams are typically comprised of designers, developers, testers, and any other required roles. The cross-functional development teams consist of professionals who deliver potentially releasable product on a regular cadence. Cross-functional teams are critical because they can deliver finished work in the shortest possible time, with higher quality, without external dependencies.

q.en: On traditional projects, a change control board is usually established to authorize change requests. Who is responsible to authorize changes on an Agile project.

en: Product owner
Agile team
Scrum master
End users

x.en: Product owners have the ultimate responsibility of the project success. They prioritize the project backlog and authorize change requests on an Agile project.

q.en: You have asked a publisher to print some Agile principles on posters. When the posters were delivered, you found out that some of them had incorrect Agile principles printed on them. Which of the following posters has an incorrect Agile principle printed on it

en: Focus on technical excellence
Continuous delivery of valuable software
Plan conservatively and deliver aggressively
Working software is the primary measure of progress

x.en: Plan conservatively and deliver aggressively is not a valid Agile principle. The rest of the choices are all valid Agile principles. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 9]

q.en: An agile team is planning for tools they will use for the project. The team members are debating how they should show what work is in progress. Of the following options, which tool are they most likely to select

en: WBS
Product Roadmap
task board
Use Story backlog

x.en:
Of the options presented, the best tool to show work in progress is a task board. The user story backlog shows what work is still remaining to be done on the project. The product roadmap shows when work is planned to be completed. Work breakdown structures are not commonly used on agile projects. 
 

Very Important Question In Real Exam 

In agile environments (like Scrum or Kanban), the Task Board (or Kanban board) is the primary tool to visualize what tasks are To Do, In Progress, or Done. It provides transparency and enables the team to manage work-in-progress effectively.

🔑 Keywords: Agile – Task Board – WIP – Visualization – Transparency

📚 PMBOK 6: Agile Practice Guide p. 58
📚 PMBOK 7: Delivery Performance Domain – Agile Tools & Techniques

q.en: A new team member joined your agile team. He asked you what we use MOSCOW for. You answer him it is used for

en: Risk planning and calculation
Sizing the story
Doing workload estimation
Prioritization

x.en: MoSCoW prioritization, also known as the MoSCoW method or MoSCoW analysis, is a popular prioritization technique for managing requirements. ... The acronym, MoSCoW, stands for 4 different categories of initiatives: must-haves, should-haves, could-haves, and will not have at this time.

q.en: A key team member informs the project manager that they have been accepted to a master’s degree program. The team member explains that the first semester of the master’s program will coincide with the last phase of the project. What should the project manager do

en: Ask the team member to inform human resources(HR) about their enrollment in the master's program
Ask the team member to delegate some of their tasks to another colleague during the last phase of the project
Suggest the team member postpone their enrollment in the master's program until the project is completed
Assess the team member's commitment to the master's program and its impact on project performance

x.en:
A professional project manager always starts by assessing the situation objectively.
In this case, the PM should analyze the team member’s availability, workload, and impact on the project schedule and deliverables.
Based on that assessment, the PM may later reallocate tasks, adjust resources, or negotiate commitments.

q.en:
A project manager met with the project team weekly to evaluate the project’s progress. However, the sponsor requests that project performance be checked daily. The key team members disagree with this requirement and argue that they do not have enough time to go to daily meetings because they are at an executive level. 

What should the project manager do first?

en: Evaluate the capacity of each team member to attend daily meetings in person or virtually and reduce the time of each meeting
Review the communications management plan and submit a change request if required
Negotiate with the key team members to send a daily report and let the sponsor know that the project cost will increase
Recommend to the sponsor that performance of the project be reviewed once per week

x.en:
When there's a conflict between communication expectations of stakeholders (e.g., sponsor vs. team), the first step is to review the communications management plan. This ensures that communication frequency, format, and channels align with stakeholder needs and project constraints. If the plan doesn't cover such changes, the PM may submit a change request.

q.en: You are managing a few projects and the sponsor asks you to submit CPI and TCPI numbers for them. You provided CPI = 1 for project A, CPI = 1.2 for project B, TCPI = 0.9 for project C and TCPI = 1.2 for project D. Which project do you think the sponsor might terminate based on this data

en: Project B
Project A
Project D
Project C

x.en: Project D has a TCPI of 1.2, a higher TCPI indicates a higher ask rate for the CPI in the future which is not good and Harder to complete. All other projects are in good shape.[PMBOK 6th edition, Page 267]

q.en: You are the project manager of a large IT project. During the implementation phase, you sign a contract to rent an additional server from a local company because of the possibility that the main server may fail due to constant, local-area electrical outages. As a project manager, what strategy are you using

en: Transfer
Escalate
Mitigate
Avoid

x.en: In risk mitigation, the action is taken to reduce the probability of occurrence and/or impact of a threat. the project manager wants to reduce the probability and impact by renting the generator.[PMBOK 6th edition, Page443 ]

q.en: If the project manager wants to ensure that the work carried out and the product being created do not deviate from the prescribed business value. What should the project manager pay special attention to in order to achieve this goal

en: Immediately meet with the developers and quality control team to ensure that the quality standards are met.
Carrying out quality audits and failure analyses
Update the quality management plan
Outsourcing the quality management activities

x.en:
To ensure that the work aligns with the intended business value, the PM must ensure that quality standards are being applied effectively and immediately.
The best way to do that is through direct interaction with the team responsible for delivery and quality assurance. This proactive engagement helps in early detection of misalignment or quality issues.

q.en: Which two actions should a project manager consider while launching a new virtual team? (Choose two)

en: Identify the types and quantities of resources required for each work package or activity
Recruit the best resources within the organization to be part of the virtual team
Evaluate the project manager's own strengths and weaknesses as a virtual team leader to identify avoidable pitfalls
Establish in the beginning, how progress will be monitored and the best means for communicating progress
Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

1. ✅ In virtual teams, clear expectations for monitoring progress and communication methods (email, video calls, dashboards, etc.) are critical from day one.

2. ✅ Many virtual team members are part of multiple projects. Ensuring that they have enough capacity is crucial for scheduling and team performance.

So The Correct Answer 

1- Establish in the beginning, how progress will be monitored and the best means for communicating progress.

2- Verify if team members are on more than one team and cannot devote enough time to this team.

q.en: During the closing process, the project manager learns that one deliverable is not meeting customer expectations. How should the project manager proceed

en: Ask the customer to issue a change request with the information to analyze and provide a solution
Meet with the customer to reach agreement on the scope of the deliverable that will satisfy both parties
Review the deliverable requirements, check the customer approval criteria, and proceed accordingly
Contact the project sponsor and ask for help in negotiating the closing of the project with the customer

x.en:
In the closing phase, the goal is to obtain formal acceptance. If the customer expresses dissatisfaction, the PM should negotiate directly to align expectations and agree on what would satisfy both sides. This maintains the relationship and integrity of project closure.

q.en:
During the implementation phase, you want to compare the baseline to the actual results and determine if the variance is within the threshold amount or if corrective or preventive action is appropriate. 

Which of the following techniques can help you

en: Decomposition
Control chart
Trend analysis
Variance Analysis

x.en: Variance analysis is used to compare the baseline to the actual results and determine if the variance is within the threshold amount or if corrective or preventive action is appropriate. [PMBOK 6th edition, Page170 ]

q.en: A project manager led the implementation of an electronic invoicing project that has just been completed. The financial manager communicated that the team discovered three invoices with errors. Which two documents should the project manager update as soon as possible? (Choose two).

en: Risk register
Issue log
Backlog register
Change log
Stakeholder register

x.en: The project manager should update the issue log to record the errors and update the risk register because may be impact the project completion date

q.en: The vendor told the project manager that they completed the scope successfully and is asking for approval. What should the project manager do in response to this request

en: Obtain approval from the project sponsor.
Update the project management plan and mark the milestone as completed
Ask the vendor to validate the agreement for any deviations.
Set up a meeting with stakeholders to validate and confirm acceptance of the deliverables

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

When a vendor claims the scope is complete, the PM should verify the deliverables with key stakeholders and obtain formal acceptance. This is part of the Validate Scope and Close Procurement processes.

q.en: A project manager has been authorized to begin a project and realizes that an effective high-performing team is needed to finish the project successfully. What should the project manager do next

en: Set performance standards and direction
Select members for their skill or potential
Establish the project scope and set clear team objectives
Hold early kick-off meetings and regular weekly meetings

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

To build a high-performing team, the project manager must first define the project scope and team goals.
This provides a shared vision, helps define needed roles and skills, and aligns the team toward a common purpose.

q.en: Internal restructuring by the customer has resulted in the replacement of some key stakeholders. What should the project manager do first

en: Distribute a summary of the project’s current status to the new stakeholders.
Review and execute the communication management plan.
Review and update the stakeholder engagement plan.
Hold another kick-off meeting with the new stakeholders to re-establish the project baseline.

x.en: As a result of the replacement of some key stakeholders, the project manager should Review and update the stakeholder engagement plan. The stakeholder engagement plan is updated regularly to reflect changes to the stakeholder community. Typical trigger situations requiring updates to the plan include:: When there are changes to the organization structure or within the industry and When new individuals or groups become stakeholders, current stakeholders are no longer part of the stakeholder community, or the importance of particular stakeholders to the project’s success changes. PMBOK 6th edition Page, 518

q.en: You are a project manager who is in charge of an important project for your company. In your project, there are frequent technical disagreements among team members and the lead. What conflict management technique should the project manager use to resolve this

en: Collaborate /problem solve
Withdraw/avoid
Force/direct
Compromise/reconcile

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

Keyword ( frequent technical disagreements ) so the project manager should solve the proplem to reach to consensus. Collaborate/problem solve. Incorporating multiple viewpoints and insights from differing perspectives;requires a cooperative attitude and open dialogue that typically leads to consensus and commitment. This approach can result in a win-win situation.
PMBOK 6th edition page, 349.

q.en: A project manager has been assigned to a project where the budget is very tight. Incurring extra costs is not an option. What should the project manager do to manage this situation

en: Ask the project resources to finish their assignments in less time than originally planned
Monitor the budget for the project continually and anticipate any issues if possible
Ask the accounting department to forward all project expenses to the project manager's email
File a change request to make the customer billable for all extra costs incurred for the project

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

In a project with tight budget constraints, the project manager must apply cost control techniques, including continual budget monitoring, forecasting, and early risk identification.
This proactive management ensures financial discipline and prevents deviations.

q.en: You are a project manager for an important project. due to a technical issue with the sub-supplier, there is a potential delay in delivery. To stay on schedule, the vendor proposed replacing the sub- supplier’s component with a similar part that is different from the one that is stipulated in the project specifications. As a project manager, what should you do next.

en: Instruct the vendor to use the part that is compliant with the project specifications and update the schedule
Consult with a subject matter expert (SME) to see if the proposed change is acceptable
Accept the proposed replacement in order to keep procurement activities on track
Insist on using the component per the project specifications and air freight the equipment to mitigate the delay

x.en: Keyword ( What should you do next ) The project manager should Consult with a subject matter expert (SME) to see if the proposed change is acceptable or not then he can take the Right decision. If the proposed change is not acceptable, so the project manager should Instruct the vendor to use the part that is compliant with the project specifications.

q.en: You are the project manager of a large project for your organization. You have recently reported that the project’s SPI is 0.85 and the CPI is 1.17. You want to focus that the project is under control in the next project status review. How should the project manager report the project status to key stakeholders

en: Use Pareto chart and why- why diagram to demonstrate that the project is under control
Report that the project is behind schedule but that an additional experienced resource can be added to stay within schedule and maintain the budget
Report that the project is not tracking as expected, but is still under control
Prepare a detailed presentation for stakeholders on earned value, including how it’s calculated

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

The project's SPI is 0.85 and the CPI is 1.17. SO the project is behind schedule and under budget. The project manager should report that the project is behind schedule but that an additional experienced resource can be added to stay within schedule and maintain the budget. 0.85

q.en: You are authorized to approve expenditures above $15,000. For the last several weeks, you have been negotiating the terms and pricing of a contract with a vendor, and you want to keep costs as low as possible. This has been an exceedingly difficult negotiation process. A colleague suggests you tell the vendor you can only approve expenses below $10,000 as a way to keep the price low. What do you do?

en: Put a deadline on the negotiation completion
Tell the vendor you are only authorized to approve expenses under $10,000
Ask for binding arbitration
Do not follow the colleague's advice

x.en: Do not follow your colleague's advice. Providing false or misleading information for any reason is a violation of the PMI Code of Ethics.

q.en: During project execution, a project manager learns that a team member’s functional manager believes they shouldn’t execute a certain task. What document should the project manager review to resolve this

en: RACI (responsible, accountable, consult, and inform) chart
Work breakdown structure (WBS)
Organizational chart
Resource management plan

x.en: The RACI chart is useful for ensuring team members' roles and responsibilities are clear, especially when the team consists of internal and external resources.

q.en: During project execution, a high-performing team member leaves. Following this loss, a planned quality audit is conducted that indicates the work product’s quality standards are unmet. What should the project manager do next

en: Crash the schedule
Create a cause and effect diagram
Perform a reserve analysis of the work performance
Consult the resource management plan

x.en: Keyword ( Following this loss ) may be the issue not only related to the leaving of the team member. Since the work product’s quality standards are unmet , the project manager should FIRST Create a cause and effect diagram to identify the main or root cause of the problem.

q.en: A highly skilled team resource received a job offer and is leaving the project soon. What should the project manager do to maintain project performance while a new team member is being onboarded

en: Offer to cross-train and mentoring to the new team member
Share project documents with the new team member
Motivate the new team member to perform
Log a risk in the risk register and work with the new team member to mitigate it

x.en: Offer to cross-train and mentoring to the new team member

q.en: The project manager has recently received funding approval for a training program for the entire project team but has not yet defined the most effective training course. One team member submitted a request for specialized training that is required for the project. How should the project manager handle this request

en: Reject the request as it does not impact the project deliverables
Approve the request for the specialized training
Validate if the training is within scope and budget.
Send this change request to the change control board (CCB) for approval.

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

 

Before approving or rejecting the request, the project manager must validate that the training:

 
 Is within the approved scope
 
 
 Fits the training budget
 
 
 Is aligned with project objectives
 

This step ensures responsible use of project funds and alignment with the project’s performance needs.

q.en: A team member in a hybrid organization informs the project manager of a new way to execute an activity with a shorter duration. The project manager has not used the new process before, but a trusted team member explains that their previous experience with the process validates the efficacy of the new process. Which two actions should the project manager take? (Choose two)

en: Assess the impact and implement this new process.
Postpone the decision until the next sprint
Update the project schedule.
Update the work breakdown structure (WBS)
Involve the team member's functional manager.

x.en:
Assess the impact and implement this new process

Update the project schedule.

q.en: During project execution, the risk owner is monitoring the critical speed rate of a power engine to eventually trigger the defined risk-response strategy. During the risk analysis and management process phase, it was defined that the power engine has the following characteristics 1,600 rpm (rate-per-minute) -> stops working and crashes the system 1.500 rpm (rate-per-minute) -> warns of max rate allowed 1.400pm (rate-per-minute) -> reduces the power and brakes the engine Which of the following statements is correct

en: 1.600 rpm is an event that triggers a response strategy. 1,500 rpm is a project issue and 1,400 rpm is a project risk.
1600 rpm is a project issue; 1,500 rpm is a project risk; and 1,400 rpm is an event that triggers a response strategy
1,600 rpm is a project issue, 1,500 rpm is an event that triggers a response strategy and 1,400 rpm is a project risk
1,600 rpm is a project risk, 1,500 rpm is an event that triggers a response strategy and 1,400 rpm is a project issue.

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 
1,600 rpm (rate-per-minute) -> stops working and crashes the system so 1600 rpm is a project issue. 1.500 rpm (rate-per-minute) -> warns of max rate allowed so 1,500 rpm is an event that triggers a response strategy. 1.400pm (rate-per-minute) -> reduces the power and brakes the engine so 1,400 rpm is is a project risk

q.en: You are a project manager managing a construction project. The project schedule is negatively impacted due to one team member’s performance. If the project’s deliverables due date are approaching, what should you do as a project manager

en: Mentor the team member
Acquiring a more skilled resource.
Remove the team member from the project.
Schedule training sessions for the team member to optimize his performance.

x.en: Mentor the team member is the best option and will be the first action to do. Schedule training sessions for the team member will take more time and the project is impacted negatively.

q.en: Stakeholders in some industries prefer to deal with programmers and system analysts directly, bypassing project managers. This complicates managing resources on projects How should a project manager solve this issue

en: Propose implementing a new project management information system (PMIS).
Host a team-building event to develop team cohesion and improve communication
Promote the adoption of the communications management plan with the project team.
Request a meeting with senior management to escalate the situation.

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

When stakeholders bypass the PM, it undermines governance and can lead to misaligned work.
Reinforcing the communications management plan ensures the right flow of information and supports authority structure.

q.en: A company is running a project to eliminate a sales channel that has been unprofitable for the past 3 years. A key stakeholder from another area, who has legacy ties to that sales channel, objects to the project. What should the project manager do in this situation

en: Assess the impact of the stakeholder and engage properly
Develop a specific communications strategy for this stakeholder
Use interpersonal skills to gain stakeholder engagement
Escalate the stakeholder issue to the project sponsor

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

To resolve stakeholder resistance, the PM must begin with a stakeholder analysis. 

This ensures communication and engagement strategies are aligned with the stakeholder’s influence, interest, and concerns.

 PMBOK® 6th Edition:

  📖 Section 13.2 – Plan Stakeholder Engagement

q.en: A project manager primarily works on implementation projects. Depending on the deliverable, the project manager is able to estimate the timeline based on previous projects. The project manager now receives a project that is different from the previous implementation projects. What should the project manager do next

en: Use expert judgment to estimate the schedule and then adjust the schedule as the project progresses
Ask the project management office (PMO) by when the project can be completed and use that date as the project timeline
Break down the project into smaller tasks and estimate the durations of the activities.
Refer to the previous project they worked on and base the estimate on that

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

For a new or unfamiliar project, using bottom-up estimation by breaking work into tasks and estimating each is the most accurate and defensible method.

 PMBOK® 6th Edition:

  📖 Section 6.4.2.5 – Bottom-Up Estimating
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Edition:
