  📖 Measurement and Planning Tailoring Considerations

q.en: During the course of a project, the team develops negative group behaviors and becomes unmotivated and unproductive. What should the project manager do to improve the project team’s performance

en: Escalate poor performance to functional managers
Update the stakeholder engagement plan
Conduct a root cause analysis session
Define and analyze performance metrics

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

Root cause analysis is a best practice for diagnosing team dysfunction before reacting. It allows a tailored, effective solution that rebuilds team dynamics and restores motivation.

📚 PMI References 

 
 PMBOK® 6th Edition:
  📖 Section 9.4 – Manage Team
  📖 Section 13.3 – Manage Stakeholder Engagement
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Edition:
  📖 Team Performance Domain
  📖 Performance Enablers – Resolve team issues collaboratively

q.en: A company’s CEO has just returned from a conference on the use of artificial intelligence AI and would like the project manager to implement this technology in the organization. What should the project manager do first

en: Start developing a business case
Start a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats. SWOT.
Engage stakeholders and allocate resources

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

SWOT analysis. This technique examines the project from each of the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) perspectives. For risk identification, it is used to increase the breadth of identified risks by including internally generated risks. The technique starts with the identification of strengths and weaknesses of the organization, focusing on either the project, organization, or the business area in general. SWOT analysis then identifies any opportunities for the project that may arise from strengths, and any threats resulting from weaknesses. The analysis also examines the degree to which organizational strengths may offset threats and determines if weaknesses might hinder opportunities.

q.en: A company has a lot of experience with predictive projects The project management office (PMO) has been trying to implement iterative tools within the project management framework, and the project manager has been asked to use these tools in their current project. After the successful implementation of the iterative tools, the PMO asks the project manager to determine the benefits these tools brought to the project. What should the project manager do

en: Determine the data to be monitored during the project as well as the expected performance and targets.
Update the communications management plan to consider performance review meetings with the project stakeholders
Conduct reviews with stakeholders to discuss the potential benefits the approach may have to the project
Prepare and submit a status report to the steering committee to update performance monitoring

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

The PMO is asking the project manager to evaluate the benefits of the iterative tools used. The most effective and inclusive way to do that is by reviewing the project with the stakeholders (including team members, sponsor, end users) to:

 
 Gather feedback on what worked well
 
 
 Identify improvements in flexibility, response time, team performance
 
 
 Discuss measurable value compared to previous predictive-only projects
 

This aligns with benefits realization management practices.

📚 (PMI):

 
 PMBOK® Guide – 6th Edition
  📖 Section 1.2.6 – Benefits Management Plan
  📖 Section 4.6 – Monitor and Control Project Work
 
 
 PMBOK® 7th Edition
  📖 Performance Domains – Measurement, Delivery, Stakeholders

q.en: A project manager has been assigned to a hybrid project. The project manager needs to ensure all team members are collaborating and are aware of the project’s ongoing changes. What should the project manager do

en: Send out daily emails with the project status and task lists to all team members
Encourage collaboration on a daily basis, facilitating different communication channels
Meet daily with the project team and include a monthly report on the risks and issues
Distribute a project newsletter that includes any project changes and required project information

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

In a hybrid project, communication is critical because the project involves both structured predictive planning and adaptive agile elements.
To maintain alignment:

 
 Daily collaboration ensures real-time awareness of changes.
 
 
 Multiple communication channels (chat tools, video, standups, dashboards) support diverse teams across models.
 
 
 This creates a transparent environment and keeps everyone aligned with evolving priorities.
 

📌 This approach follows PMI Agile Practice Guide and PMBOK 7's Team Performance Domain.

📚 PMI References:

 
 PMBOK® 7th Edition
  📖 Team Performance Domain
  📖 Communication and Collaboration Principles
 
 
 PMI Agile Practice Guide
  📖 Section 4 – Tailoring Agile and Hybrid Environments
  📖 Section 5.3 – Communication in Agile Teams

q.en: A new project manager has been assigned to an environmental project. After reviewing the project plan, the project manager notices that health and safety requirements have not been properly addressed. This is a serious concern, and the project manager wants to fix this issue immediately. Why is this situation problematic

en: The project manager is obligated to comply with the project location's regulatory requirements
It is imperative that established performance metrics are met.
The project manager must follow their employer's organizational process assets (OPAs).
Injury or loss incidents could delay project deliverables.

x.en:
Very Important question in Real Exam 

This situation is problematic because health and safety regulations are not optional—they are mandatory legal requirements.
If the project plan overlooks them:

 
 The project could be shut down by authorities.
 
 
 The organization may face legal liabilities, penalties, or accidents.
 
 
 It reflects poor risk management and governance.
 

PMI emphasizes that compliance with environmental, legal, and safety standards is a fundamental responsibility of the project manager, especially in environmental projects.

q.en: Which of the following requires the bulk of planning activities to be conducted upfront and then executing the project in a single pass

en: Iterative life cycle
Incremental life cycle
Agile life cycle
Predictive life cycle

x.en: Predictive life cycle, also known as the traditional approach, requires the bulk of the planning to happen upfront and then executing the project in a single pass. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 17]

q.en: The project manager invites the company CEO, sponsor, team members, and external client representative to a meeting to review the project management plan. The project manager starts presenting the budget but the CEO suddenly asks to end the meeting. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

en: Reviewed the cost management plan with internal participants and CEO prior to inviting an external client representative to the meeting
Performed a root cause analysis with the external client representative and documented the findings in the lessons learned register
Sent the presentation slides to internal participants first and then to the external client representative prior to the meeting
Reviewed the communications management plan before inviting an external client representative to the meeting

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

This situation reflects a communication planning failure. The CEO likely expected the budget to be reviewed internally first before it was shown to the client.
By reviewing the communications management plan, the project manager would have:

 
 Identified the proper flow of information
 
 
 Scheduled sensitive content (like cost) for internal review before external sharing
 
 
 Prevented reputational or trust damage
 

This aligns with PMI’s emphasis on managing stakeholder expectations and tailoring communication strategies.

 PMBOK® Guide – Sixth Edition
  📖 Section 10.1 – Plan Communications Management
  📖 Section 13.2 – Plan Stakeholder Engagement
 
 
 PMBOK® Guide – Seventh Edition
  📖 Communication and Stakeholder Principles

q.en: In a hybrid project, a project team is facing a lot of obstacles and blockers from some stakeholders. As a project manager, what should you do to improve project performance

en: Empower the team members to remove obstacles and blockers
Ask stakeholders to communicate with the project manager and not directly with the team
Add blockers to the issue log and risk management plan
Address and remove obstacles and blockers for the team

x.en: As the project manager, you need to demonstrate the type of leadership that facilitates collaboration among the team and stakeholders, manages conflict, removes obstacles, and supports the team's performance. Removing distraction, randomization, and other confusion enables the project team to be more effective and efficient. Project managers can take on most of the burden of addressing and removing impediments so the team can do their best work on the project to achieve its desired objectives.

q.en: You have been assigned as a project manager to a software project. Before creating your product, you decided to create a prototype to ensure that it is acceptable to stakeholders. This is an example of

en: Risk avoidance
Risk mitigation
Risk acceptance
Risk Transference

x.en: In risk mitigation, action is taken to reduce the probability of occurrence and/or impact of a threat. Early mitigation action is often more effective than trying to repair the damage after the threat has occurred. Adopting less complex processes, conducting more tests, or choosing a more stable seller are examples of mitigation actions. Mitigation may involve prototype development to reduce the risk of scaling up from a bench-scale model of a process or product.

q.en: The project team is reviewing the requirements documentation that they are responsible for working on. Which project artifact can they reference to see the connection between the requirements and the business and project objectives

en: Requirements traceability matrix
Scope management plan
RACI Chart
Project charter

x.en: The requirements traceability matrix is a grid that links product requirements from their origin to the deliverables that satisfy them. The implementation of a requirements traceability matrix helps ensure that each requirement adds business value by linking it to the business and project objectives.

q.en: A hybrid project is used to transit from a current system to a new and enhanced system. The plan is to transit the system in stages. However, the operations team is complaining that they are not ready to start supporting the new system. How should the project manager effectively approach this situation

en: Prepare detailed documentation to be shared with the operations team during project closure
Create lessons learned register to include operations team training for future projects
Change the project management plan to add a final stage for product handoff to the operations team.
Include knowledge transfer sessions between the project and operations teams at every stage

x.en:
Keyword (The plan is to transit the system in stages )

SO the project manager can Include knowledge transfer sessions between the project and operations teams at every stage to effectively approach this situation

q.en: You have been invited by your colleague to attend one of the project standup meetings. You notice that the team has got a big chart on a wall, divided into sections such as “Ready”, “In Development”, “Being Tested”, and “Completed”. What tool are they using

en: Burnup chart
Burndown chart
Kanban board
War room

x.en: This is an example of Kanban board. A Kanban board provides a means to visualize the flow of work, make impediments easily visible, and allow flow to be managed by adjusting the work in process limits. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 31]

q.en: The project manager for a virtual team is struggling to track progress and productivity because the team is spread out over several time zones. What should the project manager do to enhance communication

en: Establish an information-sharing portal.
Create and update the issue log.
Update the lessons learned register.
Set up a Kanban board .

x.en: Communication technology is important in addressing the team development issues in colocated and virtual teams. It helps build a harmonious environment for the collocated team and a better understanding for the virtual team, especially those working in different time zones. Examples of communication technology that may be used are: Shared portal. A shared repository for information sharing (e.g., website, collaboration software or intranet) is effective for virtual project teams.

q.en: Creating a recognition plan with established times for rewards ensures that recognition takes place and is not forgotten. This is usually part of the.

en: HR Company Management plan
Resource Management Plan
Stakeholder engagement plan
Communications Management Plan

x.en: The plan for rewards and recognition is part of the Resource Management plan. The recognition and rewards are developed as part of the Plan Resource Management process.

q.en: A security team notifies a project manager of a change in security procedures. The project manager uses the change control process to update the project management plan. After seeing the change, a stakeholder complains that it was unnecessary because the project is almost complete. What should the project manager do

en: Create a change request to reverse the change until a consensus is reached.
Ignore the stakeholder’s concern and follow the new procedures.
Convince the stakeholder of the benefits resulting from the change.
Add a risk to the risk register to track the impact of stakeholder disagreement.

x.en: The project manager used the change control process to update the project management plan because its a very important change and necessary for the project. The project manager with the team member have evaluated the impact of this change on project constraints and then approved by the CCB. SO he should Convince the stakeholder of the benefits resulting from the change.

q.en: A team member misses a project meeting without it being approved and has been penalized as defined in the ground rules. This team member, as well as other team members, insist that it is the first time they have seen this rule regarding the project and they do not agree with the penalty What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation

en: Used a charismatic leadership style
Ensured the team members are fully supportive of all decisions
Ensured the team charter was developed by the team members
Distributed the project charter to all team members

x.en: The correct answer is : Ensured the team charter was developed by the team members. The team charter is a document that enables the team to establish its values, agreements, and practices as it performs its work together. Ideally the charter should be produced by the team, or at least with the team’s active participation.

q.en: Some of your project management peers are of the opinion that leadership and project management software usage skills are some of the important skills a project manager should have. As per PMI Talent Triangle. which of the below reflects all the competencies of a project manager

en: Knowledge, performance, personality
Project management, people management, Business and strategy
Technical project management, leadership , strategic and business management
Management experience, process expertise, domain experience

x.en:
This is the correct answer as per PMI Talent Triangle.

Technical project management, leadership , strategic and business management

q.en: Which of the following will most likely require an approved change request before the change can be accommodated? (Choose Three)

en: The project is running well over budget, and the cost baseline needs to be revised to reflect reality.
A suggestion has been made to change from predictive to a hybrid development approach.
The revised status of several tasks needs to be reflected in the project schedule.
A senior executive has recommended updating the project life cycle description to include an additional phase.
A new stakeholder has just been identified and needs to be added to the stakeholder register.

x.en:
A suggestion has been made to change from predictive to a hybrid development approach.
 A senior executive has recommended updating the project life cycle description to include an additional phase.
 The project is running well over budget, and the cost baseline needs to be revised to reflect reality.

q.en: In your project, a supplier delivers equipment that fails to meet customer requirements. after the investigation, you determined that the supplier misunderstood the requirements and make incorrect assumptions without clarifying them with the customer. As a project manager, what type of communication methods should you have used to avoid this

en: Push communication
Manual communication
Pull communication
Interactive communication

x.en: ( Interactive communication ) is The best communication methods can be using to avoid the supplier misunderstood the requirements with the customer.

q.en: Your project expense has increased in the last quarter due to the required office space for personnel and some of their travel. What can you do from a resource management planning perspective to address this

en: Plan to incorporate a virtual team environment, if not done already
Use video conferencing and web based meetings
Bring all project team members to work from one location
Reduce the travel and office equipment cost

x.en: Virtual team environment helps to move forward with projects that would have been canceled due to travel expenses, and save expenses of the office and physical equipment for employees. In this arrangement, project team members need not work face to face, and facilities like video conferencing may be used.

q.en: A project manager is starting a project using a hybrid approach. The customer decided on a major change for the project design. This change was approved. The software team leader who is supposed to develop the software refuses to commit to delivery dates, claiming that they work using an agile approach and cannot commit to the final delivery date. The hardware team depends on this software to develop their part of the product. As a project manager, what should you do

en: Escalate this to higher management and ask for help to resolve the issue.
Impose the delivery dates on the software team leader and notify the functional manager about the situation.
Ask the software team leader to use a predictive approach and commit to the delivery date.
Update the risk register with this risk and monitor it according to the risk management plan.

x.en: Keyword ( using a hybrid approach ) .. hybrid approach is a combination of predictive, iterative, incremental, and/or agile. The project manager should ask the software team leader to use a predictive approach and commit to the delivery date. and can follow agile to develop The hardware.

q.en: Your project scheduler has just started working with your project and has produced defective reports for the past two accounting cycles. You are now checking your company policies before moving to the next step with the corrective actions. In which process are you now

en: Validate Scope
Control Scope
Perform Quality Audit
Manage Quality

x.en: Keyword ( checking your company policies ) its - Audit technique- is a structured, independent process used to determine if project activities comply with organizational and project policies, processes, and procedures.

q.en: There is disagreement among the project stakeholders makes the project manager having difficulty obtaining approval of the project requirements. As a project manager, what should you do first to facilitate the approval of project requirements

en: Conduct a stakeholder analysis
Review the project charter
Identify the source of the disagreement
Team building Activities

x.en: The project manager should first identify the source of the disagreement to facilitate the approval of project requirements

q.en: You are a project manager in a critical project for your organization. Your project sponsor has asked you to finish the project early as soon as possible. As a project manager, to motivate your project team, which of the following will you use

en: Training
Reschedule baselines to finish the project early
Perform quality assurance
Recognition and rewards system

x.en:
Very important question in real exam

As a project manager, to motivate your project team to finish the project early, you should conduct the recognition and rewards system.

q.en: The project sponsor recently requested that a vendor begins working toward adopting a hybrid approach. In response, the vendor hired a project manager experienced in agile for the project. What does that project manager need to do to make the team work in a collaborative way.

en: Allocate time to mentor the team
Identify any training gaps
Request the project management office (PMO) for a team of mentors
Update the issue log

x.en: Allocate time to mentor the team . A type of leadership style used in agile and other types of projects which encourages the self-definition, self-discovery, and self-awareness of team members by listening, coaching, and providing an environment that allows them to grow.

q.en: A company has been following a predictive approach and always waits for the preceding phase to be completed before evaluating the quality of its products. A new project manager with experience in hybrid approaches has been assigned to help increase the efficiency of the company’s quality management process. What should the new project manager do to address the process improvements

en: Discuss the process improvement with the project management office (PMO) lead to update the project delivery framework
Understand the context and interdependencies of the process from the team members and then define improvements
Define a ground-rule to comply with the quality standard and ask the team members to apply it.
Continue with the process as is. and wait until the next phase to suggest any improvements

x.en: As a new project manager, you should first meet with the team and discuss the current status and how processes are being implemented before suggesting any new modifications and then define improvements

q.en: Six agile teams working together on a product. When all of the teams integrated at the product level, many integration issues were observed. The overall product release progress declined and the content will not be able to be accomplished. What should the project manager have done differently

en: Performed a scrum of scrum on a regular basis to help the teams remove impediments
Conduct an online session on the integration concept to teach the teams
Formed a quality control team to test all items coming from each team at the end of each iteration
Ensured frequent and continuous integration of work to obtain early feedback and continuous learning

x.en:
Very Important Question In Real Exam 

Scrum of Scrums (SoS), also known as “meta Scrum,” is a technique used when two or more Scrum teams consisting of three to nine members each need to coordinate their work instead of one large Scrum team. A representative from each team attends a meeting with the other team representative(s), potentially daily but typically two to three times a week. The daily meeting is conducted similar to the daily standup in Scrum where the representative reports completed work, next set of work, any current impediments, and potential upcoming impediments that might block the other team(s). The goal is to ensure the teams are coordinating work and removing impediments to optimize the efficiency of all the teams. Agile Practice guide page, 111

q.en: A company has been following a predictive approach and always waits for the preceding phase to be completed before evaluating the quality of its products. A new project manager with experience in hybrid approaches has been assigned to help increase the efficiency of the company’s quality management process. What should the new project manager do to address the process improvements

en: Define a ground-rule to comply with the quality standard and ask the team members to apply it
Understand the context and interdependencies of the process from the team members and then define improvements
Continue with the process as is. and wait until the next phase to suggest any improvements
Discuss the process improvement with the project management office (PMO) lead to update the project delivery framework

x.en: As a new project manager, you should first meet with the team and discuss the current status and how processes are being implemented before suggesting any new modifications and then define improvements

q.en: An architectural firm has spent a great deal of time and effort creating the design and blueprints for the building. They had to purchase materials and hire consultants and have been working on this project for six months. They have submitted all the invoices for the money they have spent on the work, as well as an invoice for the fee of $5,000. What type of contract was this

en: Fixed price with economic price adjustments (FPEPA)
Time and materials
Cost-plus incentive fee (CPIF)
Cost-reimbursable

x.en: This example of Cost plus fixed fee (CPFF). The seller is reimbursed for all allowable costs for performing the contract work and receives a fixed-fee payment calculated as a percentage of the initial estimated project costs.

q.en: A large organization will transform from a predictive environment to agile methodologies. In its current state, the work in the organization is decomposed into departmental silos, and the employees are best described as specialized contributors. What is the best strategy for this agile transformation

en: Introduce some agile techniques to a large and complex project
Establish a fixed date for all projects to transition from predictive to agile
Use hybrid life cycles as a transition strategy from predictive to agile
Tailor projects so that the scope is fixed with time and cost being variable

x.en: A large and complex organization will likely require a gradual approach to transition from predictive to agile methodologies. Incorporating elements of agile within the existing predictive framework will allow for the gradual adoption and acceptance of agile methods

q.en: A project manager is in charge of an important project, and the customer requests changes on a continuous basis. The project manager implemented the change requests without documenting the change requests to satisfy the customer. The project manager realized that his project exceeded costs. What could have been done by the project manager to prevent cost overruns

en: Schedule management plan
Project management plan
Cost management plan
Change management plan

x.en: The correct answer is (change management plan), which provides guidance for managing the change control process and documentation of a formal change control board. If the project manager implements change requests without analyzing the impact of changes on time, cost and quality, it will increase risks in the project and lead to increased costs (cost overruns).

q.en: A project manager working with a risk-averse financial firm has just started a new project. The project sponsor is extremely concerned that the project may run over budget and is looking to the project manager for confirmation that this won’t happen. In order to alleviate the sponsor’s concerns, what should the project manager do

en: Run a Monte Carlo simulation
Use historical data analysis
Create the probability and impact matrix.
Perform a strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis

x.en: The project manager should first identify the risks, update the risk register then analyze the risks... SWOT analysis is one of the tools and techniques in identifying the risk process to identify the strengths and weaknesses of the organization, focusing on the project, organization, or business area in general. The SWOT analysis then identifies any project opportunities that may arise from strengths and any threats arising from weaknesses. The analysis also examines the degree to which organizational strengths may offset threats and determines whether weaknesses may hinder opportunities

q.en: Due to a recent technological development, a significant change in the product design is required. This change would require a 50 percent increase in the project budget. The project manager prepares a detailed report and emails it to the project sponsor, and the sponsor acknowledges the receipt of the report. What should Ben do next

en: Update the Project management plan
Update the project schedule
Wait for the formal approval of the new budget
Update the Cost Baseline

q.en: You have submitted the cost baseline to the sponsor. After a review, the sponsor tells you that the amount you have estimated for a certain month is more than the funds the sponsor can disburse you for that month. What do you think the sponsor will advise you next

en: To reduce the cost estimates of the activities for that month
To motivate the project team do the work of that month without being fully paid for it
To reschedule the work of that month
To remove some of the work scope for that month

x.en: Rescheduling work for the period where funds are lower than estimated will be required in this situation

q.en: You are managing a complex construction project and you request a five-year schedule for this project. Although multiple brainstorming sessions with your project team, you struggle to provide detail for the project management plan. This causes a delay in obtaining the project management plan approvals. As a project manager, what should you have done to avoid this situation

en: Used subject matter expert to develop the detailed schedule.
Used the rolling wave planning technique for activity planning.
Created a high level Gantt chart to represent the milestone only.
Used decomposition techniques.

x.en: Rolling wave planning is an iterative planning technique in which the work to be accomplished in the near term is planned in detail, while work further in the future is planned at a higher level. During early strategic planning when information is less defined, work packages may be decomposed to the known level of detail. As more is known about the upcoming events in the near term, work packages can be decomposed into activities.

q.en: Which three of the following are impediments the scrum master should pay attention to? Choose three

en: A lack of team empowerment and an inability to self-organize.
A team member talking about a user story that is not on the scrum board
A team member is talking about a user story that is on the scrum board.
A technology that blocks agile capabilities
A review of the backlog at daily standup meetings.

x.en:
The impediments are Actions that slow down or hinder progress. The Three impediments are: 

1- A lack of team empowerment and an inability to self-organize. 

2- A technology that blocks agile capabilities. 

3-A team member talking about a user story that is not on the scrum board.

q.en: Early in the establishment of the project, the project manager spends time looking for historical data that might be helpful in planning the new project. She is looking for examples of project documents in similar projects that have been completed that she might be able to use as templates for the new project. She is also looking for information about established processes and procedures that will help the project run more smoothly. What is the term used to define these

en: Enterprise environmental factors (EEFs)
Organizational process assets (OPAs).
Retrospective
Progressive elaboration

x.en: templates, processes, and procedures are an example of Organizational process assets (OPAs).

q.en: When can the contract closeout occur

en: Whenever a contract is completed and accepted
At the end of a project only, unless the project is terminated early
At the end of a project only
Whenever a seller is selected

x.en: Whenever a contract is completed and accepted

q.en: Many organizations favor fixed-price contracts because the buyer's risk is minimized by such contracts. However, to minimize the seller's risk, which of the following is crucial for a fixed price contract

en: The buyer must precisely specify the number of resources to be used for procurement.
The buyer must precisely specify the price of the contract.
The buyer must precisely specify the service or product to be procured.
The buyer must precisely specify the time for the contract.

x.en: In a fixed-price contract, the buyer must precisely specify the product or service to be procured. Any changes in the contract may involve additional cost to the buyer. Therefore, buyers must be careful while preparing the statement of work.

q.en: You have a contract to build a manufacturing plant in Kuala Lumpur. However, you are not familiar with the building codes in Kuala Lumpur or Malaysia, so you are reviewing all their building codes prior to turning a shovelful of earth.? This is an example of

en: Project initiation
Quality control
Quality assurance
Quality planning

x.en: All types of quality plans, such as building codes, OSHA guidelines, ISO 9000, or company quality plans are examples of Enterprise Environmental Factors and Organizational Process Assets which are inputs to the Plan Quality Management process.

q.en: You have recently joined an organization as the Marketing Manager. You have been told that a new product has just been created and you will need to get it into market within the next month. This is means press released , TV,Radio , Internet and Newspaper adverts, abig launch , withat least one local celebrity.you request a meeting with a project manager for advice on initiating the project ,butyou are told the organization doesn't have a Project Manager , it Just has a part time Project Coordinator . What is the organizational structure of the organization

en: PMO
Balanced Matrix
Project -Oriented
Strong Matrix

q.en: You are managing a project for your company constructing an office complex in another country. The construction work on two of the buildings is complete, and those buildings are ready for move-in. However, the construction supervisor informs you that you must pay a fee to a local government agency to issue an occupancy permit for any new construction in that country. What should you do?

en: Pay the fee
Do not pay the fee
Notify project stakeholders that you have been asked to pay a bribr
Ask your legal department if this is legal

x.en: Pay the fee to the local agency. Because it is a standard fee for a permit that is required of all new construction, it is not a bribe.

q.en: You are managing a project team that is distributed across global locations. You communicate by email daily and have a status call by telephone once a week. Which of the following statements is valid?

en: Remote teams are an overhead on the project and should be avoided as far as possible.
The receivers of communication at the remote location cannot pick up nonverbal cues and this results in a certain loss in communication. You need to factor this in your planning.
The communication of status reports and work allocation can never be done effectively via email. Plan for 50 percent efficiency for the remotely located team.
Plan telephonic status calls every day and follow up every email communication with a telephone call to discuss whether the remote team has understood the task allocation.

x.en: Nonverbal cues represent a significant part of communication. In the absence of this element, as project manager, you may need to take further actions to ensure that communications are being properly understood by the remote team. Consider options such as team building to improve team cohesiveness and videoconferences on a regular basis. The other options are invalid since they quote invalid inferences. [PMBOK® Guide 6th Edition, Page 384]

q.en: A functional manager in your organization has recently filed a complaint against a junior project manager regarding his project management certification. The functional manager claims that the PMP certification claimed by the junior project manager is invalid and needs to be checked. What should be your response as a senior project manager

en: Ask your project manager to provide evidence for his/her PMP certification
Report to PMI
Suspend the junior project manager
Ask your functional manager to provide evidence for his argument

x.en: One of the mandatory standards in the PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct is respect. A project manager must listen to others’ points of view and understand them. However, before asking the junior project manager for evidence of his or her PMP certification, you must ask your functional manager to provide evidence to support his or her allegations. You can suspend the junior project manager or report him or her to PMI if there is sufficient evidence of his or her guilt.

q.en: A number of teams are developing an enterprise system using the agile approach for product development. Which of the following is a major risk item for such a complex project being performed in an agile environment.

en: Number of interconnected dependencies between the features developed by different teams.
Scope definition and freezing early during the planning phase.
Emphasis on schedule control over risk management
Number and size of teams developing the larger features.

x.en: In adaptive life cycles, when multiple teams are concurrently developing a large number of features, the interconnected dependencies between the features become a major risk item. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 177]

q.en: A conflict appeared between two members of your team , and the conflicts began to affect to the entire project team . The team's morale has become low . As project manager , whar should you do ?

en: As the team members to solve the conflict by them selves .
Escalate the problem to HR department
Interfering for solving the problem immediately
Do nothing

x.en: Internal conflicts affect team morale. This represents negative Risk and threat to the success of the project, so the project manager must intervene to solve the problem immediately

q.en: You are project manager for Steco company . Two team members come to you with a dispute regarding who will perform and report the status of a particular task. To resolve the conflict , which document will you refer to?

en: Responsible , accountable , consult , and inform ( RACI) matrix.
Project Sponsor
Stakeholder register
Functional manager

x.en: RAM or RACI Connection between work packages or activities and team members

q.en: The project manager wants to capture information related to roles and responsibilities and release , training needs , resource calendar , recognition , and rewards . Which of the dollowing documents would be most appropriate.

en: Issue log
Project Team Assignments
Resource Management Plan
Project Management Plan

x.en:
Resources Management Plan
Identifying, documenting, project roles, responsibilities, and reporting relationships, as well as creating the staffing management plan and training needs , resource calendar , recognition , and rewards.

q.en: Your administer surveys , interviews , assessments and focus groups within your project team and create a team performance assessment with observations on their skills , competencies , turnover rate and cohensiveness. You then evaluate the team's overall performance . How will you use this report now?

en: Estimate the cost of improving the team's performance.
Identify specific training , coaching , mentoring or other changes required to improve the team's performance.
Make changes to the team members who are performing poorly.
Estimate project schedule based on the team's performance.

x.en: The team performance assessment is used to identify performance improvement strategies and actions. Though at some point this may include changing team members, or reviewing impact to project schedule or estimating training costs , the first step is to identify actions to be undertaken specifically with respect to team performance improvement. Also, team members cannot be changed without giving them the opportunity to improve first.

q.en: Two of your team members have come to you due to a difference of opinion between them . What is the best way to resolve this situation.

en: When one of them backs out due to frustration
Refuse conducting meeting to resolve this situation.
By understanding the needs of both and guiding them towards successful resolution and their full satisfaction.
When one of them is very flexible to accept the other person's opinion in front of you.

x.en: The best way is understanding the needs of both and guiding them towards successful resolution and their full satisfaction.(Collaboration Strategy)

q.en: You are planning for project resources and have created a table showing indvidual roles for various tasks in the project. What sort of representation is this called , from a resource planning perspective?

en: RBS
An OBS
A project organization chart
A RACI chart

x.en:
RACI Chart ( atype of Responsibility Assignment Matrix(RAM))
R---- Responsible
A---- Accountable
C------ Consult
I------- Inform

q.en: A customer has been consistently late with approvals on design documentation. George , the project manager , has raised the subject in the past , but the practice of delayed approval has not changed. George has been documenting the delays. Which conflict resolution technique is he following?

en: Withdrawal
Collaboration / Solve Problem
Smoothing
Forcing

x.en: Avoidance / Withdrawal is strategic technique since project manager document the delays isnoy an attempt to solve the problem.

q.en: The project team members are in conflict are not collaborative and differ in opinion on the architecture. Which of the following phases of Team Development are they in now?

en: Forming
Performing
Norming
Storming

x.en: Storming Stage : Team member argue and are not openly collaborative Storming

q.en: You have presented a unique and verifiable product to your customers for their approval. Approval of this product may allow you to move on to your next phase. This unique and verifiable product is also known as

en: A deliverable
A project
A plan
A portfolio

x.en: A unique and verifiable product produced in each phase or at the end of the project is known as a deliverable. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 4]

q.en: A risk analyst has produced the following chart for your project. Which risk management tool is this?

en: RBS
Pareto Chart
Histogram
Tornado diagram

x.en: This is an example of a tornado diagram which is a typical display of sensitivity analysis. The tornado diagram presents the calculated correlation coefficients for each element of the quantitative risk analysis model that can influence the project outcome ordered by descending strength of correlation. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, page 434]

q.en: The scope of work in a project could not be clearly defined. There was also a strong possibility that the scope would change during the course of the project. Which type of contract would suit this type of situation?

en: Fixed-price with economic price adjustment contract
Cost-reimbursable contract
Fixed-price contract
Fixed-price incentive contract

x.en: A cost-reimbursable contract gives the project flexibility to redirect a seller whenever the scope of work cannot be precisely determined at the start of the project and needs to be altered, or when high risks may exist in the effort.

q.en: A project manager gives monthly status updates to the key stakeholders. After every status update meeting, a copy of the presentation, the updated action tracker, and the stakeholder feedback must be:

en: Emailed to the project sponsor
Emailed to all the participants of the meeting
Updated to the project management information system
Added to the project folder as an organizational process asset

x.en: All of the choices are actions that can be performed next. However, emailing the mentioned documents to the stakeholders and the project sponsor depends on their needs and the communication management plan requirements. Further, updating the project management information system is conditional on the availability of the system. Hence, these three actions may or may not be done. However, adding a copy of these documents to the project folder is an absolute must for the project manager. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 388]

q.en: You have been recently hired as a PMO Expert in an organization that has historically delivered projects under functional managers. You were able to gather necessary resources to establish a central PMO in the organization and now you have shifted your attention on standardizing project management processes. Historically the organization has stressed quality control processes instead of scope validation processes. You now have a stiff challenge to convince the senior leadership that scope validation is equally important. Why must the Validate Scope process be completed in a project?

en: To determine whether the scope is at the correct complexity level
To obtain scope documents from recent similar projects for benchmarking
To determine whether the scope is at the correct complexity level
To obtain formal acceptance of deliverables by the customer or sponsor

x.en: Validate Scope is the process of formalizing acceptance of the completed project deliverables by the customer or sponsor of the project. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 163]

q.en: You want to subcontract a number of work packages on your construction project and have invited a number of subcontractors to submit their proposals. You have explicitly mentioned your intention to negotiate a firm fixed-price contract with the selected subcontractor. You are now negotiating with the top three subcontractors but are unable to negotiate a reasonable price. What you should do to resolve this issue?

en: Consider a cost-plus contract instead.
Reduce the project scope to suit your budget.
Go for a second RFP round.
Openly discuss subcontractors’ concerns with them.

x.en: Openly discuss subcontractors’ concerns with them. Try to understand why they are inflating prices and what risks they think can harm them in this project. Only when you will successfully address their concerns, can you reach mutual agreements.

q.en: Ibrahim Mohamed Saeed is currently working for ABC Contractors as a quality control manager for a railway track construction project. National Railways awarded this cost-plus construction contract to ABC Contractors a few months ago. As a contractual requirement, ABC Contractors has to submit each completed deliverable for client acceptance. Reviewing project data, Ibrahim found that the current submission rejection rate is 22 percent. He conducts a root cause analysis and submits his findings along with construction process improvement recommendations to the project director. In this scenario, Ibrahim’s report is an example of:

en: Work performance information
Raw observations
Work performance data
Work control report

x.en: The data on rejections is the project performance data. Ibrahim analyzed it and converted it into work performance information, i.e. reasons for rejections and recommendations.

q.en: Eyad, a member of another project team, advised Ibrahim that he was concerned the final requirements document released by the project manager intentionally misrepresented the requirements gathered. Eyad stated that many requirements included had only a plurality of supporters. Corporate project management methodology specifies that plurality support is the minimum level of support for requirements. What should Ibrahim do?

en: Notify the project sponsor there is a discrepancy and suggest a formal requirements review.
Discuss the issue with another project manager.
Report the project manager to his or her manager. Requirements must be supported by more than 50 percent of the team.

Do nothing. The corporate methodology permits decisions to be made by a plurality, rather than a majority. A plurality decision is based on the largest block of supporters, even if that block is not a majority.

x.en: There is no wrongdoing in this scenario, so no action is required of Bader. Using a plurality to determine requirements is consistent with the company's project management methodology. PMI's code of ethics requires project managers to follow all policies, rules, and regulations.

q.en: You have recently been successful in passing the Project Management Professional exam. Others within the organization you work for are also pursuing the certification and have sought your assistance. They have requested that you provide them with a detailed list of the questions that you had on the exam. What is the FIRST course of action you should take?

en: Offer your coworkers a listing of all the questions you recall from the exam
Pretend you do not recall any of the questions
Report the violation to the PMI
Indicate that you cannot disclose questions you saw on the exam

x.en: The first course of action is to indicate that you cannot disclose questions you saw on the exam. PMI requires the candidates and those seeking certification to maintain and respect the confidentiality of the contents of the PMP examination. The PMI code of conduct mandates respecting copyrights of others. [PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct].

q.en: The paint on the exotic cars that are manufactured in your plant is bubbling about a year after application. What would be the best tool for your team to use to find potential causes of the peeling paint?

en: Scatter diagram
Ishikawa Diagram
Inspection
Control Chart

x.en: All the choices are tools and techniques in quality control; however, the best choice would be the Ishikawa or cause-and-effect diagram. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 293]

q.en: One of the senior team members, who is the best performer in your project, plays favorites. A few of the other team members who work closely with this team member have gotten exceptionally good appraisal reports in the past, even though they may not have deserved them. As the project manager, what do you need to actively do?

en: Ask all the members of your team who are appraisers of other team members to be liberal in their appraisals. This will help compensate for the appraisals the senior team member does.
Ignore the matter since you would otherwise lose a senior team member who is key to your project.
Ensure that the senior team member does not get to appraise anybody.
Speak to the senior team member and ask him or her to do appraisals fairly, in accordance with the appraisal guidelines.

x.en: As project manager, you need to speak to the senior team member and ask for all appraisals to be done in an objective manner. The other options are incorrect. Ignoring the matter will not help solve it. The other two options are likewise impractical.

q.en: You are automating a manual business workflow. The system has to integrate with some legacy system which lacks documentation. The project team is hesitant in reviewing and editing the source code of this legacy system as the system is already in production. This risk was never considered earlier and it was assumed that you will face no issues during the integration. What needs to be done now?

en: Descoping of the project
A detailed risk assessment
Acceptance of the risk
A new change request

x.en: A major assumption was made earlier. Now once the risk has been identified, this needs to be analyzed in detail and an appropriate response strategy needs to be planned. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, page 439]

q.en: Your project is running slightly over budget. You mention this to another project manager, who suggests you shift some of your direct project expenses to indirect costs that are not charged to your project budget. What do you do?

en: Use project reserves and do not shift direct project expenses
Re estimate the project
Fast track the project
Examine project expenses to see whether you can take any indirect expenses off your project

x.en: You should use your project reserves to cover the budget overruns. Project managers are required to disclose accurate and truthful information about their projects. Masking an expense or otherwise using a half-truth to cover a budget overrun is a violation of the PMI Code. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, page 254 & PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct]

q.en: Which of the following arrangements allows least flexibility to the buyer to alter the contracted scope of works?

en: Fixed-price arrangements.
Not-to-exceed time and materials arrangement.
Early cancellation option.
Dynamic scope option.

x.en: A not-to-exceed time and materials allows replacing original scope with new scope. The dynamic scope option allows scope adjustments at specified points in the project. The early cancellation option allows termination halfway through the project. The fixed-price arrangement is the least flexible option. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 78]

q.en: During a discussion with the quality department, Dave, a project manager, was told that as applied to projects, the terms “prevention” and “inspection” are synonymous. However, his understanding of the terms is different. What would you comment on this situation?

en: The project manager is wrong. Both inspection and prevention are about keeping errors out of the process. They are used in different contexts.
The project manager is wrong. Both inspection and prevention are about keeping errors out of the customer's hands. They are used in different contexts.
The project manager is correct. Prevention is about keeping errors out of the process; inspection is about keeping errors out of the customer's hands.
The project manager is correct. Inspection is about keeping errors out of the process; prevention is about keeping errors out of the customer's hands.

x.en: The project manager is correct. Prevention is about keeping errors out of the process, whereas inspection is about keeping errors out of the hands of the customer. This is an important distinction, which the project management team needs to be aware of. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 274]

q.en: Your organization has been awarded a contract by a major US oil company to build 500 US-style houses and 10 office buildings in a Middle Eastern country so that its American employees feel more like home when working abroad. There is a lack of workforce in this country skilled in US-styled construction. You cannot take the entire construction crew from the US to the site for this entire project due to cost constraints. Which of the following is LEAST recommended?

en: Consider training the local workforce.
Bring the senior construction managers from the US and hire the rest of the crew from the local market.
Consider taking the crew to build a few model houses and buildings.
Outsource the project to local subcontractors and make US-style construction part of their contractual obligations.

x.en: If there is a shortage of a specific skill in the market, you need to determine ways you can meet the requirement. You cannot shrug the responsibility off your shoulders by outsourcing the project to multiple subcontractors and making US-style construction part of their contractual obligations, especially when you know that the local market is not skilled in US-style construction. [PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct]

q.en: “Customer collaboration over contract negotiation” is one of the key Agile Manifesto values. Which of the following Agile approaches helps in achieving this value?

en: Agile measurements
Backlog preparation
Backlog refinement
Daily standups

x.en: Agile measurements measure value delivered to the customer rather than how the project is performing against project baselines. This shifts the focus from the contract to the customer. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 97]

q.en: Your friend went to a conference where he heard the term “follow-the-sun” development process. What does that mean?

en: Teams are dedicated to the project 365 days a year.
Team begins the work slowly in the morning and reaches a peak point by the noon.
Teamwork only during working hours and no overtime is allowed.
Work is handed off at the end of every day from one site to the next.

x.en: A follow-the-sun development process is one where work is handed off at the end of every day from one site to the next, many time zones away in order to speed up product development. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 44]

q.en: Which of the following terms refers to the deferred cost of work not done at an earlier point in the product life cycle?

en: Opportunity cost
Sunk cost
Net present value
Technical debt

x.en: Technical debt refers to the deferred cost of work not done at an earlier point in the product life cycle. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 154]

q.en: Performance reports are produced during the Control Procurements process by evaluating work performance data against the agreement requirements. Which of the following is the prime objective of producing such reports?

en: Performance reporting is a good project management practice and must be carried out on all projects.
Performance reports are produced so they can be added to lessons-learned database, and the future project might benefit.
Providing management with information about how effectively the seller is achieving the contractual objectives.
Performance reports document the analysis of the project manager and does not require supplier's participation.

x.en: All of the choices are valid but the question is asking for the prime/main reason for conducting this exercise. The prime objective of this exercise is to provide management with information about how effectively the sellers are achieving the contractual objectives and obligations. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 499]

q.en: The WBS represents all product and project work. The total work at the lowest levels should roll up to the higher levels so that nothing is left out and no extra work is performed. This principle is also the:

en: 100 percent rule
Pareto's rule
Ground rule
80/20 rule

x.en: The WBS represents all product and project work. The total work at the lowest levels should roll up to the higher levels so that nothing is omitted and no extra work is performed. This principle is also called the 100% rule. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 161]

q.en: According to the Agile principles, all of the following are important factors to be considered when forming an Agile team EXCEPT

en: Office environment
Team RACI
Motivation level
Trust level

x.en: Build projects around motivated individuals. Give them the environment and support they need and trust them to get the job done. Agile teams are supposed to be self-organizing and to work as a unit, developing a team RACI doesn’t support this view. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 9]

q.en: An Agile team is progressing a little slower than what was planned at the start of the iteration. Which of the following Agile metrics will this effect?

en: Story points
Actual duration
Ideal time
Velocity

x.en: Story points and ideal time are sizing/estimating metrics; these do not change with actual performance. Velocity, however, would get reduced if the team is delivering fewer story points than planned. Actual duration is an absolute number you get at the end of an activity, it can be different than the planned duration, but the final value doesn’t change. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 61]

q.en: Large organizations typically manage a wide range of projects; from small projects to large initiatives requiring long-term commitments. Which of the following factors can be used in scaling such projects:

en: Team size, geographical distribution and regulatory compliance.
Team size, geographical distribution, regulatory compliance and organizational complexity.
Team size, geographical distribution, regulatory compliance, complexity, technical complexity, and funds availability.
Team size, geographical distribution, regulatory compliance, complexity and technical complexity.

x.en: In large organizations, there may be a mixture of small projects and large initiatives requiring long-term commitments to manage these programs using scaling factors such as team size, geographical distribution, regulatory compliance, organizational complexity, and technical complexity. Funds availability is a constraint applicable to all projects. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 178]

q.en: One of the stakeholders of a project initiated a change request, which was then documented in the change control system. Who would typically be responsible for approving or rejecting the change request?

en: An authority within the project management team or external organization
The sponsor
The project manager
The stakeholder who raised the change request

x.en: Typically, some authority within the project management team or an external organization would approve or reject the change request. However, on many projects the project manager is given authority to approve certain types of change requests. [PMBOK® Guide 6th edition, Page 115]

q.en: A Project manager is in the middle of an agile project comprised of 100 user stories broken down into five iterations . Each user story is worth 50$ . The actual expenditure is 2,000$ and 50 user stories have been delivered. How is the project performing.

en: The project is under budget and on schedule
The project is over budget and behind schedule
The project is on budget and on schedule
The project is under budget and behind schedule

x.en:
EV = 50*50 = 2500 , AC = 2000 

CV =EV-AC= 2500-2000 = + 500 so The project is under budget 
 

 The Project is the middle = 1/2 *100 = 50 user stories 

PV = 50*50 = 2500
SV= EV-PV = 2500-2500 = 0 so The project is on the schedule .

q.en: There is a conflict between two members on how they complete a task. The conflict is not yet escalated to the project manager and there is no impact to the project . What should the project manager do

en: Ask the functional managers to get involved and facilitate a resolution
Help facilitate a satisfactory conflict resolution
Allow the project team members to find a resolution to their conflict
Reassign both resources to different projects

x.en: Since the conflict is not yet escalated to the project manager and there is no impact to the project, the project manager should allow the project team members to find a resolution to their conflict

q.en: What is difference between a predictive lifecycle and an adaptive lifecycle

en: Predictive lifecycle is plan-driven; adaptive lifecycle is change- driven
Predictive lifecycle forecasts project completion; adaptive lifecycle completes the project when the money runs out
Adaptive lifecycle is plan-driven; Predictive lifecycle is change- driven
The predictive follows the same pattern for each iteration and the adaptive lifecycle changes its approach based upon performance growth of the project results.

x.en: Predictive lifecycle is plan-driven; adaptive lifecycle is change- driven

q.en: The project manager works in risk management and creating a risk register. The risk register records details of all the risks identified at the beginning and during the life of the project. What tool or technique should the project manager use to generate a list of all possible project risks

en: Probability and impact matrix
Monte Carlo
Tornado diagram
Brainstorming

x.en: Brainstorming is a data-gathering technique that can be used for identify risk process and The goal of brainstorming is to obtain a comprehensive list of individual project risks and sources of overall project risk. PMBOK 6th edition page, 414

q.en: A project manager is starting a new project and has identified an opportunity to use the iterative tools. One of the senior managers is concerned about this modified framework as it is new to the company. What should the project manager do first.

en: Organize individual sessions with the stakeholders to build awareness and trust in the new framework.
Send documentation to the senior manager about the advantages of the new framework.
Look for external training on the new framework to eliminate the risk of low engagement from stakeholders.
Escalate the senior manager's concern to the project sponsor and distribute the status ti the team.

x.en:
Very Important question in Real Exam 

Project Manager should Organize individual sessions with the stakeholders to build awareness and trust in the new framework.

q.en: A skilled project manager should have the necessary to identify appropriate project management approaches ( traditional vs . Agile ) and tailor the tools , techniques , and methods for each project. What are these skills called

en: Technical project management skills
Interpersonal Skills
Strategic and business management skills
Leadership skills

x.en: identify appropriate project management approaches are example of Technical project management skills

q.en: Which of the following main events are defined by the scrum framework?

en: Sprint planning meeting , Daily scrum meeting , Sprint Review and Kanban meeting.
Sprint planning meeting , Daily scrum meeting , Sprint Review and Sprint retrospective meeting and Mid-sprint status review meeting.
Sprint planning meeting , Daily scrum meeting , Sprint Review and XP meeting.
Sprint planning meeting , Daily scrum meeting , Sprint Review and Sprint retrospective meeting.

x.en: The main events are defined by the scrum framework (Sprint planning meeting , Daily scrum meeting , Sprint Review and Sprint retrospective meeting)

q.en: Which of the following is not a typical artifact of the scrum framework

en: Sprint backlog
Incremental
Pareto Chart
Product backlog

x.en:
Typical artifacts of the Scrum framework
1-Product backlog
2-Sprint backlog
3- Incremental

q.en: You are a scrum master leading an agile project team that has been consistently meeting the goals set for each iteration. However , you feel that one team member is less productive than the others . What is the most appropriate feedback approach for you to take in this situation

en: Allow the project team members to address the issue if they deem necessary
From the next iteration onward , assign the team member the easiest user stories.
Call out the team member's low productivity at the upcoming iteration retrospective
Direct the underperforming team member to work extra hours to bridge the gap

x.en: Scrum Master should encourage the development team to be self- organizing and self-managing so Agile team should collaborate to complete the work and the role of Scram Master is empower the development team to solve their problems themselves first and work as a team and help team member to improve his performance

q.en: One of your team leaders informs you that a team member criticizes him constantly about the allocation of tasks. The team leader also asserts that this team member is also responsible for the delay of many tasks, leading to delays in the project schedule. What action should you take as a project manager?

en: Direct your team leader to issue a memo
Replace the team member
Conduct a meeting with the sponsor, team leader, and the team member
Approach the team member and understand his point of view

x.en: A project manager should manage such a conflict by directly approaching the team member who caused the conflict. According to the PMI Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct, a project manager must be responsible and show respect. He or she must listen to others’ viewpoints, seeking to understand them before making a decision. Neither replacing the team member nor issuing a memo is an appropriate action. Involving the sponsor in team issues is not an appropriate action either, unless the issues are beyond the project manager’s control. [PMBOK® Guide 6th Edition, Page 348]

q.en: Which of the following is one of the major challenges faced by an organization just beginning to use Agile approaches

en: Avoidance of multi tasking introduce inefficiency
Agile approaches could be viewed as plan-driven.
Daily standup could be viewed as time intensive activities
Iterative prototypes involve rework that could be viewed negatively

x.en: Agile approaches are not plan-driven and multi-tasking is inefficient due to waste involved with task-switching. These are plain facts. Daily standups are short team meetings and are not time-intensive. One of the major problems faced by organizations new to Agile is rework related to prototyping and could be viewed negatively in the beginning. [Agile Practice Guide, 1st edition, Page 73]

q.en: A vendor has been contracted by a buyer to develop a new device . The buyer does not have clear requirements upfront and , therefore , requested that the vendor develop the device using agile. The vendor delibers as per the contract , but the buyer is not satisfied with the outcome. Which Agile manifesto's value was most likely not approptiately applied?

en: Individuals and interactions over processes and tools
Business people and developers must work together
Pair programming over continuous integration
Customer collaboration over contract negotiations.

x.en: In the scenario , however , the customer does not have detailed requirements upfront and requests that the vendor develops the device using agile methods . Collaboration over negotiations would be more beneficial for both parties.

q.en: You have been hired as an agile expert for an organization that is in the transition phase from predictive to the agile approach in project management. The organization has recently embarked upon the Agile journey . Which of the following is not a change - friendly characteristics for organizations beginning to use Agile approaches

en: Executive management's commitment
Focus on short -term budgeting and metrics versus long -term goals
Talent management maturity and capabilities
Existence of department silos

x.en: If the organization is decomposed into department silos , that prevents accelerated delivery and doesn't encourage forming across- functional teams . The rest of the choices are desirable attributes . [ Agile Practice Guide . 1st edition , pages 73,74]

q.en: One of your project team members doesn't finish his tasks on time . As a project manager, what should you do next ?

en: Release a team member
Conduct one-on-one meeting with the team member
Schedule training sessions for the team member to optimize his performance
Meeting with the project team members and evaluate the impact on the project

x.en: The first step is to Conduct one-on-one meeting with the team member to understand why he leaves the site early and why he does not finish his tasks on time

q.en: As a project manager , you are leading a software development project as a result of observation and conversation , you notice some of the team members need to improve their skills . What should you do first

en: update cost baseline
Review the resource management plan
acquire new members
update risk register

x.en:
The correct answer is Review the resource management plan .
Resource management plan include (Training strategies and Mehods for developing the project team. [PMBOK 6th edition , page 319]

q.en: Situational awareness is a key interpersonal skill for all effective project managers and means knowing what is going on around you and being able to quickly switch your focus. What another skill is often used in conjunction with situatioanl awareness where you the project manager , have to be persuasive in expressing your point and position in order for your project team and stakeholders to react quickly to changing project priorities?

en: influencing
negotiation
Leadership
conflict management

x.en: Influencing is an interpersonal skill that involves awareness of , and consideration for the various perspectives in any situation. It helps you gather relevant and critical information in order to address changing project priorities and resolve unexpected project challenges . It is often used in conjunction with the situational awareness interpersonal tool [PMBOK 6th edition, Page 350]

q.en: Your project is very complex and due to a scope change , you need a few additional experts , which you did not think of earlier . You request that your company provide you with some experts for consultancy work . Although your company has provided you with those experts , they are located in a different geographical location. In this situation , how will you get their input?

en: Ask management to bring them to you
Recruit new members with same skills
choose from current employees
Create a virtual team

x.en: If your experts are located in different geographical locations and you need their input , you will create a virtual team including all these experts [PMBOK 6th edition, Page 333]

q.en: Two team members on your project often disagree . You need a conflict resolution method that provides a long - term resolution. You decide to use which one of the following approaches

en: Compromise
Problem solving
Smoothing
Withdrawal

x.en: Problem solving / Collabotation is long -term resolution while incorporating multiple viewpoint and insights from differing perspectives. This strategy can result in a win -win situation

q.en: While you are in one of the first meetings for your new project that you have been assigned to early, two team memebrs were discussing new ideas that each one thinks is correct and their opinion is the best for the project . You didn't interact or cut the discussion , as you know this is a normal discussion in this phase , which is?

en: Norming
Adjourning
Storming
Performing

x.en: Storming Phase ----- Team members argue and are not openly collaborative while each one thinks is correct and their opinion is the best for the project.

q.en: A project manager wants to recruit another team member to replace an architect who resigned . What document should capture this change .

en: Responsibility assignment matrix ( RAM )
Project management plan
Organizational Process Assets
Ground rule

x.en: Responsibility assignment matrixs ( RAM ) are used to designare roles , responsibilities and levels of authority for specific activities.

q.en: Your project team members have just started to work together and are now adjusting their work habits and behaviors to support each other. Which stages of the Tuckman ladder has your team just enterned and once the current stage ends , what is the next stage?

en: The current stage is Forming and the next stage is Norming
The current stage is Forming and the next stage is Storming
The current stage is Performing and the next stage is Adjourning
The current stage is Norming and the next stage is Performing

x.en: The current stage is Norming and the next stage is Performing

q.en: During a project that affects the entire organization, some groups of stakeholders appear to have low product expectations. As a result, they are not performing as expected . This may put project objectives at risk . What should the project manager do?

en: Ask the project sponsor to intervene and motivate the under performing stakeholders.
Submit a change request
Follow the stakeholder engagement plan
اطلب من راعي المشروع التدخل وتحفيز أصحاب المصلحة ذوي الأداء الضعيف.

x.en: Keywords ( Stakeholders appear to have low product expectations) ------- The stakeholder engagement plan is a component of the project management plan that identifies the strategies and actions required to promote the productive involvement of stakeholders in decision making and execution. It can be formal or informal and highly detailed or broadly framed, based on the needs of the project and the expectations of stakeholders. The stakeholder engagement plan may include but is not limited to specific strategies or approaches for engaging with individuals or groups of stakeholders. PMBOK 6th page ,522

q.en:
A company has always utilized a predictive approach to project management, but now the project management office wants to incorporate some agile best practices to generate earlier revenue realization.
The project manager is about to begin planning for the new project and is concerned that the project team is not equipped to work in a hybrid environment. What is the project manager's best course of action?

en: Check the lessons learned repository for agile best practices
Request the training from the project management office (PMO)
Empower the team to self-organized and study agile best practices
Add the risk of the team's inadequate agile skills to the risk register

x.en: The PMO will typically provide project managers with resources to improve productivity. In this case , the PMO may or may not have internal resources with the necessary knowledge to provide agile training . However , the PMO should be able to provide guidance and external resources, if needed , to train the project team on agile best practices.

q.en:
A project manager is in charge of managing a large construction project of 4 billion USD. Various teams from different countries are involved in this project and the teams need to work cohesively and seamlessly for the success of the project . The task of one team member is highly dependent on that of other team members.
Which of the following is important for the overall success of project integration?

en: Detailed definition of the work packages
Change management
Communications management plan
Adherence of professional code of conduct

x.en: Communication management plan is vital for the success of project integration.

q.en:
You are the project manager of a project to solve customer service problems in your company's call center.
During the execution phase , several quality defects have been discovered , causing customer concern . You would like to create a chart showing the frequency of problems and the causes that have the largest number of defects . Which tool shows defects by volume from greatest to least?

en: Ishikawa Diagram
Flowchart
Pareto Chart
Matrix diagrams

x.en: Keyword ( greatest to least) A pareto chart is specific type of histogram that ranks causes or issues by their overall influence . A Pareto Chart assists in prioritizing corrective actions as the issues with the greatest impact are displayed in order.

q.en: The risk breakdown structure (RBS) helps the project team consider the full range of sources from which individual project risks that may arise. The second level of RBS include Regulatory and Legislation. In which category are these risk included?

en: External Risk
Technical Risk
Internal Risk
Management Risk

q.en: As a project manager , you know the importance of risk management. You always try to include risk management as an agenda item in your status meetings. Some of your project team members complain that discussing risk management issues in status meetings is a waste of time because none of the risks identified on the project so far have actually occurred. What should you do in this situation ?
