Revise the project management plan and move the task to a time when the technical resource will be available.

x.en: The project manager identified a risk where a technical resource for a critical path item may not be available when needed So the project manager should Consult the risk register for an appropriate planned risk response and implement.

q.en: A team has just adopted an agile approach. During daily standup meetings, the team expressed concerns about task delays. The project leader worked with the product owner to get clarity on the features. The project leader asked the team to fast-track all product features to ensure delivery. Sprints are being completed but with either fewer features or low quality. What should the project leader have done to ensure success?

en: Empowered the team to improve their processes, tools, and interactions to be more effective in delivery and removing impediments
Directed teams to possible solutions that help in removing the impediments and contribute to a timely delivery
Suggested to the team to add impediments as work items in the product backlog to be fixed in the next sprints
Asked the team to create an impediment log and keep it updated for use in the next sprint planning

x.en: Project leader/ Scrum master is servant leader so he should empower the team to solve to improve their processes. The team in agile approach is self organized.

q.en:
A project team member is having difficulty delivering assigned tasks for a project that is at risk of being delayed. The main issue is that the team member does not understand a new system that was recently implemented.
What should the project manager do

en: Ask the team member to learn the new system as on-the-job training.
Issue a change request to extend the project schedule
Escalate the team member's performance to the project sponsor
Assign an experienced resource to support the team member

x.en: The Best option (Ask the team member to learn the new system as on-the-job training. )

q.en: During the third iteration of a project, the product owner requests another mandatory feature. This also happened in the previous two sprints, which resulted in failure and caused frustration within the team. What should the project manager do next?

en: Call for an internal meeting to discuss the changes and their value
Ask the product owner to prioritize the backlog with the project team
Request the scrum team to prioritize the product backlog
Incorporate the changes in the last sprint before the first release

x.en: The team could've accepted the PO's requests previously without analyzing the impact of the changes, which resulted in failures. This time the team should discuss the changes first and then make a proper decision. Also in accordance Agile principles, the team shouldn't accept any new features in the middle of the sprint.

q.en:
A company is implementing a project with team members located in different countries and time zones. Individual performance is satisfactory, but the team's performance as a whole is low, especially in terms of group activities.
What should the project manager do?

en: Facilitate communication and team building
Negotiate for new team members
Review and reassign team assignments
Review and update the communications management plan

x.en: As group activities performance is low and team members located in different countries and time zones, thus they need more chances to communicate, team building is a good idea. Good communicate will improve team work as agroup

q.en:
A project team has expressed concern that certain remote team members are not able to collaborate with the larger project team due to their work schedule. The project manager is confused since the entire team is located in the same time zone and believes there are other factors at play.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Examine the team's virtual needs
Implement new options
Rectify ground rule violations
Review performance formally

x.en: Project manager need to find out (examine) the issues first before you can rectify anything. It may just be technical issues or other things

q.en:
A project manager is working with a customer's team on a new project. Some product definitions and requirements are still not clear, but the customer wants to start activities as soon as possible. The organization is also expecting product delivery for a specific date due to a regulatory requirement. Due to the nature of the project, the project manager has decided to use a hybrid approach.
Why did the project manager choose a hybrid approach?

en: A hybrid approach will allow for management of the requirement uncertainties as well as the date restriction
A hybrid approach will allow the project manager to revise the product specifications
A hybrid approach will enable project activities to start immediately and allow for a plan for the requirements definitions
A hybrid approach will ensure the delivery date is accomplished and will eliminate product uncertainties

x.en: Without knowing what is the requirement, as a project manager you cannot plan or schedule. Scope of a project comes from requirements. Schedule development can only be done scope is defined and validated - because it is Hybrid.

q.en: A project manager is part of a team that is launching a series of features to comply with a new regulation. The team has only 6 weeks to release the features to the legacy applications. During the standup meeting, a software engineer indicated that the development of an important feature is on hold until the assigned designer completes a specific task. This delay is a serious road block to meeting the release date. What should the project manager do?

en: Meet with the design team manager to inform them of the current status and request an additional designer
Ask the software engineer to move forward without completing the important feature
Meet with the designer to share the current status and develop a solution to complete the task
Contact the design team manager and ask to reconsider the priority list based on the latest situation

x.en: Always prefer face to face discussion. And involve the person/team. Team are self organized

q.en: A team is delivering features to a customer at every iteration. After completing each iteration, the customer is invited for a review. However, the customer is frequently not available and the review is often delayed, which results in increased rework for the team. What should the project manager do?

en: Request the customer to clarify all requirements at the start of each iteration
Ask the customer to review the deliverables in each iteration based on their availability
Include the customer in daily project activities to gain the required guidance
Plan ahead and define the best way to review the deliverables with the customer

x.en: It is important for the project manager to plan ahead and find a way to review the deliverables with the customer that is efficient and effective, despite the customer's availability. This could involve scheduling regular review sessions in advance, using online collaboration tools to facilitate remote reviews, or finding other ways to ensure that the customer is able to provide timely feedback. By proactively addressing the issue of customer availability, the project manager can help to minimize rework and ensure that the team is able to make progress efficiently.

q.en:
A project team consisting of four team members will be rolling out a company-wide application to both staff and contractors in a country. To deliver within strict the time lines, a local company skilled in application deployment and change management will need to be contracted.
What should the project manager do to empower the local company?

en: Begin to roll out the application by micromanaging the contractor
Manage expectations and agree on the requirements that the contractor will deliver under the supervision of the project manager
Set expectations and agree on the requirements that the contractor will deliver with periodic progress reports
Deploy the contractor's staff under the supervision of the project manager

x.en: Project manager should Manage expectations and agree on the requirements that the contractor will deliver under the supervision of the project manager

q.en: A project manager is managing a construction project that is facing challenges. There is schedule overrun, cost overrun, and the client is unhappy with the specific scope progress. What should the project manager do first?

en: Take action to reduce the cost overrun
Review the scope and project objectives.
Enforce the penalty clause on the supplier
Work with the client on the scope completion

x.en: If the Customer is unhappy about the scope it's better review it

q.en:
In a geographically distributed project team, the project team members continue to email status reports and update schedules after their weekly meeting discussions. However, the team is having difficulty tracking the changes and progress made.
What should the project manager do?

en: Develop a document management software for version control
Maintain separate document control via regions to avoid discrepancies.
Facilitate training on version control and project artifacts.
Maintain a central repository of artifacts with a version control system

x.en: The correct Answer ( Maintain a central repository of artifacts with a version control system)

q.en: A project manager has been assigned to a project where collaboration with the business is a critical key factor. The project manager is not sure about which approach to use. A senior project manager has been assigned to help the project manager. What advice should the senior project manager provide?

en: Establish a project management methodology that requires the customer to provide daily updates to the team
Suggest using an agile approach since customer and team collaboration is critical for project success
Provide a project management template for the project manager to follow as a guide
Work with the project manager to develop a new approach that will bring benefits to the project

x.en:
Keyword (collaboration with the business is a critical key factor) so the Agile approach is the best .
Agile Values 

 Individuals and interactions over processes and tools.
 Working software over comprehensive documentation.
 Customer collaboration over contract negotiation.
 Responding to change over following a plan

q.en: A project manager is managing a large project. A stakeholder has just discovered a new risk that has not been identified in earlier stages. What should the project manager do?

en: Confirm to the stakeholder that the risk register has been completed and validated by all stakeholders
Perform a risk analysis directly with the stakeholder who raised the risk and update the risk register
Add the risk to the risk register and reevaluate the register with help from the project team and stakeholders
Communicate the risk to the steering committee and request a mitigation plan from senior management

x.en: Any new risk that is discovered, the project manager must add / update the risk register and then conduct a risk analysis to prioritize the risks to develop effective response plans for the risks according to their priorities

q.en: A Scrum team is analyzing the burndown chart on day four of a 15-day sprint. The burndown chart is shown below. What should the team do next?

en: Ask the project team to select any additional stories as they have additional capacity than planned
Continue with the sprint work as planned and keep monitoring
Continue with the sprint as the progress shows buffers for potential interruptions
Ask the product owner if some low-priority stories could be cut from the sprint

x.en: It's just day 4 of 15 days sprint. it's too early to take any action. Monitoring will be appropriate

q.en: A project manager is closing a project and preparing to hand it over to the operations team. During handover, a delayed invoice was submitted with a higher-than- planned cost against the project work. Consequently, project handover was delayed and the project's reported completion costs were increased. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

en: Involved the finance team and discussed the issue with the vendor
Reviewed the total committed cost against the cost invoiced at project closing
Captured and reviewed all of the project work and related costs regularly
Notified all vendors about the invoicing and nonpayment deadlines

x.en: The project manager should Captured and reviewed all of the project work and related costs regularly to avoid the delay and increasing of cost.

q.en: A project manager is working with a co-located agile project team that has worked together long enough to be in the performing phase of team development. An unforeseen event has caused the team to be dispersed and they are now unable to co-locate. What should the project manager do to keep the team performing as effectively as possible

en: Provide the team with virtual collaboration software and training on the software to minimize disruption
Transition the team from an agile approach to a predictive approach for better performance control
Ask the project sponsor and executive stakeholders to encourage the team to maintain their performance
Evaluate project performance and step in if performance decreases to an unacceptable level

x.en: The team is in the performing stage of Tuckman, they are self-organizing and they can work through issues smoothly and effectively. What the Project manager need to do is monitor their performance to be sure they are still performing as they usually do, and, if there is a drop in performance, the team will be notified, and they will discuss to proffered a solution to the drop in performance

q.en: A project manager is reviewing the requirements of a large program.Which requirements should the project team prioritize to avoid getting fines

en: Establishing company processes
Complying with new regulations
Developing new product lines
Certifying sustainable products

x.en: Complying with new regulations to avoid getting fines

q.en:
A project manager is assigned to a critical software development project. The team is using a hybrid approach and has divided development into four sprints. At the end of sprint three, the project manager discovers that the earned value (EV) is US$500,000 and the planned value (PV) is US$550,000.
What should the project manager do?

en: Adjust the budget
Introduce a float
Fast track the project
Adjust the project time line

x.en: SPI = EV/ PV. EV(US$500,000) / PV(US$550,000) = 0.9 So current SPI is < 1. It means behind schedule So the best option is Fast track the project

q.en:
During the lessons learned workshop, one stakeholder mentioned that the project was unsuccessful as it did not deliver the expected business value.
What should the project manager do to address this concern

en: Review the communications management plan with the stakeholders
Review the business benefits realization plan with the stakeholders
Review the project management plan budget with the stakeholders
Review the project management plan tasks with the stakeholders

x.en: BENEFITS REALIZATION PLAN: A document outlining the activities necessary for achieving the planned benefits

q.en:
There is a conflict on an agile project about following organizational processes, many of which do not add any value to the project.
To resolve this, which one of the following should be regarded with the highest priority

en: Needs of the organization
Needs of the customer
Needs of the project manage
Needs of the agile lead

x.en: One of the agile principle is customer satisfaction

q.en:
A project team is using one of the visual management tools to identify dependencies. It was identified that domain knowledge from one team needs to be shared with another team to ensure the continuity of deliverables.
What should the project manager do?

en: Redistribute the team members so knowledge is available in both teams
Request the respective teams to plan for knowledge-sharing sessions
Remove the dependency to eliminate the need for knowledge sharing
Merge both teams into one team so the knowledge is commonly available

x.en: The correct Answer (Request the respective teams to plan for knowledge-sharing sessions)

q.en:
A team member who is working on a critical project deliverable reported that their computer is not working. The IT department says that due to a high workload, they will not be able to provide assistance for 1 week.
How should the project manager address this situation?

en: Ask the team member to find an innovative solution or workaround to overcome the issue and avoid project delays
Explore options with the IT department to expedite the necessary repairs based on criticality of the project
Schedule a meeting with the project sponsor to request a budget to buy or rent a new computer
Use project reserves to buy new equipment to avoid an impact to the critical path of the project

x.en: The correct Answer (Explore options with the IT department to expedite the necessary repairs based on criticality of the project)

q.en:
A project manager is leading a team of diverse individuals of all ages. The working hours for the project were set at the beginning of the project, and all team members agreed to the hours. However, later in the project, one of the team members informed the project manager that the previously agreed upon hours no longer work due to the team member's personal commitments.
What should the project manager do?

en: Helped the team redefine the MVP
Validated the iteration goals with the customer
Invited the customer to the daily meetings
Changed the duration of iterations to deliver more value

x.en: The Correct Answer (Validated the iteration goals with the customer)

q.en:
A project manager works in a hierarchical organization. The project team members are used to being told what to do, and the performance reviews include the percentage of completion of the allocated tasks. After a conversation with the sponsor, the project manager realizes that they need to reassign a couple of tasks to meet the next milestone. This change can be perceived as poor performance by the current assignees.
What should the project manager do?

en: Ask the less experienced team member privately to stop working on the task and inform another team member that the work has been reassigned
Ask the more experienced team member privately to take the task and inform the other team members that work has been reassigned
Organize a team meeting to inform team members about a change in direction and work with them to change the task allocation
Organize a team meeting and inform the team members that, as the person accountable for delivery, they decided to change the task allocation

x.en: The Correct Answer (Organize a team meeting to inform team members about a change in direction and work with them to change the task allocation)

q.en:
A project manager has just been hired to lead a project team in a hybrid environment. The team is working on a group of critical projects.
What should the project manager do to ensure the right environment and authority are in place to effectively deliver the projects?

en: Appoint a self-organizing project team that is not influenced by organizational factors
Develop a detailed project management plan to share with project resources
Create a project steering committee aligned with existing organizational structures.
Develop a detailed risk log and share it with all of the project stakeholders

x.en: The Correct Answer (Create a project steering committee aligned with existing organizational structures.)

q.en:
A building management system (BMS) project is in its commissioning phase and handover to the operations team will commence soon. However, the project manager noted that both the project and operation teams are not able to properly operate the BMS. As a result, there is an increased risk of the project schedule being delayed.
What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

en: Allocated a dedicated handover team at early stages of the project
Allocated proper resources for training on BMS in the project plan
Brought both teams together in a joint meeting to resolve the issue
Made some adjustments to BMS to be more suitable for the teams

x.en: The questions get tricky sometimes with the end, I think thats really the trick to beating this exam. This particular question asks "What should they have done?" Not "What should they do" or "what should they do next" The issue is that neither of them know how to operate it. If this was a design flaw that made it over-complicated, that would be an issue where the team could get with operations and train them, but the issue here is that its such a complex software by nature that the team can build it but not know how to operate it/how things interact with each other.

q.en: Due to a company merger and acquisition process, the main stakeholder of a critical project has been changed.This new stakeholder complains that they were unaware of a delay on the project of which the rest of the stakeholders were aware. All the communications about the project are shared via email at the start of every week. How should the project manager address this situaion?

en: Send evidence to the new stakeholder that the project's status was sent according to the schedule
Suggest that the new stakeholder review the project status before the next board meeting
Discuss project requirements with the new stakeholder, and update the communications management plan
Share the communications management plan with the new stakeholder

x.en: New stakeholder complains that they were unaware of a delay on the project So the project manager should Discuss project requirements with the new stakeholder, and update the communications management plan

q.en: Ehab has assigned as a project manager im a multinational company to implement new software that will impact serveral departments. To guarantee alignment of stakeholder expectations with th final product , what should Ehab develop?

en: Stakeholder engagement assessment matrix
Stakeholder engagement plan
Business Case
Resources breakdown structure (RBS)

x.en: Stakeholder engagement plan: identifies the management strategies and actions required to effectively engage stakeholders. The stakeholder engagement plan provides guidance and information on managing stakeholder expectations. The stakeholder engagement plan include specific strategies or approaches for engaging with individuals or groups of stakeholders.

q.en: One of the factors in making a project successful is stakeholder engagement level. Which of the following is the characteristic of a supportive stakeholder on a project ?

en: Unaware of potential impacts
Actively engaged in project success
Aware of potential impacts but resistant to change
Aware of potential impacts and supportive to change

x.en:
Stakeholders Level of Engagement
- Unaware. Unaware of project and potential impacts.
- Resistant. Aware of project and potential impacts and resistant to change.
- Neutral. Aware of project yet neither supportive nor resistant.
- Supportive. Aware of project and potential impacts and supportive to change.
- Leading. Aware of project and potential impacts and actively engaged in ensuring the project is a success.

q.en: A key stakeholder in your construction project has recently resigned from his duties due to personal reasons. What should you do next as part of stakeholder management?

en: Remove all changes suggested by the stakeholder
Update stakeholder register
Contact the sponsor
Initiate an investigation into his resignation

x.en: When stakeholders are no longer involved in the project, you should update the stakeholder register to remove them from the project.

q.en: A recently appointed project manager is in constant conflict with a senior manager . Since this is not ideal for the team , the project manager wants to resolve this. What should the project manager do

en: Escalate the issue to the project sponsor
Seek guidance from other project managers
Enlist the help of a neutral mediator
Request scheduled face-to-face meetings with the senior manager

x.en:
Keywords(A recently-conflict with a senior manager-the project manager wants to resolve).
It is obvious that you will choose the answer scheduled face-to-face meetings with the senior manager , but you need to read the question again - A recently appointed project manager and the conflict with the senior manager, that is, he may has authority over the project manager himself, and it was not clarified in the question what kind of organizational structure is it (Projectized / functional) in addition to the question It says resolve so the best option in this case if the problem is out of control or authority of the project manager's is escalation

q.en: You are always struggling with resource supply for your project as they are shared across various projects. Who should you escalate this isse to

en: PMO
The sponsor
HR department
Executive manager

x.en:
Shared resources are usually administered by PMO.
PMO: A structure to support decision making and delivery of change work within the organisation. PMOs are constantly evolving as organizations try to ensure that the PMO meets the needs of the organization. It is not enough to see the PMO within the context of a project management office supporting a particular project. It is much better to envision the PMO as the structure put in place to carry out projects for the entire organization. This may happen through a permanent PMO or via multiple offices (portfolio offices, program offices or project offices) which may be permanent or temporary. The focus is on providing central and local services.

q.en: You have been appointed a project manager within an information systems organization. You arenot aware of the organization's policies and procedures. If you want to know more about the organization's general issues management procedures, which of the following should you review?

en: Enterprise Environmental Factors(EFFs)
Organizational Process Assets (OPAs)
Issue log
Project Management Plan

x.en:
If you are a new manager.

You find yourself in a new company.

The culture is different. The processes and policies are unlike anything you’re used to.

To make things more complicated, you have a team that expects you to provide strong leadership and stakeholders who expect reports on your progress.
Organizational process assets are tangible resources used by an organization to guide the management of its projects and operations. They include things like templates, contracts, processes, reports, and financial statements.

According to The Standard for Project Management and A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide), “Organizational Process Assets (OPAs) are the plans, processes, policies, procedures, and knowledge bases specific to and used by the performing organization. These assets influence the management of the project. Organizational process assets include any artifact, practice, or knowledge from any or all of the performing organizations involved in the project that can be used to execute or govern the project. The organizational process assets also include the organization’s lessons learned from previous projects and historical information. Organizational Process Assets may include completed schedules, risk data, and earned value data.”

q.en:
In the middle of a project , a business unit manager who regularly interacts with the project manager's team is promoted to a higher management position . The replacement manager is from the same unit and is somewhat familiar with the project.
After getting more information about the new manager , what is the project manager's next step?

en: Send the new manager a copy of the project charter to ensure the project objectives are understood
Schedule a meeting with the new manager to discuss the business analysis team's plan
Update the stakeholder register and the stakeholder engagement plan to include the new manager
Contact the previous business unit manager to learn mire about the new manager.

x.en: Through your reading of such a question, you find the answer clear. The question says that the business unit manager who interacts regularly with the project manager team is promoted to a higher administrative position. Here he interacts regularly, that is, affects the project, and as long as he affects the project, she is among those Stakeholders The question also clarifies that he has been promoted to an administrative position The highest, then, here means a change in the level of power, so we must update and put a plan for it, any strategies.Do not forget, my dear brother, that the project management professional exam relies heavily on understanding, and if you focus on understanding, the exam will become very easy and very interesting. No matter how difficult the questions are, it will not affect your passing the exam.

q.en: In a global project , the project manager has to plan and manage communication between the team members and stakeholders in order to ensure the project will remain on track and achieve its goals. What should the project manager do?

en: Consider cultural difference among stakeholders
Schedule communication training for management level stakeholders
Conduct an integration meeting among all stakeholders
Understand how political aspects can affect the project

x.en: The question here focuses on ensuring that the project stays on track and achieves its goals. In addition to a global project, the project manager must plan and manage communication between team members - communication here is the answer to the question. We are in a different environment and we plan to communicate between the team so the project manager must differences between cultures to ensure success. .

q.en: Which of the following activities is the most important to perform to help manage a project meeting ?

en: Limit the meeting to a specific length of time
Create and follow an agenda
Ensure that every attendee has a chance to speak
Follow up on action items

x.en: The meeting agenda sets the tone , the length,and the format of how the meeting will be conducted. Using a formal agenda makes it easy to create meeting minutes and followup actions items after the meeting

q.en: Eng.Ramadan Mouftah has recently been assigned as the project manager for a new shopping mall construction project. Eng.Ramadan suspects that there are materials in the building that may be a serious health hazard. What should Eng.Ramadan do?

en: Perform integration change control
Hire a hazardous materials expert to investigate
Implement the risk response plan
Asses the risk and update the risk register

x.en: Keyword (suspect) so, the first step you should Hire a hazardous expertto carry out inspection. The project manager can stop the work immediately if the scenario mentioned (ensure) not suspect.

q.en: A project manager for a software technology project works in a matrixed organization with virtual teams. Unfortunately, the functional manager informs the project manager that there may not be any resources available to test the software. What should the project manager do next?

en: Engage with the functional manager to discuss details to obtain the required support
Discuss testing requirements at the weekly project meeting to negotiate the best approach to test software.
Send an email to the procurement specialist to negotiate with a company that specializes in software testing
Request a teleconference meeting with the sponsor to submit a change request to allow the development team to conduct testing

x.en: The project manager works in a matrix organization, meaning the decision is based on consultation and participation, and it is taken between the project manager and the functional manager. So, the project manager should engage with the functional manager to discuss the details.

q.en: A project manager is attending a progress meeting with a client . The client requests a design change which might potentially add value to the project. What action should the project manager take

en: Consult with team members and allow them to make a decision
Accommodate the change request to serve the client's needs
Make transactional decisions focusing on the project goals
Convince the client not to make changes to the project

x.en: In this scenario of the question being asked, the best option is to consult the team to enable the team to make decisions

q.en: A project manager has recently assigned to a new project. When the project manager first meets the project team , the team tells the project manager that all of the management plans and documents for the project are missing . What should the project manager do ?

en: Create the project management plans with the project team and share the documents with the stakeholders
Adapt the project management plans and documents from previous executed projects in order to save time
Ask the stakeholders to develop all of the project artifacts so the project team can continue their scheduled activities
Continue working on scheduled tasks to avoid delaying the project and leave the development of the project artifacts for later

x.en: In this question, it is mentioned that all plans and documents are missing, so the project manager must create them and participate with those involved in the project to review and evaluate them.

q.en: A stressful situation has presented some challenges for the team. The project manager notices strees behavior in some of the team members, and it is beginning to spreed across the group. The project manager needs to coach the team to change their mindset in order to more efficient. What should the project manager do

en: Meet with the team to discuss the correct, expected behavior in stressful situations and start practicing it
Create an environment of respect and fairness so the team can increase their project performance is stressful situations.
Ensure the people care about each other and work effectively together through effective team management

x.en:
In this scenario from the question asked, the best choice is to create an environment where the team can adapt with changes and stressful situations needs as a project manager to change the mindset and this needs to create an environment of cooperation and fairness
Option(Establish a productive environment where all team members can assist one another with the workload) Already it is a productive environment like many environments that exist in the world, but there are conflicts between the team. There are suspicions and psychological wars that create a threat and It is indeed a productive environment like many environments that exist in the world, but there are conflicts between the team. There are suspicions and psychological wars that can pose a threat and create stressful situations. Therefore, to change the mentality, you start by changing the environment and in it there is respect and fairness. Why? to increase performance in difficult situations? Here is the answer (creating an environment of respect and fairness So that the team can increase their project performance in stressful situations.) Related to the question

q.en: A project requires the procurement of a large a,ount of equipment that needs to be on site before any other activity can begin. The procurement department has a lengthy approval process. What should the project manager do?

en: Use the existing equipment and replace it later with the new equipment
Contact the vendor that supplied similar equipment for a previous project
Ask the project sponsor to expedite the vendor selection process
Work with the procurement team to find alternative options

x.en: In this scenario, although the procedures are lengthy and may take a lot of time, and may pose a danger in the event of a delay in the project, so we should not take the procurement procedure without participation and consultation. Here, the skills of the project manager appear in working with the team, communicating with the departments, and finding alternative solutions.

q.en: A project is currently in the execution phase. Because of the complexity of the project and the large number of regulatory requirements involved, the project manager decides to hold a management review with senior executives to ensure the successful implementation of project deliverables. What should the project manager review during the management review to ensure the meeting is effective?

en: Metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs) that objectively reflect the status of deliverables
The deliverables that are performing well and those that need more work
Potential changes to the project's strategy and the feedback from senior executives
Specialized reports created specifically for the meeting as per directions from the project sponsor

x.en: In this scenario, as a project manager, you must choose metrics that reflect the status of the deliverables. It might be metrics such as number of defects and percentage of completion.

q.en: Project progress meetings occur via virtual conference calls. In every project progress meeting, one team member continuously interrupts others during discussions. Other team members often have no opportunity to talk or complete their explanations. What should the project manager do ?

en: Manage time efficiently using the agenda and ask each participant to contribute
Start the meeting with a review of the ground rules, meeting objectives,and the agenda
Speak individually with the team member who always disrupts the conversations
Speak individually with the team members who do not participate in conversations

x.en: In this scenario, as a project manager, you should start with the general rules for preventing interruptions. The general rules are guidelines agreed upon by the meeting participants in order to make the meeting more productive and enjoyable.

q.en: A project stakeholder complained that they didn't receive an important delivery that was stated in the schedule. The team member responsible for this deliverable explained that they sent an email to the stakeholder, adivising them that the deliverable would not be delivered on time. What should the project manager have done to avoid this situation?

en: Ensured that the team member didn't communicate directly with the project stakeholder
Told the team member to send the unfinished deliverable to the stakeholder and finalize it later
Communicated with the stakeholder directly regarding the delivery delay
Confirmed that the stakeholder was made aware of the delivery delay

x.en: In this scenario, as a project manager, you must confirm that the dispatch has been completed. The option may be to review the communication management plan, but it is not among the options. x.en: Lesson learned repository is One of the frequent deconflictions is the difference between the lessons learned register and the lessons learned repository. At first glance, these two concepts may seem the same to each other, it can be said that they are created in the same logic as the decency of the documents, but the main difference between the two is this. Lessons learned register is a document that is constantly created and updated with the start of the project, while lessons learned repository is a document that contains lessons learned about past projects, not limited to the current project. In the process of closing the project, the lessons learned register is transferred to the lessons learned repository. q.en: A recently promoted project manager must facilitate the weekly status update meeting. What should the project manager do to ensure a productive meeting?

x.en:
Agendas are a common meeting tool. A good agenda should provide a high-level list of activities that will enable the team to achieve the meeting objectives. In addition to providing the meeting roadmap, it can also be used as a motivational tool. Refer to it frequently to check off the items that have been completed. This will reinforce what's been accomplished so far and keep the momentum moving forward.

The agenda can also be used to manage conversation. If the team begins to discuss topics that are scheduled for later in the meeting, refer to the agenda and ask them if the conversation can be postponed until then. Offer to capture a few relevant ideas in the parking lot to make sure you don't forget to discuss them.

The following steps should be used for meeting planning

 Prepare and distribute the agenda stating the objectives of the meeting.
 
 Ensure that the meetings start and finish at the published time.
 
 Ensure appropriate participants are invited and attend.
 
 Stay the topic.
 
 Manage expectations , issues , and conflicts during the meetings.
 
 Record all actions and those who have been allocated the responsibility for completing the action.

x.en:
The term enterprise environmental factors refers to an input/output mechanism that is supposed to identify factors that cannot be controlled by the project team but have a significant impact on how the project has to be managed or on the outcome of the project, program or portfolio. This impact can be of positive or negative nature. The term is not very popular, but the concept is really important, given that most if not all projects are affected by the context they are managed in. As an example, if you are not allowed to use external resources and your project team lacks some skills to successfully execute the project, this is a result of an enterprise environmental factor.

q.en: An organization has established a controlling project management office (PMO). The first task of the PMO is to update the guidelines for project compliance in the organization. Which of the following could the PMO enforce ?( Choose three)

en: Use of particular project management methodologies
Adherence to local health regulations
Adoption of specific templates, forms , and tools
Assignment of project managers by the PMO
Conformance to governance frameworks

x.en:
There are three basic types of Project Management Office (PMO) organisations, varying in the degree of control and influence they have on projects within the organisation. You will need to determine which type you need to establish in order to have an effective project office.

The three types of PMOs include:

1. Supportive PMO
The Supportive PMO generally provides support in the form of on-demand expertise, templates, best practices, access to information and expertise on other projects, and the like. This can work in an organisation where projects are done successfully in a loosely controlled manner and where additional control is deemed unnecessary. Also, if the objective is to have a sort of "clearing-house" of project management information across the enterprise to be used freely by project managers, then the Supportive PMO is the right type.

2. Controlling PMO
In organisations where there is a desire to "rein in" the activities, processes, procedures, documentation, and more - a controlling PMO can accomplish that. Not only does the organisation provide support, but it also requires that the support be used. Requirements might include adoption of specific methodologies, templates, forms, conformance to governance, and application of other PMO controlled sets of rules. In addition, project offices might need to pass regular reviews by the controlling PMO, and this may represent a risk factor on the project. This works if a) there is a clear case that compliance with project management organisation offerings will bring improvements in the organisation and how it executes on projects, and b) the PMO has sufficient executive support to stand behind the controls the PMO puts in place.

3. Directive PMO
This type goes beyond control and actually "takes over" the projects by providing the project management experience and resources to manage the project. As organisations undertake projects, professional project managers from the PMO are assigned to the projects. This injects a great deal of professionalism into the projects, and, since each of the project managers originates and reports back to the directive PMO, it guarantees a high level of consistency of practice across all projects. This is effective in larger organisations that often matrix out support in various areas, and where this setup would fit the culture.

The best type is very specific to the organisation, culture, and history of what works and what does not. But the objectives are - more or less - to:

Implement a common methodology
Standardise terminology
Introduce effective repeatable project management processes
Provide common supporting tools
Ultimately, the objective is to improve levels of project success within the organisation
Being aware of these types can help you and your organisation more easily accomplish this.

q.en: The project near to complete and a previously unidentified risk is discovered . Which funds will the project manager use to cover this risk?

en: Project funding baseline
Cost baseline
Management reserve
Contingency reserve

x.en:
During the course of a project, you and your project team identify risks which are referred to as known/unknown risks. These risks are known – that is, they've been identified. However, we don't know the amount of rework that will be required if the risks occur.

We handle the known/unknown risks by creating a contingency reserve using estimating techniques such as the Expected Monetary Value (EMV) Method. The project manager adds the contingency reserve to the project budget, resulting in the cost baseline.

Cost Baseline = Cost Estimate + Contingency Reserve

Furthermore, project managers encounter unknown/unknown risks. These risks have not been identified. Therefore, we don't know the cost of responding to these risks. Here's where the management reserve comes into play.
The management reserve is the amount of the project budget reserved for unforeseen work that is within the scope of the project. The project manager adds the management reserve to the cost baseline resulting in the total project budget.

Project Budget = Cost Baseline + Management Reserve
The project manager does not have control of the management reserve. That's why it's called the "management" reserve. It's controlled by management, typically the project sponsor or senior management. Consequently, the project manager cannot access or adjust the management reserve without approval from the sponsor.

q.en: At the daily project meeting , team members are complaining about receiving emails from their functional managers to support other nonproject-related tasks. This is having a negative impact on the team's productivity. What should the project manager do next?

en: Log this as a risk in the risk register and continue to monitor the issue at subsequent meetings
Ask the product owner to speak with the functional managers to ensure future requirements come through the product owner.
Address this concern with the functional managers to ensure there will be no further delays
Schedule a meeting with all of the functional managers to resolve the resource conflicts

x.en: The project manager should Schedule a meeting with all of the functional managers to resolve the resource conflicts

q.en: A company's new communication system will include online dashboard reporting. The executive board might receive bi-weekly performance reports through the online dashboard. What should the project manager do ?

en: Update the communications management plan
Review the project management plan
Update the stakeholder engagement plan
Review the configuration management plan

x.en: A company's new communication system need to Update the communications management plan to comply with expectations of stakeholders

q.en: You are a project manager for a construction project. During the project review meeting, the stakeholders decided to respond to known and new risks encountered during project execution. Which of the following artifacts should the stakeholders review?

en: Risk-adjusted backlog
Document management plan.
project log
Assumption/constraints log

x.en:
A risk-adjusted backlog is a backlog that includes work and actions to address threats and opportunities. Pmbok7 page#185.

The risk-adjusted backlog is a sprint or release backlog containing risk response tasks for actionable risks. For negative risks, these actions include avoiding, mitigating, and transferring. For positive risks, they include exploiting, enhancing, and sharing

q.en: The management of the stakeholder expectations in a high-risk project is the responsibility of……

en: Project sponsor.
Project manager.
Senior Manager.
Project Officer.

x.en: The project manager is responsible for the management of stakeholder expectations in the project.

q.en:
A company that is heavily focused on delivering projects using predictive approaches on-boards a new project manager who uses hybrid approaches. The scope of the project contains a number of unclear requirements.
How should the project manager plan the delivery of the project?

en: Break down the requirements and prioritize the requirements into iterative work packages
Escalate the issue of unclear requirements to the management team and wait for final authorization
Ignore the unclear requirements and focus on the delivery plan of the project.
Wait for the requirements to be more clear before any further action is taken on the project

x.en: In the scenario The scope of the project contains a number of unclear requirements so The best option (Break down the requirements and prioritize the requirements into iterative work packages).

q.en:
A company is changing their current business model. The change requires implementing a complex project using multiple agile teams.
What three options should the project manager have the testing team adopt as testing mechanisms? (Choose three.)

en: Security and performance testing
Tests based on behavior and test-driven development
Independent personal testing
An experimental approach to cover all possible choices
Story testing

x.en:
The three options should the project manager have the testing team adopt as testing mechanisms in agile teams.
A. Story testing
B. Tests based on behavior and test-driven development
C. Independent personal testing

q.en:
A customer's technical lead discussed a new feature with the project manager. The project manager believes the new feature will boost performance significantly and adds it as a high-priority item in the sprint backlog. At the end of the sprint, all of the planned stories were not completed because the new feature took more time.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Agree with the project team to modify and delete some of the stories in the current sprint backlog
Negotiate with the scrum master before adding the new story to the sprint backlog
Obtain approval from the project team and add the new story to the product backlog
Receive an agreement from the product owner and add the new story to the product backlog

x.en: The product owner is responsible for adding and prioritizing user stories in product backlog. Adding new features took a long time, which led to the incompleteness of all the planned user stories. Therefore, to get the team back on the right track, agree with the project team to modify and delete some stories in the sprint backlog.

q.en:
The project sponsor of a major initiative is consistently changing the prioritization of modular work packages. The team is used to three week sprints and is becoming increasingly frustrated with the daily changes in scope.
What should the project manager do?

en: Set up a meeting with the project team and ask for their opinion on what to do
Set up a meeting with the sponsor to explain the importance of keeping a strict sprint cycle
Decrease the sprint cycle to the average reprioritization request by calculating it in days.
Move to a Kanban strategy so that work can be reallocated more easily

x.en: The project manager should communicate with the sponsor and discuss the impact of the frequent changes in prioritization on the team's work and schedule. They should explain the importance of a strict sprint cycle for maintaining momentum, predictability, and accountability for the project, and find ways to align the sponsor's priorities with the team's work. This can help to mitigate the frustration of the team and ensure the project is on track.

q.en:
An agile team is required to address a technical, complex requirement that has no visual deliverable to show the customer.
What guidance should the product manager provide to improve the requirement development?

en: Allow the team to focus and complete the complex work because it will reduce the risk of finding issues later in the project
Reprioritize the product backlog by lowering the priority of the complex activity, so it will be worked on later in the project
Inform the customer that there will not be any deliverable due to the complexity involved in the requirement
Discuss this with the team and reprioritize the backlog to deliver maximum value by including a portion of the complex work

x.en: The product manager should collaborate with the team to break down the complex requirement into smaller, manageable portions that can be incorporated into the product backlog. This approach allows the team to work on the complex requirement incrementally, delivering value to the customer and potentially making it easier to demonstrate progress. By reprioritizing the backlog and integrating portions of the complex work, the team can better manage the requirement development process.

q.en:
A project is halfway through its execution phase. The quality specifications for the project deliverables are formally accepted. However, a key stakeholder is dissatisfied, stating that the deliverables do not meet the quality specifications.
What should the project manager do in this situation?

en: Inform the project sponsor of the stakeholder's dissatisfaction
Notify the stakeholder that arbitration procedures will be followed
Document the issue in the issue log and send a report to management
Review the requirements traceability matrix and conduct inspections

x.en: A key stakeholder is dissatisfied, stating that the deliverables do not meet the quality specifications SO the project manager should Review the requirements traceability matrix and conduct inspections

q.en:
A team is finishing the third release to present to the stakeholder as part of a demonstration. The company that subcontracts the developers has communicated that there is a cash flow problem and the company will not be able to provide the same resources for the next iterations.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Create a risk register to track the risks and request additional budget
Analyze the impact against the release plan if the blocker is not addressed
Work with the project owner to prioritize the product backlog
Escalate the situation to the project sponsor for a possible resolution

x.en: Analyze the impact against the release plan if the blocker is not addressed

q.en:
An organization is transitioning from a predictive to an agile approach.
What should the project manager do to ensure that the agile approaches will bring about significant change?

en: Learn as much as possible about the organization
Identify the organization's key clients
Obtain full management support
Conduct agile training for the team members

x.en: An organization is transitioning from a predictive to an agile approach so the project manager should Conduct agile training for the team members to ensure that the agile approaches will bring about significant change

q.en:
A project manager has been transferred to another country to work on a key project. The project manager successfully completed the planning phase and has started the execution phase, reporting good progress. During the last meeting with the project sponsor, the project manager was told that some stakeholders have complained that the project manager's emails are very harsh.
What should the project manager do to solve this situation?

en: Determine the level of influence of the stakeholders who are complaining
Adjust the communications management plan to gain stakeholder trust.
Change the communication mode from emails to meetings to reduce stakeholders complaints
Explain to the sponsor that the communication model being used is from company headquarters

x.en: some stakeholders have complained that the project manager's emails are very harsh so the project manager should Adjust the communications management plan to gain stakeholder trust.

q.en:
A project manager is assigned to work on a complex and innovative project. The technology being used and developed is new and complicated, and most of the stakeholders are unfamiliar with it.
Which approach should the project manager use as a servant leader?

en: Allocate resources to provide training about the new technology to the stakeholders
Contact the project sponsor to get those stakeholders removed from the project
Ask stakeholders to find and self-fund education about this new technology
Escalate the issue with upper management to find a novel solution for this situation

x.en: Allocate resources to provide training about the new technology to the stakeholders

q.en:
A company is about to start a complex research project. Due to the level of uncertainty, the project manager recommends the use of a hybrid approach; however, the organization only has experience with predictive projects.
How can the project manager strategize the use of a hybrid approach to the organization?

en: Present the benefits of a hybrid approach to key stakeholders to get their support
Create a project change request to execute the project using a hybrid approach
Submit a notification to the project team confirming they will be using a hybrid approach on the project
Send a letter to the project management office (PMO) requesting to use a hybrid approach

x.en: Present the benefits of a hybrid approach to key stakeholders to get their support

q.en:
A company plans to initiate a project involving a new technology. Approval for the project is required.
What should the project manager do?

en: Identify the risks in implementing the new technology
Review the cost and schedule baselines for execution
Define change management for the new technology
Analyze the cost and identify the project benefits

x.en: New Technology so the project manager should evaluate this technique before Approval by Analyzing the cost and identify the project benefits

q.en:
In the middle of a software development project, the lead design programmer accepted an offer from a competitor. The project manager needs to find a replacement to meet an upcoming milestone.
What should the project manager do?

en: Update the resource calendar
Issue a request to the change control board (CCB)
Consult the risk response plan
Assign the tasks to another team member

x.en: Loosing an expert to a competitor is a risk that shoul have been envisaged and planned for.

q.en:
A project is in progress with a team that is new to agile approaches. After the first sprint review, the team performance begins slipping, and the conclusion is that there is not an adequate flow of work for the team.
What should the project manager do?

en: Submit a change request to re baseline the project
Discuss the issue with the stakeholders
Change the project approach to hybrid
Provide the product owner with training

x.en: The flow of work in an agile process stems from the product backlog. The backlog is provided by the product owner/customer, which are important stakeholders. They prioritize work packages based on value, put them in the product backlog, and then during the sprint, the team picks items off of the backlog that they think they can finish in the time alotted for the sprint.

q.en:
A project manager is assigned to a new project team that has several stakeholders who can have significant influence over the project outcomes. The project manager categorized the stakeholders into four different groups and wants to define the communication strategy.
 

How should the project manager handle communication?

en: Utilize a uniform communication structure across all groups
Develop and define a communication strategy for stakeholders.
Define and direct communication to influential stakeholders.
Describe the four groups in the project stakeholder matrix

x.en: The best option (Develop and define a communication strategy for stakeholders) to define the communication strategy .

q.en:
A project team is conducting sprint planning. At the end of the sprint, the product increment must be deployed on a customer's site. The product owner received an email from the account manager that the customer may not be ready to install the new version of the product.
What should the project manager do?

en: Contact the customer's project manager
Ask the product owner to inform the customer
Contact the customer's technical lead
Ask the sales team to inform the customer

x.en:
The project manager should contact the customer's project manager to understand the reason for the delay and to determine if there are any issues that need to be addressed before the product increment can be deployed. This will give the project manager an opportunity to discuss any concerns or issues the customer may have and to develop a plan to address them. The project manager should also inform the product owner and the rest of the project team of the situation and discuss the potential impact on the project schedule and deliverables.

It is not appropriate to ask the sales team or product owner to inform the customer as they may not have the necessary expertise or experience to address the customer's concerns. Contacting the customer's technical lead may not be the best approach as they may not have the authority to make decisions about the installation of the new version of the product.

q.en:
A project manager has been assigned with initiating a large project to deliver complex equipment. Part of the project will be the result of a long research process, but once this is completed, the other part of the project must be incrementally delivered to the customer.
Which approach should the project manager choose for this project?

en: Adaptive
Predictive
Incremental
Hybrid

x.en: Adaptive is the correct answer. This is nowhere mentioned that the first part had a predefined scope. Since the first part was a long research, that has a high chance to be iterative and the 2nd part is evident enough to be increment. Both are the part of Adaptive but not Hybrid.

q.en:
A project manager is using a subcontractor for mobile application development. When the project team tests the application, they realize it does not comply with the new company user-interface standards. Even though these new standards were not included in the statement of work (SOW), the subcontractor agrees to the additional scope as long as payment for this additional work is paid immediately.
What should the project manager do?

en: Negotiate new pricing based on the revised estimations from the subcontractor that reflect the new work
Initiate a change request and review the contract to evaluate the payment options before responding
Deny the subcontractor's payment request, because the product does not comply with the project needs and close the project.
Initiate a change to incorporate an immediate payment milestone in the contract as per the subcontractor's request.

x.en: New standards were not included in the statement of work so the project manager should Initiate a change request to reflect the new standards and review the contract to evaluate the payment options before responding

q.en:
A project manager assigned to an education project needs to train a workforce in application development. The customer is responsible for providing the training center, and the deadline to start the first training is in 2 weeks. The customer calls to say that the center will not be available in 2 weeks due to some unforeseen problems.
What should the project manager do next?

en: Update the project schedule with the new date for training
Apply the terms and conditions of the contract with penalties
Issue a change request to reflect the anticipated date for training
Help the customer find an alternative location to start the training

x.en:
The customer is responsible for providing the training center and he calls to say that 
... 761192 bytes omitted ...
or this risk?

en: Because it is a high-priority risk.
Because this activity is on the critical path.
Because it is a financial risk
Because the response strategies should be assigned for all identified risks.

x.en: The impact is very high that will cancel the project if occurs and the probability is high, so the risk is a high priority risk and should be mitigated.

q.en: You are a risk manager of a new pipeline project. According to past experience, you selected DAN inc. is that the main supplier of critical materials that may not deliver on time. You have already accounted for this risk in the risk management plan. If this risk materializes, you plan to purchase the material from another supplier. A new risk in this plan is that there may be differences in the material provided by the two suppliers. What is the type of the new risk?

en: Residual risk.
Primary risk.
Secondary risk.
Procurement risk.

x.en:
The new risk is a secondary risk because it arises due to the implementation of a primary response “If this risk materializes, you plan to purchase the material from another supplier. A new risk in this plan is that there may be differences in the material provided by the two suppliers “

Risk responses, when implemented, can have potential effects on the objectives and as such, can generate additional risks. These are known as secondary risks and are analyzed and planned for in the same way as those risks that were initially identified. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page# 37.

en: Technical points.
Cost
Methodology performance
Schedule

x.en:
The probability and impact scales should reflect the stakeholder's risk tolerance. The project can’t delay and the time is critical, so the tolerance regarding time is very small (Averse). Therefore the most important point is the schedule.

The agreed-upon definitions of probabilities and impacts reflect stakeholders’ risk tolerances and thresholds.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. You are working on a critical path activity and notice a delay in product delivery due to an anticipated event. What should you do first?

en: Issue a change request.
Update the risk register.
Follow the risk response strategy.
Use the contingency reserve.

x.en: The delay(impact) is due to an identified risk (anticipated event). The risk was in the register and has already been analyzed and has a response plan. The project is in the execution so the risk response plan has already been implemented but failed or is not effective. The first action you should update the status of the risk and response then perform the fallback plan.

q.en: You are a project manager for the construction of a new Substation project. You have scheduled the fourth workshop for qualitative risk analysis. One of the team members complains that the risk analysis should be done only one time in the early stage of the project. What should you do to handle this situation?

en: Continue with the workshop, but discipline the team member because he is against your decision.
Continue with the meeting, but remove the team member from the participant's list.
Yes, the team member is right because the risk analysis is in the planning stage only.
Explain to the team member that the perform qualitative analysis should be performed throughout the life of the project.

x.en: Performing Iterative Qualitative Risk Analysis is a key success factor of this process. The success of qualitative risk analysis is enhanced if the process is used periodically throughout the project. The reference is the standard for risk management in portfolios, programs, and projects page#34.

q.en: A project manager of a new power plant project. After identifying risks, he starts the qualitative risk analysis process, and now he is prioritizing them. Which of the following tools/techniques is he using now?

en: Monte Carlo.
Status meeting.
Brainstorming.
Probability and impact matrix.

x.en: He is in the qualitative risk analysis process prioritizing the risks using the probability and impact matrix.

q.en: A petrochemical organization starts a new project with a high budget. The organization pursues high margins on investments and has an aggressive growth plan. The company has a central project management office to support and assist the new projects and record information on the past project's performance. The executive managers regularly request comprehensive reports. The project manager has a very good experience in project management and risk management. The PMO regularly requires full documentation of the project management plans and in particular risk management. Within the above context, what is the risk management strategy of this project?

en: The stakeholders' risk appetite is low, leverage historical information, define standard metrics and reports, and create a formal risk management plan.
The stakeholders' risk appetite is high, leverage historical information, define standard metrics and reports, and create a formal risk management plan.
The stakeholders' risk appetite is high, leverage historical information, use informal metrics and reports, and use an informal risk management plan.
The stakeholders' risk appetite is low, leverage historical information, use informal metrics and reports, and use an informal risk management plan.

x.en:
It’s clear that the organization has an aggressive plan to achieve high margins, so it’s willing to take a high degree of risk ( high appetite). The PMO is the central follow up all the projects, so the reports and metrics should be in specific formats (standard formats). The PMO records the data from the past projects to support and assist the new projects, so the project leverages the historical information.

A project management office (PMO) is a management structure that standardizes the project-related governance processes and facilitates the sharing of resources, methodologies, tools, and techniques.

q.en:
The project has reached the final development stage, the test leader informs the risk manager that one of the key characteristics may not be testable due to changes in the environment.

What should the risk manager do?

en: Review the property with the project team.
Ensure that risk triggers are still valid
Request engineers to set acceptance criteria.
Escalation of the problem to the project board of directors.

x.en: Request engineers to set acceptance criteria , Review the property with the project team and Escalation of the problem to the project board of directors. are the responsibility of the project manager. So the correct answer is “Ensure that risk triggers are still valid”.

en: Holding weekly risk management meetings with all concerned.
Adopting agile methods of risk management
Adopting a predictive approach to risk management.
Use appropriate documentation to help manage risk.

x.en: High-variability environments, by definition, incur more uncertainty and risk. To address this, projects managed using adaptive approaches make use of frequent reviews of incremental work products and cross-functional project teams to accelerate knowledge sharing and ensure that risk is understood and managed. Risk is considered when selecting the content of each iteration, and risks will also be identified, analyzed, and managed during each iteration. Additionally, the requirements are kept as a living document that is updated regularly, and work may be reprioritized as the project progresses, based on an improved understanding of current risk exposure. Pmbok6 page#94 agile section.

q.en: ALFA is a Mega Organization working in Construction. You are the Project manager of the XSE project. You and the risk manager in the meeting are discussing the quantitative risk analysis tools and techniques. The Monte Carlo simulation technique is one of the techniques used in this process. Using the below graph, what is the probability of the project completion at the “H” point?

x.en: From the graph take the probability besides the H point = 80%.

q.en: Which of the following are regulatory requirements when evaluating the project environment for risk threats/opportunities?

en: Portfolio information and the acquisition system.
Project information.
Organizational policies, processes, standards, and procedures.
Organizational channels requirements.

x.en: Organizational standard policies, processes, and procedures are legal and regulatory requirements.

q.en: You are a risk manager recording the causes and effects of risks in the risk register but need to ensure the risk is adequately described. Which one of the following is critical for the risk manager to consider when describing the causes?

en: Each cause should be approved by the executive manager.
Each cause should represent actual conditions.
Each cause has a risk manager.
Each cause has a degree of uncertainty.

x.en: It is important to distinguish risks from risk-related features. Causes are events or circumstances that currently exist or are certain to exist in the future, which might give rise to risks. Effects are conditional future events or conditions that directly affect one or more objectives if the associated risk occurs. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page#11.

q.en: You are a project manager of a new project. You are discussing with the project management office PMO the implementation of risk audits in the project. What is the purpose of a risk audit?

en: Allows considering the effectiveness of the risk management response strategy.
Allows validating the existence of a risk management plan.
Allows verifying the project management plan.
Allows considering the effectiveness of the entire risk management process.

x.en: The risk audits examine and document the effectiveness of risk responses in dealing with identified risks and their root causes, as well as the effectiveness of the risk management process.

q.en: You are a project manager of a construction project. During the execution, you have received reports from a supplier that he is over capacity, which may delay the delivery. What should you update next?

en: Issue log
Cost baseline.
OPA
Risk register

x.en: You should identify this risk, record it in the risk register, perform an analysis to assess the impact of this delay on the project objectives, and assign a risk response plan.

q.en: You are a project manager of a pipeline project. You and the project team have identified a risk with a high probability of occurrence and a high-cost impact on the project. The customer decides that the requirements surrounding the risk should be removed from the project. The removal of the requirements does affect the project scope, but it can release the project from high-risk exposure. What risk response has been taken in this project?

en: Accept
Exploit
Mitigate
Avoidance

x.en: Risk avoidance is when the portfolio, program, or project team acts to eliminate a threat or protect activity from risk impact. It may be appropriate for a high-priority threat with a high probability of occurrence and a large negative impact. Avoidance may involve changing some aspect of the management plan or changing the objective that is in jeopardy in order to eliminate the threat impact entirely. Should the risk materialize, it would have no effect with respect to the objective. The risk owner may also take action to isolate the objective from the risk's impact if it were to occur. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, page 36

q.en: You heard your team members discussing a chosen mental disposition towards uncertainty, adopted explicitly or implicitly by individuals and groups, driven by perception, and evidenced by observable behavior and about an uncertain event or condition that, if it occurs, has a positive or negative effect on a project’s objectives. What are your team members discussing?

en: Risk Tolerance/Event.
Risk attitude /Risk.
Risk Tolerance/risk-averse.
Risk Tolerance/risk.

x.en:
Definition of attitude :mental disposition towards uncertainty, adopted explicitly or implicitly by individuals and groups, driven by perception, and evidenced by observable behavio .
Definition of risk :an uncertain event or condition that, if it occurs, has a positive or negative effect on a project’s objectives .

Reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#8.

q.en: You are a risk manager for the construction of a new hospital. You want to determine what is to be measured, how it is to be measured, and what project outcomes are to be measured. In which processes group should the above be established?

en: closing
Initiating
Monitoring and controlling.
Planning

x.en: What is to be measured, how it is to be measured, and what project outcomes are to be measured” are documented in the project management plan and the subsidiary plans during the planning process.

q.en: Kelly is a project manager of a telecommunications project. She wants an appropriate channel for risk response assistance, risk visibility, and escalation support. Which of the following is the correct choice?

en: Project governance board.
Project management office.
Change the control board.
Program management office.

x.en: The project management office PMO provides support, assistance, templates, and training for the project.

q.en: Which of the following indicates that the organization has a successful risk management process?

en: The high-risk Projects are given additional time.
Accelerate the project with additional resources.
The profitability of the organization has increased due to the risk management process.
The number of identified and unidentified risks increased.

x.en: An effective and successful risk management process will improve the effectiveness of the project and increase the chance of success. Due to this, the profitability will be increased.

q.en: During the execution of your project, a risk remains after implementing a risk response plan, how can you deal with the remaining risk?

en: Analyzed and planned for in the same way as those risks which were initially identified.
Workaround
Analyze this risk and update the risk register.
Fallback plan.

x.en: The residual risk should be clearly identified, analyzed, documented, and communicated to all relevant stakeholders. The reference is the standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects, Page#37.

q.en: One of the important outputs of the control risk process is the project document updates. Due to that, the risk register will be updated by the outcomes of.....

en: Profile analysis and stakeholders' risk attitude.
Risk analysis and risk reserve analysis.
Risk Reassessments and risk audits.
Risk reviews and risk register analysis.
