q.en: After identifying the risks by the risk manager and the project team members, the risk manager wants to engage the whole project team in prioritizing the identified risk but the project manager refuses the engagement of the whole project team due to resource concerns . As a risk manager , what should you do?

en: Ask the functional manager to replace the project manager with another helpful
Convince the project manager of the importance of the whole project team's engagement in all risk processes
Engage the project team in the risk prioritization process and then discuss lessons learned with the project manager after finishing the process
Follow the project manager's instructions , as the project manager is responsible

x.en: The best option (Convince the project manager of the importance of the whole project team's engagement in all risk processes)

q.en: A project manager has received an email from a key stakeholder illustrating that the project is small and a risk management plan is not needed and lack of a plan will reduce costs . As a project manager , what should you do ?

en: Advise the stakeholder that risk management must be applied to all projects as it is valuable
Assess the impact of removing the risk management processes from the project
Remove the stakeholder from the stakeholder register and inform the sponsor
Cancel the risk management as the project is small

x.en: The best Option (Advise the stakeholder that risk management must be applied to all projects as it is valuable)

q.en: The general manager of the organization wants to reduce some of risk management activities . What step did the risk manager fail to perform?

en: Preventing all issues from occurring
Properly communicating the risk management activities and their outcomes
Explaining the purpose of the management and contingency reserves
Identify all risks and assigning the CEO as a risk owner

x.en: The risk manager should Properly communicating the risk management activities and their outcomes to avoid this situation.

q.en: What technique can be used to justify risk response decisions taken on a high -risk project?

en: prompt lists
Interviews
Decision tree analysis
Nominal group technique

x.en: Decision tree analysis is used to determine partial and global probabilities of occurrence ,  justify risk response decisions taken on a high -risk project.

q.en: Rick has just been assigned as the project manager of a project to construct a football stadium. During a planning meeting , the team decides to conduct a site survey to determine the ground conditions before engineering the design. Which of the following risk management processes is the team implementing?

en: Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis process
Identify Risk Process
Plan Risk process
Plan Risk Management process

x.en: The project team is implementing the Identify Risk Process to identify the risks that may impact the project before engineering the design.

q.en: One of the project risks is likely to cause a negative impact of $15,000 with a probability of 50%. At the same time, there is a possibility of saving 10000$ by choosing alternate resources, this has a likelihood of 25% . What is the EMV of the project?

A project manager is working on a project for which some requirements have not been clearly defined. The customer insists that this should not be considered a problem and that the project should continue without delay. What should the project manager do?

en: Log the risk in the risk register
Meet with the team to discuss the concerns
Speak with the customer to avoid the risk
Accept the risk and start project work

x.en: Some requirements have not been clearly defined , it's a risk and the project manager should log the risk in the risk register then analyse the impact on project objectives.

q.en: A project manager is working with his project team to prioritize the identified risks within the project. He and the team are prioritizing risks for further analysis or action by assessing and combining the risks probability of occurrence and impact. What process is the project manager completing?

en: Perform quantitative analysis
Risk Breakdown Structure creation
Risk Identification
Perform qualitative analysis

x.en:
Keyword( prioritizing risks for further analysis)
Perform Qualitative Risk Analysis is the process of prioritizing risks for further analysis or action by assessing and combining their probability of occurrence and impact.

q.en: Which tool can the project risk manager utilize to help identify and assess project risks ?

en: Sensitivity Analysis
Interviews
Risk Surveys
Risk audit

x.en: Interviews are utilized to help identify and assess project risks. Interviews are information- gathering techniques used in identifying risks. Interviews used also in Risk probability and impact assessment during the perform qualitative risk analysis process also used in perform quantitative risk analysis process.

q.en: A heavy industrial design firm has over 3$ billion in current contract value. As a result of quantitative risk analysis of geographically separated project, opportunities have been identified and assessed as high priorities for the project. What is the most effective method to capture these opportunities?

en: Formally notify the project manager
Establish a contingency reserve
Integrate them into the RBS
Schedule a project team meeting

x.en: Contingency reserves are established to provide for the capture of opportunities that are judged to be priorities for the project.

q.en: At the completion of a small project, the risk manager performs a risk audit and finds that several identified risks had occurred, and the impact was significantly large than expected . While the project remained on schedule, the project budget increased by 50%. The project met all risk response milestonesand no additional previously unidentified risks, occurred on the project. Based on this information, what risk management process improvement should the risk manager recommend for future similar projects?

en: Revise the level of accuracy of probability and impact scores
Expand the use of risk identification techniques
Document the risk audit report and capture it in the lessons learned database
Increase the frequency of risk management meetings with the project manager.

x.en: Document the risk audit report and capture it in the lessons learned database

q.en: Which approach should be used when considering human factors to influence the risk management process for optimal effects at the group and indvidual levels ?

en: Proactive
Reactive
Agile
Ongoing

x.en:
Everyone is involved in the risk management process. Any actions or attitudes that hinder communication about risk reduce the effectiveness of risk management regarding proactive approaches and effective decision making. 

The standard for risk Management in Portfolios, Programs , and Projects Page,17.

q.en: A project managers assigns a risk owner during wich of the following processes ?

en: Plan risk management
Plan risk responses
Monitor Risk
Identify risks

x.en: All identified risks are recorded , and a risk owner may be identified at the same time. The risk owner is the individual responsible for monitoring the risk and for selecting and implementing ab appropriate risk response strategy. It is the responsibility of the risk owner to manage the corresponding risk throughout the subsequent risk management processes.

q.en: What quantitative risk analysis tool is used to support stakeholder decision -making for the project?

en: Probability and impact matrix
Risk probability and impact assessment
Interviewing
Sensitivity analysis

x.en: Sesitivity analysis : risk analysis tool used to support stakeholder decision -making for the project  because it helps to know the risks that have the highest potential impact on the project objectives.

q.en:
The project manager is implementing a computer interface to facilitate communication between two ticketing systems for two major companies in the IT industry.
During the plan risk response process, the project team agrees on the contingency plan that should mitigate the negative impact of the risk. However , during the project execution , one of the subjects mater experts identifies a residual risk that wasn't taken into consideration during the risk response planning session , but could potentially affect the project schedule baseline . What should the risk manager be to handle this residual risks?

en: Reject the risk, since the risk plan will take care of all risks.
Analyze this risk and update the risk register
Increase the management reserve
Accept the risk , since it is minor

x.en:
The residual risks that remain after the responses are implemented. These residual risks are clearly identified , analyzed , documented , and communicated to all relevant stakeholders untill they are satisfied.


The standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs , and Projects, Page 37.

q.en: During project execution, the project team realizes that the power outlet for imported equipment isn't compatible with the current customer's electrical infrastructure . The event wasn't orginally identified as a risk. To maintain the project schedule , the project manager decides to purchase a new power adapter . What type of response best describes this course of action?

en: Contingency plan
Workaround
Management plan
Full -back plan

x.en:
Keyword ( This event wasn't originally identified as a risk.)


The workaround is an action used when unidentified risks occurred. 

The project manager decides to purchase a new power adapter due to this unidentified risk when occurred.

q.en: During a status meeting, a functional manager complains that the server back up failed, impacting the department . This way a known risk documented in the risk register as an accepted risk. After reviewing the meeting minutes , it is determined that the functional manager hadn't participated in the risk planning phase. Which of the identification methods should have been applied?

en: Stakeholder analysis
Quantitative analysis
Qualitative analysis
Sensitivity analysis

x.en: Stakeholder analysis  helps to identify stakeholder relationships (with the project and with other stakeholders) that can be leveraged to build coalitions and potential partnerships to enhance the project's chance of success, along with stakeholder relationships that need to be influenced differently at different stages of the project or phase.

q.en: What should be used to determine how often a project's risk register should be updated or reviewed in a given year when the project is in an industry with a very high business rhythm?

en: The risk triggers
The Risk management plan
The risk prioritization criteria
The program management plan

x.en:
Keyword (how often)

The risk management plan defines both the normal frequency for repeating the processes in addition to specific or exceptional conditions under which the corresponding actions are initiated.

The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, Programs , and Projects Page, 30.

q.en: The project manager performed a variance analysis on the project during the execution phase. The variances were shown as increasing . What does this result imply?

en: The uncertainty and risk are increasing
The project is behind schedule
There is no potential for future deviation
The project is over budget.

x.en: The variances were shown as increasing which means that The uncertainty and risk are increasing .

q.en:
The project sponsor has a great deal invested in a project . The sponsor has scheduled a meeting with the project risk lead to find out more information on managing risks and opportunities . 

What are two actions the project risk lead should do to evaluate the project environment and the chances of managing them ?( Choose two)

en: Review the policies and practices that are outlined in the risk management plan
Review the scope of work to determine the prescribed project methodology
Review the contract and determine the resources and project funding
Schedule a meeting with the project team to determine next steps
Review corporate templates and check it they consider external and internal factors

x.en:
Two actions the project risk lead should do to evaluate the project environment and the chances of managing them.


- Schedule a meeting with the project team to determine next steps .


- Review the policies and practices that are outlined in the risk management plan

q.en:
A project manager works on a long-term and high-visibility project at an organizationa that has a low - risk appetite towards this project due to its impact on the company's business. 

The project sponsors follow up weekly with the project manager, who was just informed by one of the risk owners that the exposure from high impact risks are hitting the risk thresholds . 

What should the project manager do next?

en: Update the project management plan to add contingency
Complete an assessment and confirm the response with the sponsors
Implement mitigation measures for those risks
Perform an assumptions and constraints analysis

x.en: The organization has a low - risl appetite towards this project due to its imapct on thr company's business so the project manager should Complete an assessment and confirm the response with the sponsors .

q.en: The risk manager is facilitating risk planning activities with the team . The team is documenting all the checkpoints along the way that might indicate delays on critical deliverables. What is this an example of

en: Risk categories
Risk register
Risk triggers
Risk response

x.en: A risk trigger is a indicator that a risk is about to occur or has occurred. Triggers may be discovered during the risk identification process and monitored as the project is executed. Once the risk trigger occurs, the project team needs to implement a risk response.

q.en: A risk manager notices that a risk owner is facing challenges implementing their response strategy and the costs are significantly exceeding expectations. What is the first thing the risk manager should do ?

en: Conduct a cost -benefit analysis
Analyze the situation and meet with the risk owner
Highlight this situation to the project manager
Change the risk response strategy

x.en: Risk owner is facing challenges implementing their response strategy so the risk manager should analyze the situation and meet with the risk owner .

q.en: A project manager identified a risk of communication issues with the client which may impact the project schedule. A member of the sales team advises that this client prefers face-to-face conversations. What should the project manager do to avoid this risk?

en: Call the client and advise that online communication is easier and faster
Meet the client and plan for critical milestone meetings
Ask the salesperson to lead the communication with the client.
Record this risk and the client's preference in the risk register

x.en: The project manager should record this risk and the client's preference in the risk register to avoid this risk.

q.en: A project manager is assigned to a new project and is told they need to develop the project's risk register. When should the project manager identify the project risks?

en: Identify risks only at the project's midpoint for the stakeholders to review them.
Ensure project team members proactively identify risks throughout the project to plan for possible response strategies.
Identify risks at the beginning of the project because the risk posture will not change.
Delegate risk identification to each team member and have them record the risks on separate risk registers for their areas .

x.en: The project manager should ensure project team members proactively identify risks throughout the project to plan for possible response strategies to develop the project's risk register.

q.en: A project manager has been assigned to a project that is just starting. The organization has a very low -risk appetite towards this project due to constraints on budget and schedule. The project stakeholders are very engaged on the project and want to ensure that there is clear visibility on the project risks and progress. How should the project manager handle stakeholder expectations?

en: Discuss the risk response strategies with the stakeholders
Develop a communication plan to share updates on risks
Ensure the risk register includes all identified risks
Add buffers to the schedule to accommodate risk

x.en: The project manager should develop a communication plan to share updates on risks to ensure that there is clear visibility on the project risks and progress.

q.en: When should project risks be closed?

en: When the forecast activity date has been met or exceeded
When the risk has been realized and can no longer happen again
When iterative data analysis determines the risk is not applicable
When the stakeholders agree a risk is no longer applicable

x.en:
The risk should be closed when:

1. When the risk is considered successfully mitigated. 

2. When the risk becomes a problem and must be tracked as such. 

3. When risks becomes no longer relevant to the project.

4. When the risk has been realized and can no longer happen again.

en: Documenting the communication strategy for risks throughout the project.
Being able to monitor and control risks throughout the project.
Defining how risk management will be executed throughout the project.
Having the ability to identify risks throughout the project.

x.en:
Effective risk management requires the creation of a risk management plan. This plan describes how the risk management processes are to be carried out and how they fit in with other processes. On a broader level, the risk management plan describes the relationships among the risk management processes; general portfolio, program, or project management; and the management processes in the rest of the organization. Initial risk management planning
is carried out early in the overall planning of the work, and the corresponding activities are integrated into the overall
management plan. The risk management plan may need to be adapted as the needs of the work and stakeholders
become clearer or change.
The feasibility of risk management planning is dependent upon the features of the organization in which it is
carried out. The rules and guidelines defined in the risk management plan reflect (a) the culture of the organization,
(b) its capabilities regarding people and facilities, and (c) its values, goals, and objectives. The risk management plan
identifies and describes relevant organizational procedures and any other enterprise environmental factors that apply,
such as strategic risk management, enterprise risk management (ERM), and corporate governance processe.

TheStandardForRiskMgmt , Page 30.

q.en: A project manager has determined that an activity is too complex to complete internally, so they hire a licensed contractor to complete the work. What is the project manager performing in this situation?

en: Risk transfer
Risk acceptance
Risk avoidance
Risk mitigation

x.en:
Keyword (hire a licensed contractor)
Risk transfer involves shifting the responsibility of a threat to a third party to manage the risk and to bear the impact if the threat occurs.

The Standard for Risk management in Portfolios , Programs , and Projects , Page 36.

q.en: Project stakeholders can often be risk - averse with little to no knowledge of the risk process. How should a risk manager increase stakeholder risk appetite ?

en: Develop a generous probabilistic cash flow model
Explain risk handling and mitigation strategies
Increase the impact of all risks in the risk breakdown structure (RBS)
Exclude risk averse stakeholders from future risk discussions

x.en: The project manager should  explain risk handling and mitigation strategies to increase stakeholder risk appetite.

q.en: A project that was in the execution phase for the last six months was put on hold and was eventually cancelled after numerous scope-related challenges . It was decided to re-plan the scope and divide the project into multiple projects to have better insight into end objectives. As part of the project srart-up, the project manager is developing the risk planning for the project. What three artifacts should the project manager consult or review during this process? (choose three)

en: Code of regulations
Risk register
Risk management plan
Lessons learned registers from analogous projects
Project contracts

x.en:
The three artifacts should the project manager consult or review during plan risk management 

. Code of regulations 

. Lessons learned registers from analogous projects 

. Project contracts

q.en: The project sponsor asks the project manager about the accuracy of the project data. The project manager realizes that some risks have not been updated recently. What should the project manager do first regarding those risks?

en: Conduct a checklist analysis on each risk
Review the risk register to check for the new risks
Perform an assumptions analysis for those risks
Create a risk response plan for those risks

x.en: The project manager realizes that some risks have not been updated recently so the project manager should Review the risk register to check for the new risks .

q.en: Virginia is the project manager for her organization. She has hired a subject matter expert to interview the project stakeholders on certain identified risks within the project. The subject matter expert will assess the risk event with what specific goal in mind:

en: To determine the level of probability and impact for each risk event
To determine the probability and cost of the risk event
To determine the bias of the risk event based on each person interviewed
To determine the validity of each risk event

x.en: Expert judgment is required to assess the probability and impact of each risk to determine its location in the matrix. Experts generally are those having experience with similar, recent projects , Gathering expert judgment is often accomplished with the use of risk facilitation workshops or interviews.

q.en: A project manager is creating a risk response plan. However , every time a risk response is suggested, another risk is identified that is caused by the response . Which of the following is the BEST thing for the project manager to do?

en: Spend more time making sure the risk responses are clearly defined.
Get more people involved in the identify risk process since risks have been missed
Document the new risks and continue the plan risk responses process .
Make sure the project work is better understood

x.en: Since not all risks can be identified at any given point in the project, it is essential that risk identification is repeated throughout the project life cycle.

q.en: What best describes the job of a risk owner

en: Creating a detailed description of risk
Responsible and accountable for the risk management plan
Actively involved in the identification of new risks
Responsible and accountable for managing risks.

x.en:
The risk owner is the individual responsible for monitoring the risk and for selecting and implementing an appropriate risk response strategy. It is the responsibility of the risk owner to manage the corresponding risk throughout the subsequent risk management processes.
A risk owner is accountable for each risk,

Standards of risk management portfolio, program and project page 32

q.en: A project manager is hired as a consultant by the executive sponsor to manage a major change program that has experienced two past failures. The current executive sponsor believes the project is in good shape based on feedback from the last project manager and reports this to senior executive management. The executive sponsor believes there were no major risks threatening the time, budget or quality of the project. In the first week of risk analysis , the project manager concludes the project timeline is unrealistic and is three months behind schedule. The organization's risk appetite is low. What is the first step that should be taken?

en: Immediately call a steering committee meeting , report the project status , and suggest project scope reductions to save time .
Review the project schedule and recommend fast tracking the schedule and / or crashing the critical path.
Update existing risk response plans and include more resources to get the project back on track.
Discuss the projects schedule with the executive sponsor and agree on a strategy for updating the risk management plan and risk response plans.

x.en: The executive sponsor believes there were no major risks threatening the time, budget or quality of the project. In the first week of risk analysis , the project manager concludes the project timeline is unrealistic and is three months behind schedule. The organization's risk appetite is low. so, the project manager is the first step that should be taken " discuss the projects schedule with the executive sponsor and agree on a strategy for updating the risk management plan and risk response plans".

q.en: During project execution, the project team realizes that the power outlet for imported equipment is not compatible with the current customer's electrical infrastructure . This event was originally identified as a risk during earlier stages of the project and the associated risk response indicated a plan to purchase a new power adapter . Which project fund will be used to cover this cost?

en: Management budget
Contingency reserve
Management reserve
Project budget

x.en: Keyword ( This event was orginally identified as a risk) so the correct answer is Contingency reserve to fund the identified risk.

q.en: The risk management process should be"

en: Iterative throughout the planning phase
Iterative throughout the entire project
Updated throughout the entire project
Updated in the execution phase

x.en:
The emergent nature of risk requires the risk management process ti be iterative , repeating the risk identification activities in order to find risks that were not previously evident.

The standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects , Page 52.

q.en: During the identification risk process, the project manager identifies four risks. What is the estimated monetary value of the cost for this project?

A project manager needs a method to create a quick and simple approach to risk identification to communicate the project risk with the stakeholders . Which one of the following approaches to risk identification should the project manager choose to provide a quick and simple listing of the project risks?

en: Assumptions analysis
Delphi Technique
Brainstorming
Checklist analysis

x.en:
Risk identification checklists can be developed based on historical information and knowledge that has been accumulated from previous, similar portfolios, programs, or projects and from other sources of information. The lowest level of a risk breakdown structure can also be used as a risk checklis while a checklist can be quick and simple, it is impossible to build an exhaustive one. 

The standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs , and Projects , Page 131,132

q.en:
Henry is the project manager of the KHG project for his company. The project team reported that they hace found a way to complete the project work for less cost than what was originally planned. The project team presents a new software that will help to automate the project work. While the software and the associated training costs 25,000$ it will save the project nearly 65,000$ in total costs . Henry agrees to the software and changes to the project management plan accordingly.
What type of risk response has been used in this instance

en: Accepting
Avoidance
Exploiting
Enhancing

x.en:
The exploit strategy may be selected for high-priority opportunities where the organization wants to ensure that the opportunity is realized. This strategy seeks to capture the benefit associated with a particular opportunity by ensuring that it definitely happens, increasing the probability of occurrence to 100%.

The standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs , and Projects , Page 36

q.en: The risk manager organizes a stakeholder meeting to obtain agreement on project risk response strategies. At the conclusion of this meeting, the risk response strategies should be which of the following?

en: Scheduled, budgeted, and easy for project stakeholders to understand
Iterative, scaled to the project, and addressing threats and opportunities
Timely, cost-effective, agreed-upon, and accepted
Cost-effective, validated by Monte Carlo analysis, and assigned

x.en: The purpose of responding and treating risks is to minimize or eliminate the potential impact the risk may pose to the achievement of set objectives . Risk response is concerned with developing strategies to reduce or eliminate the threats and events that create risks or enhance opportunities

q.en: A new resource is added to the project team from a matrix organization. How should the project's risk manager familiarize the new team member with the project's risk management process?

en: Provide the new team member with a copy of the risk register and latest status report.
Send the new team member the risk management plan to read.
The functional manager is responsible for providing the training.
Provide project specific risk training and mentor through the risk process.

x.en: The best option "Send the new team member the risk management plan to read."

q.en: The stakeholder is unwilling to make decisions that would result in negative consequences to the project. Which of the following describes the stakeholder's attitude regarding project risks?

en: Not enough information available to describe the stakeholder's risk attitude
Risk neutral
Risk accepting
Risk averse

x.en: Keyword (unwilling) so the stakeholder's attitude regarding project risks "Risk averse"

q.en:
A project manager is running a high-cost telecommunications project. There is a monthly status meeting, and the risk manager should provide an update to the project team and project sponsors on major risks.
What risk related information should be included in the monthly status meeting of this complex project?

en: Top priority risks at present, risks that have occurred, risk management plan
Top priority risks at present, risks closed in the last period, milestone changes
Top priority risks at present, risks that have occurred, changes in scope
Top priority risks at present, risks that have occurred, risks closed in the last period

x.en:
Agenda items should cover the following:
1-Top priority risks at present (Are there any changes?).
2-Risks or trigger conditions that have occurred (What is the status of the actions?).
3-Risks responded to in the last period (Effectiveness of actions taken, Are there any additional actions required?).
4-Risks closed in the last period (Impact on the plans). 

5-Lessons to be added to the Organizational Process Assets.

The reference is risk practice standard Page #104&105

q.en: An issue that had not been registered as a risk appeared. This issue may have a big impact on the project. What should the project manager do?

en: Hold a meeting with the project team and relevant stakeholders to agree on the best way to manage the issues.
Inform the sponsor that the issue is addressed
Avoid managing the issue as it was not registered as a risk for the project
Delay the project until the issue is addressed

x.en:
When an unregistered issue arises that could significantly impact the project, it is crucial for the project manager to gather insights and perspectives from the project team and relevant stakeholders. This collaborative approach allows for:

1. Understanding the Issue: The project team can provide valuable input on the nature and implications of the issue.
2. Identifying Solutions: Stakeholders can contribute different viewpoints on how to address the issue effectively.
3. Taking Timely Action: A meeting helps ensure that the issue is addressed promptly, thereby minimizing its potential impact on the project’s timeline and objectives.

q.en: Your company was awarded a contract that includes a 10% bonus payment if the project is completed two months early. You consider several options to exploit this opportunity. What is the best course of action for you to increase the chances of receiving the bonus?

en: Crash the schedule
Purchase insurance
Resource leveling
Reduce project scope

x.en: Crashing a project involves allocating additional resources or working longer hours to complete project tasks in a shorter timeframe. This strategy directly targets the schedule by shortening the duration of critical path activities, potentially enabling the project to finish early.

q.en: You have just started a project. Some of the risks that you are anticipating for this project might have surfaced in previous projects. Which of the following would you review to see how these risks and issues were handled?

en: Lesson learned register
Project management Plan
Policies and procedures
Lessons learned repository

x.en: A lessons learned repository is a comprehensive archive that includes documented experiences from past projects, detailing what went well, what didn’t, and how various risks and issues were managed. This information is invaluable for understanding how to approach similar risks in your current project.

q.en: What are the key differences between risks, issues, and triggers?

en: Issue is a fact, risk is an uncertain event, and a trigger is what we should do when the contingency plan doesn’t work.
Risk is a fact, issue is an uncertain event, and a trigger is a risk that appears as a result of implementing a risk response
Risk is a fact, issue is an uncertain event, and a trigger is what we should do when a risk happens.
Issue is a fact, risk is an uncertain event, and a trigger is an early warning sign that a risk is about to occur.

x.en:
Risk: An uncertain event that might happen in the future and can impact the project positively or negatively.
	➤ Example: There’s a 30% chance a key supplier may delay delivery.
	
	
	Issue: A current situation or problem that has already occurred and needs to be addressed.
	➤ Example: A team member is sick and has already missed two days of work.
	
	
	Trigger: A warning sign or indicator that a risk is about to happen.
	➤ Example: The supplier misses the first checkpoint — this may trigger the risk of full delivery delay.

q.en: A risk is identified early in the project. After six months, it is determined that the risk does not apply to this particular project. How should the risk be handled by the risk manager?

en: Conduct a risk analysis to determine how an inappropriate risk was formally accepted.
Remove the risk from the risk register and inform the project manager that it’s no longer valid.
Ignore the risk and concentrate only on the pertinent risks.
Close the risk during the next risk board meeting and keep it in the risk register.

x.en:
Very Important Question in Real Exam 

When a risk is determined to no longer apply to the project, it should not be deleted but formally closed. 

The closure of risks is a part of the "Monitor Risks" process. Closing the risk during the risk board meeting ensures that there is formal documentation, appropriate communication with stakeholders, and that the record remains available for organizational learning, audits, or lessons learned activities in the future.

q.en:
The risk register is developed during the initial phases of a virtualized desktop deployment. The register is reviewed by peers, responses are planned, reviewed again, and risks are prioritized. After project completion the risk register is reviewed as a part of the formal lessons learned process. During the review, it’s realized that the risk register wasn’t updated, and many responses were not executed during the deployment. 

Which of the following options should have been performed during the execution of the project?

en: Risk monitoring and control process
Risk identification
Risk management process
Response planning

x.en:
Very Important Question in Real Exam

The Risk Monitoring and Control process is responsible for ensuring that risks are actively tracked, responses are implemented, and the register is regularly updated to reflect current status. It involves continuous oversight during execution. The failure to update the register and execute responses indicates that this process was not properly applied during the project execution phase.

q.en: The expected monetary value of a project is above US$1 million. The risk manager is concerned about this situation, and decides to review the related plans and processes to evaluate the degree of variation from the baseline. Next, the risk manager needs to document the results of such an analysis. What is the best document for the project manager to reference to find out where the results of such analysis should be documented?

en: Communication management plan
Risk management
Issue log
Lessons learned

x.en:
The Communication Management Plan serves as the authoritative guide for documenting and distributing project information. When analysis is performed (such as expected monetary value analysis), the plan specifies where these results should be documented, who should receive the information, how frequently updates are communicated, and in what format.

q.en: A risk manager works with the project team, senior management team, subject matter experts and other stakeholders to identify the project risks. Which of the following tools/methods from the risk management plan can be used to identify a risk, which is based on project objectives by category?

en: Decision tree analysis
Affinity diagram
Risk breakdown structure
Work breakdown structure.

x.en:
The Risk Breakdown Structure (RBS) allows the risk manager to systematically identify risks by categorizing them according to project objectives and sources. This hierarchical structure provides a comprehensive view of where risks may arise and supports efficient risk identification during brainstorming and team discussions.

q.en: During project execution, the project team realizes that the power outlet for imported equipment isn’t compatible with the current customer’s electrical infrastructure. This event wasn’t originally identified as a risk. To maintain the project schedule, the project manager decides to purchase a new power adapter. What type of response best describes this course of action?

en: Workaround
Full-back plan
Management plan
Contingency plan

x.en:
Workarounds are reactive responses to issues that were not anticipated or identified during planning. They are implemented to resolve unexpected problems quickly to avoid project delays or impacts. The decision to purchase a new adapter after discovering the incompatibility is a textbook example of a workaround.

q.en: A budget change request was initiated by a functional manager in an organization due to a shortage in the functional manager's department budget. The functional manager asks the CEO to approve utilization of a contingency budget reserved for one of the projects in its closing phase. What should the risk manager of the related project have done to prevent this situation from happening?

en: Performed the risk monitoring and closing process properly
Created the project work plan and budget more accurately
Communicated better with the organization’s CEO
Educated the project team on budget change requests

x.en:
At the project closing phase, it is the responsibility of the risk manager to ensure that all contingency reserves have been properly monitored, utilized if necessary, or released if no longer required. Failure to properly close unused contingency reserves leaves them vulnerable to misuse for unrelated organizational needs.

In this scenario, because risk monitoring and closing processes were not properly performed, the contingency budget was still available and subsequently used by another department to cover a budget shortage. If the risk manager had executed the Risk Monitoring and Closing Processes correctly, this situation could have been prevented.

This highlights the critical importance of integrating disciplined Risk Monitoring (Monitor Risks) and Project Closure (Close Project or Phase) processes to ensure that all reserved risk funds are either utilized appropriately or formally closed when no longer needed.


	
	The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019):

	
		
		Section 4.8 Monitor Risks — Page 40
		
		
		Section 4.7 Implement Risk Responses — Page 38-39
		
		
		Appendix X6.7 — Risk Closure — Page 148【7】
		
	
	
	
	PMBOK Guide 6th Edition:

	
		
		Section 11.7 Monitor Risks
		
		
		Section 4.6 Close Project or Phase

q.en: If the contingency reserves are depleted before the project is completed. What recommendations could be implemented to prevent this from recurring?

en: Increase the cost and schedule baseline
Increase the contingency reserve
Implement a reserve analysis process
Use the Monte Carlo simulation

x.en:
Reserve analysis is a periodic assessment process used to monitor whether the contingency and management reserves remain adequate as project risks and conditions evolve. This analysis tracks reserve consumption trends and allows project managers to make adjustments before reserves are exhausted. It proactively prevents unexpected depletion by continuously reassessing the confidence level of remaining reserves.


	
	The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019):

	
		
		Section X6.7 Monitor Risks — Page 147
		
		
		Section 4.8 Monitor Risks — Page 40
		
		
		Reserve Analysis Tool — Appendix X6.7【7】
		
	
	
	
	PMBOK Guide 6th Edition:

	
		
		Section 11.7 Monitor Risks
		
		
		Tool & Technique: Reserve Analysis

q.en: You are managing a new project for a risk-seeking organization. Your project has an overall risk that exceeds the risk levels documented in the risk management plan. What is the best course of action for the organization to take with the project based on its current scope?

en: Perform a Monte Carlo simulation to understand possible risk outcomes
Monitor ongoing risks closely for any major changes
Cancel the project, as the overall level of risk remains unacceptable
Perform a reserve analysis to validate the remaining reserves

x.en:
Even in a risk-seeking organization, the risk management plan defines the upper limits of acceptable risk. If the project’s overall risk surpasses these thresholds and no viable risk responses can bring it within acceptable boundaries, the best course of action is to terminate the project to prevent exposing the organization to uncontrolled and unacceptable levels of risk.


	
	The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019):

	
		
		Section 2.1.5 Risk Appetite — Page 9
		
		
		Section 2.1.6 Risk Threshold — Page 10
		
		
		Section 4.7 Implement Risk Responses — Page 38【7】
		
	
	
	
	PMBOK Guide 6th Edition:

	
		
		Section 11.5 Plan Risk Responses
		
		
		Section 11.7 Monitor Risks

q.en: Which of the following represents the main goals of the Risk audit?

en: Examine the effectiveness of project team members and take the required actions
Document and assess the newly identified risks and take the required actions
Assess the risks that have occurred and take the required actions
Document what went well and not so well with the risk management process, and recommend action to improve

x.en:
A risk audit is part of the risk monitoring activities that focuses on reviewing the effectiveness of the overall risk management process. The audit evaluates what aspects of the process worked effectively and which did not, and recommends specific actions for improvement. The purpose is not to respond to risks directly but to strengthen the system managing those risks.

 


	
	The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019):

	
		
		Section 4.8 Monitor Risks — Page 40-41
		
		
		Risk Audit as part of Monitoring Processes【7】
		
	
	
	
	PMBOK Guide 6th Edition:

	
		
		Section 11.7 Monitor Risks — Risk Audit

q.en:
In a large enablement project with strict timelines, risks need to be closely monitored. The risk manager publishes reports comparing planned enablement sessions with actual enablement sessions, which help identify potential risks.
Which technique is the risk manager using?

en: Reserve analysis
Residual impact analysis
Variance analysis
Sensitivity analysis

x.en:
Variance analysis is a quantitative risk management technique used to compare actual project performance with planned expectations. In high-stakes projects with tight schedules, identifying variances helps the project team recognize deviations early and take corrective action. In this scenario, comparing planned vs. actual enablement sessions is a clear application of variance analysis.


	
	The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019):

	
		
		Section 4.8 Monitor Risks — Page 40-41
		
		
		Variance Analysis as a tool for identifying deviation【7】
		
	
	
	
	PMBOK Guide 6th Edition:

	
		
		Section 11.7 Monitor Risks — Variance Analysis

q.en:
During project execution, a project manager invites the stakeholders to a risk review meeting. During this meeting, a vendor highlights that the mitigation plan for a schedule risk has generated an additional risk.
🔹 Which technique should the risk manager use first?

en: Passively accept the new risk
Add the new risk to the watch list
Update the new risk in the risk register
Plan responses for the new risk

x.en:
Very important question in real exam:

When a new risk arises—especially as a side effect of implementing another risk response—the first step is to record that risk formally in the risk register.

The risk register is a central document that captures all identified risks and their associated data: description, source, status, owner, response strategy, etc.
Before planning a response or ignoring a risk, it must be acknowledged and analyzed.

 PMI emphasizes documentation first — before analysis or action.
 


	
	📖 The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019)

	
		
		Section 4.3 Identify Risks – Page 32
		
		
		Section 4.8 Monitor Risks – Page 40
		
		
		Risk register as the central control document
		
	
	
	
	📖 PMBOK Guide 6th Edition

	
		
		Section 11.2 Identify Risks
		
		
		Outputs: Risk Register

en: Risk Impact Matrix
Contingency reserves
Schedule and resource assumptions
Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

x.en:
🔵 Very Important question in Real Exam
When performance indicators such as CPI and SPI consistently underperform, the underlying cause is often flawed or unrealistic assumptions regarding schedule durations or resource availability.

✅ The correct project artifact to analyze is Schedule and Resource Assumptions, as it helps identify:


	
	Misaligned estimates
	
	
	Over-optimistic task durations
	
	
	Resource shortages
	


By analyzing and updating these assumptions, the risk manager can take corrective actions and prevent further delays or cost overruns.

(References):

🔷

		Section 11.2.2.2 – Assumption and Constraint Analysis
		
		
		Section 6.1.3 – Schedule Management Plan
		
		
		Section 7.1.3 – Resource Management Plan
		
	
	
	
	The Standard for Risk Management in Portfolios, Programs, and Projects (PMI, 2019):

	
		
		Section 4.3 Identify Risks – Page 32
		
		
		Focus on assumption analysis during risk identification and root cause evaluation【7】

q.en: Your organization's PMO is periodically asking for project artifacts from all projects and checking whether corporate standards of project management are being adhered to or not. They are also supportive in providing templates and guidelines related to project management when asked. Which type of PMO are we referring

en: Supporting PMO
Directing PMO
Controlling PMO
Governing PMO

x.en: In this scenario The PMO is assisting with templates and guidelines like a suportive PMO + checking whether corporate standards ,so they are playing the bigger role of a controlling PMO here .

q.en:
You are the risk manager for a project that is in the final development stage.
The test lead informs you that a key feature may not be testable due to recent changes in the environment.

What should you do first?

en: Review the feature with the project team
Report the issue to the project board
Request the architect to develop acceptance criteria
Examine whether the risk triggers are still valid

x.en:
When the test lead reports that a key feature may not be testable, this represents a potential new risk or a change in an existing risk caused by environmental changes.

As a risk manager, your first responsibility is to understand the situation before taking action. Reviewing the feature with the project team helps you to:


	
	Identify the root cause of the testability issue
	
	
	Assess the impact on project objectives (quality, schedule, scope, cost)
	
	
	Determine whether this is a new risk or a change to an existing one
	
	
	Explore possible response options or alternatives
	


Only after this analysis can you:


	
	Update the risk register
	
	
	Adjust the risk response plan
	
	
	Decide whether escalation is necessary

q.en:
You are a professional risk manager working for a company in the mining industry that encourages high levels of innovation and operates under frequently changing work conditions.

As a result, the organization finds it difficult to predict long-term business plans.

How should you manage risks in this situation?

en: Use a predictive approach to manage the risks
Carry out weekly risk management meetings with all stakeholders
Adopt agile approaches to manage the risks
Use proper documentation to help manage the risks

x.en:
📌 Exam Tip:
When the question highlights uncertainty, innovation, or frequent change, the best answer is usually Agile or Adaptive risk management.

In environments characterized by high uncertainty, rapid innovation, and frequent changes, such as the mining industry described, predictive and long-term planning approaches become ineffective.

Agile risk management is more suitable because it:


	
	Embraces change and uncertainty
	
	
	Allows for frequent reassessment of risks
	
	
	Supports iterative planning and short feedback loops
	
	
	Enables quick responses and adjustments as conditions evolve
	


Rather than relying on fixed plans, agile approaches continuously identify, analyze, and respond to risks as new information becomes available.

q.en:
A major project has an identified primary risk with a planned response in place.
Further analysis shows a high likelihood of a secondary risk, which is accepted in accordance with the organization’s risk tolerance levels and recorded in the risk register.

During project execution:


	
	The primary risk occurs
	
	
	The planned response is implemented
	
	
	The secondary risk also materializes
	


Which two actions should the risk owner take in this situation? (Choose two.)

en: Implement the response for the secondary risk and update relevant project documentation
Hold a meeting with all stakeholders to agree on solutions after the impact
Request authorization from the project manager to act on the secondary risk
Define and set trigger conditions for the secondary risk
Revise and share the updated assessment of the secondary risk’s impact

x.en:
In this scenario, the secondary risk was already identified, analyzed, accepted, and documented.
Once the secondary risk materializes, it is no longer a potential risk—it becomes an active risk or issue that requires action.

📌 Exam Rule:
When a risk occurs → Implement response + reassess + communicate

en: Assess the contract to determine available resources and funding for the project
Examine the scope of work to identify the required project methodology
Review the policies and practices that are outlined in the risk management plan
Discuss possible upcoming actions with the project team

x.en:
📌 Exam Rule:
When joining an ongoing project, always review existing plans first before engaging or changing direction.


When a risk manager is assigned to an ongoing project, the first priority is to understand how risk management is currently being performed on that project.

The risk management plan is the key document that defines the project’s risk framework, including:


	
	Roles and responsibilities for risk management
	
	
	Risk categories and sources
	
	
	Risk appetite, tolerance, and thresholds
	
	
	Risk identification and analysis techniques
	
	
	Risk response strategies
	
	
	Risk monitoring, reporting, and escalation procedures
	
	
	Risk governance structure
	


Reviewing this plan allows the new risk manager to align with existing policies and practices before proposing changes or taking action.

en: Reviewed the assumptions and exclusions listed in the project charter.
Included general construction-related risks in the risk register prior to starting construction.
Performed risk identification exercises for the full lifecycle of the project.
Conducted a Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis before mobilization.

x.en:
📌 Exam Key Point 
Risk identification should be performed continuously and across all project phases.

Risk identification is not limited to a single phase of the project. It is a continuous process that must be carried out throughout the entire project lifecycle, including design, procurement, construction, and delivery.

In this scenario, the project manager identified risks only during the design phase, which resulted in missing risks related to construction activities, such as material availability and subcontractor readiness.

By performing risk identification exercises for the full lifecycle, the project manager could have anticipated construction-phase risks and documented them in the risk register, allowing for proactive planning and mitigation.

en: The removal of manual steps involved in recording wet signatures.
Professional engineers in your organization express concerns about possible information tampering.
An increasing number of competitors adopt digital signatures.
Management agrees to provide additional resources for the digital signature initiative.
A growing trend of mobile communications within the industry.

x.en:
Because SWOT analysis focuses on identifying internal and external factors that represent Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats:


	 (Threat):


Concerns raised by professional engineers about possible information tampering represent a threat.

Stakeholder resistance related to security, trust, or data integrity can negatively affect adoption, quality, and stakeholder satisfaction.


	
	 (Opportunity):
	


An increasing number of competitors adopting digital signatures represents an opportunity.

It indicates market maturity, industry acceptance, and provides a chance to:


	
	Align with industry standards
	
	
	Improve competitiveness
	
	
	Enhance organizational reputation

en: Assumption log.
Issue log.
Change log.
Risk-adjusted backlog.

x.en:
During the execution phase, especially in Agile or hybrid environments, stakeholders need a mechanism to decide what work should be done next while considering risk exposure.

A risk-adjusted backlog prioritizes backlog items based on:


	
	Risk probability
	
	
	Risk impact
	
	
	Value delivery
	
	
	Uncertainty reduction
	


This allows stakeholders to:


	
	Address high-risk items early
	
	
	Reduce uncertainty as the project progresses
	
	
	Balance value creation and risk mitigation
	
	
	Respond effectively to both known and emerging risks
	


This artifact integrates risk management directly into execution planning, making it ideal for dynamic project environments.

q.en: During an orientation meeting, an executive asks you to clarify the fundamental difference between a project and operational work. What is the most accurate answer?
q.ar: أثناء اجتماع تعريفي، طلب منك مدير تنفيذي توضيح الفرق الجوهري بين المشروع والعمل التشغيلي. ما الإجابة الأدق؟

en: A project is temporary and creates a unique output, while operations are ongoing and repetitive
A project always has a larger budget than operations
Operations need a manager while a project does not
A project has no time constraints
ar: المشروع مؤقت وينتج مخرجًا فريدًا، بينما العمليات مستمرة ومتكررة
المشروع دائمًا أكبر ميزانية من العمليات
العمليات تحتاج مديرًا بينما المشروع لا يحتاج

x.ar:
المشروع مسعى مؤقت له بداية ونهاية وينتج منتجًا أو خدمة أو نتيجة فريدة، أما العمليات فهي أنشطة مستمرة ومتكررة تحافظ على سير الأعمال.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — مجال العمليات | PMBOK® 8 — مناطق التركيز الخمس (4.5) — الدليل ص 70–72 / Guide p.70

q.en: Your organization has a collection of projects and programs that are not technically related but are managed together to achieve strategic objectives. What is this grouping called?
q.ar: لدى مؤسستك مجموعة مشاريع وبرامج غير مترابطة تقنيًا لكنها تُدار معًا لتحقيق الأهداف الاستراتيجية. ماذا يُسمى هذا التجمع؟

en: Program
Portfolio
Megaproject
PMO

x.ar:
المحفظة تجمع مشاريع وبرامج وعمليات لا يُشترط ترابطها، وتُدار معًا لتحقيق الأهداف الاستراتيجية. البرنامج يضم مشاريع مترابطة تُدار بشكل منسق لتحقيق منافع لا تتحقق بإدارتها منفردة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — مجال العمليات | PMBOK® 8 — مناطق التركيز الخمس (4.5) — الدليل ص 70–72 / Guide p.70

q.en: Your organization's PMO enforces standardized methodologies and templates and requires compliance across all projects, but does not directly manage them. What type of PMO is this?
q.ar: مكتب إدارة المشاريع في مؤسستك يفرض منهجيات وقوالب موحدة ويتطلب الامتثال لها في جميع المشاريع، لكنه لا يدير المشاريع مباشرة. ما نوع هذا المكتب؟

en: Supportive
Controlling
Directive
Center of Excellence

x.ar:
المكتب المتحكم يفرض الامتثال للمنهجيات والقوالب والحوكمة. الداعم يقدم استشارات ودروسًا مستفادة دون إلزام، والتوجيهي يدير المشاريع مباشرة ويعيّن مديريها.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م2: تخطيط وإدارة الامتثال | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: You were just appointed 'project coordinator' in a purely functional manufacturing firm. When you asked to free two engineers for the project their functional manager refused, and you found every decision routes through him, your role being closer to administrative follow-up. What explains your position?
q.ar: عُيّنت حديثًا «منسق مشروع» في شركة تصنيع تعمل بهيكل وظيفي صرف. عند طلبك تفريغ مهندسَين للعمل على المشروع رفض مديرهما الوظيفي، واكتشفت أن كل قراراتك تمر عبره وأن دورك أقرب للمتابعة الإدارية. ما الذي يفسر موقفك هذا؟

en: Full authority over resources and budget
Little to no authority; the functional manager controls resources
Equal authority with the functional manager
Authority over budget only, not resources
ar: سلطة منخفضة أو معدومة، والمدير الوظيفي يتحكم بالموارد
سلطة على الميزانية فقط دون الموارد

x.ar:
في الهيكل الوظيفي تكون سلطة مدير المشروع ضعيفة أو شبه معدومة، ويعمل غالبًا كمنسّق، بينما يحتفظ المديرون الوظيفيون بالسيطرة على الموارد والميزانية.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — مجال بيئة الأعمال | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: According to the PMBOK® latest edition, what correctly describes the Value Delivery System?
q.ar: وفق الإصدار الثامن من PMBOK®، ما الذي يصف «نظام إيصال القيمة» (Value Delivery System) بشكل صحيح؟

en: A software program for schedule management
The set of strategic activities (portfolios, programs, projects, operations) working together to create value for the organization and stakeholders
Only the process of delivering the final product to the customer
The project team reward system
ar: مجموعة الأنشطة الاستراتيجية (محافظ وبرامج ومشاريع وعمليات) التي تعمل معًا لبناء القيمة للمؤسسة وأصحاب المصلحة
عملية تسليم المنتج النهائي للعميل فقط

x.ar:
نظام إيصال القيمة يمثل الطريقة التي تُترجم بها الاستراتيجية إلى قيمة عبر المحافظ والبرامج والمشاريع والعمليات والمنتجات، ضمن بيئة الحوكمة المؤسسية.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م3: ضمان التسليم القائم على القيمة | PMBOK® 8 — مبدأ «التركيز على القيمة» (3.4) — الدليل ص 40 / Guide p.40

q.en: A vendor competing for a contract on your project offers you an expensive gift during the evaluation period. According to the PMI Code of Ethics, what is the correct action?
q.ar: عرض عليك أحد الموردين المتنافسين على عقد في مشروعك هديةً ثمينة أثناء فترة التقييم. وفق ميثاق أخلاقيات PMI، ما التصرف الصحيح؟

en: Accept it as long as it does not influence your decision
Politely decline and disclose the incident per organizational policy
Accept it and share it with the team
Ignore the matter without informing anyone
ar: قبولها بشرط عدم التأثير على قرارك
رفضها بأدب والإفصاح عن الواقعة وفق سياسات المؤسسة

x.ar:
قيم الأمانة والإنصاف تقتضي رفض أي شيء قد يمثل تضارب مصالح، مع الإفصاح والشفافية وفق سياسات المؤسسة — خاصة أثناء عملية تقييم عروض.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 — مجال الأشخاص | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء أصحاب المصلحة/الموارد + مبدأ بناء ثقافة ممكّنة

q.en: Your project requirements are clear and stable, the technology is well understood, and the client wants a single documented final delivery. Which life cycle is most appropriate?
q.ar: متطلبات مشروعك واضحة ومستقرة، والتقنية مفهومة، والعميل يريد تسليمًا واحدًا نهائيًا موثقًا. أي دورة حياة هي الأنسب؟

en: Adaptive
Predictive
Purely iterative
Continuous DevOps

x.ar:
وضوح المتطلبات واستقرارها مع رغبة العميل في تسليم واحد نهائي هي المؤشرات الكلاسيكية لاختيار النهج التنبؤي (الشلالي).
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م2: تطوير نطاق المشروع وإدارته | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء النطاق (القسم 2.2) — المعيار ص 35–46 / Std. p.35

q.en: At the end of each phase of a construction project, management meets to decide whether to continue, modify, or stop. What is this point called?
q.ar: في نهاية كل مرحلة من مشروع إنشائي، تعقد الإدارة اجتماعًا لتقرر الاستمرار أو التعديل أو الإيقاف. ماذا تسمى هذه النقطة؟

en: Kickoff meeting
Phase gate
Sprint review
Quality audit

x.ar:
بوابة المرحلة (وتسمى أيضًا مراجعة المرحلة أو نقطة القتل Kill Point) هي نقطة حوكمة تُقيَّم فيها نتائج المرحلة لاتخاذ قرار الاستمرار من عدمه.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م5: تخطيط وإدارة المشتريات | PMBOK® 8 — ملحق X4: المشتريات — ص 245+ / p.245

q.en: In a PM hiring interview, a candidate described the role as 'assigning tasks and tracking schedules.' The panel objected that modern thinking has moved past this. Which statement reflects the PM's pivotal role per current PMI direction?
q.ar: في مقابلة لتوظيف مدير مشاريع، وصف مرشح دوره بأنه «توزيع المهام ومتابعة الجداول». اعترضت لجنة التقييم لأن هذا الوصف تجاوزه الفكر الحديث. أي عبارة تعبّر عن الدور المحوري لمدير المشروع وفق أحدث توجهات PMI؟

en: A technical expert who performs difficult tasks personally
A leader who integrates the work, empowers the team, and focuses on delivering value and outcomes
A monitor who documents errors and escalates them
Merely a contractual intermediary between client and vendors
ar: خبير تقني ينفذ المهام الصعبة بنفسه
قائد يحقق التكامل بين الأعمال ويمكّن الفريق ويركز على إيصال القيمة والنتائج
وسيط تعاقدي بين العميل والموردين فقط

x.ar:
التوجه الحديث يركز على مدير المشروع كقائد ومحقق للتكامل (Integrator) يمكّن الفريق ويوجه الجهد نحو القيمة والنتائج (Outcomes) لا المخرجات فقط.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 — مجال الأشخاص | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الموارد + مبدأ «كن قائدًا خاضعًا للمساءلة»

q.en: While analyzing a new project's environment, a team member confused what the environment imposes on the project with the organization's accumulated knowledge, so you asked him to distinguish with an example. Which of the following is an EEF rather than an OPA?
q.ar: أثناء تحليل بيئة مشروع جديد، خلط أحد أعضاء الفريق بين ما تفرضه البيئة على المشروع وما تملكه المنظمة من معرفة متراكمة، فطلبتَ منه التمييز بمثال. أي مما يلي يُعد من العوامل البيئية للمؤسسة (EEFs) وليس من أصول العمليات التنظيمية (OPAs)؟

en: Templates from previous project plans
Lessons learned register
Government regulations and market conditions
Documented change control procedures

x.ar:
اللوائح الحكومية وظروف السوق وثقافة المؤسسة عوامل بيئية (EEF) تؤثر على المشروع ولا يتحكم بها الفريق، بينما القوالب والإجراءات والدروس المستفادة أصول عمليات تنظيمية (OPA).
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م2: تخطيط وإدارة الامتثال | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: Before approving a new project, the investment committee requests a document that economically justifies the project and shows its feasibility. What is this document?
q.ar: قبل اعتماد مشروع جديد، طلبت لجنة الاستثمار وثيقة تبرر المشروع اقتصاديًا وتوضح جدواه. ما هذه الوثيقة؟

en: Project charter
Business case
Benefits management plan
Scope statement

x.ar:
دراسة حالة العمل هي المبرر الاقتصادي للمشروع (التكلفة مقابل المنفعة والجدوى)، وتُعد أساسًا لاعتماد الميثاق لاحقًا.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م1: تحديد حوكمة المشروع وتأسيسها | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) وملحق X2 — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: Your project is complete and deliverables handed over, but the sponsor asks: 'When and how will we measure actual benefits realization?' Which document answers this?
q.ar: اكتمل مشروعك وسلّمت المخرجات، لكن الراعي يسأل: «متى وكيف سنقيس تحقق الفوائد الفعلية؟». أي وثيقة تجيب عن ذلك؟

en: Benefits management plan
Risk register
Quality management plan
Work performance report

x.ar:
خطة إدارة المنافع تحدد المنافع المستهدفة وتوقيت تحققها ومقاييسها ومالكها، وتمتد غالبًا إلى ما بعد إغلاق المشروع.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م1: تحديد حوكمة المشروع وتأسيسها | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) وملحق X2 — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: Your team plans the near-term phase in great detail while keeping later phases at a high level, elaborating them as information becomes clearer. What is this concept called?
q.ar: يصف فريقك خطة المشروع بتفصيل كبير للمرحلة القريبة، مع إبقاء المراحل البعيدة على مستوى عالٍ يُفصَّل لاحقًا كلما اتضحت المعلومات. ما اسم هذا المفهوم؟

en: Progressive elaboration
Scope creep
Backward planning
Crashing

x.ar:
التوسع التدريجي هو تحسين الخطة وتفصيلها بشكل مستمر كلما توفرت معلومات أدق، ومن تطبيقاته تخطيط الموجات المتدحرجة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — مجال العمليات | PMBOK® 8 — مناطق التركيز الخمس (4.5) — الدليل ص 70–72 / Guide p.70

q.en: A PM review found he consumed shared resources without coordination and ignored his project's environmental and social impacts, saying only 'I delivered scope on time.' Which project management principle did he clearly violate?
q.ar: عند مراجعة قرارات مدير مشروع، وُجد أنه استهلك موارد مشتركة دون تنسيق، وتجاهل أثر مشروعه على البيئة والمجتمع، مكتفيًا بقول «حققتُ النطاق في الوقت المحدد». أي مبدأ من مبادئ إدارة المشاريع أخلّ به بوضوح؟

en: Completing work at the lowest cost by any means
Acting with integrity, care, and trustworthiness internally and externally
Delegating all decisions to the team
Committing only to the schedule
ar: إنجاز العمل بأقل تكلفة مهما كانت الوسيلة
التصرف بأمانة ومسؤولية والتزام بالثقة الممنوحة داخليًا وخارجيًا

x.ar:
مبدأ الإشراف يعني أن يكون الممارس وكيلًا أمينًا مسؤولًا يتصرف بنزاهة واهتمام وامتثال، داخل المؤسسة وخارجها.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م2: تطوير نطاق المشروع وإدارته | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء النطاق (القسم 2.2) — المعيار ص 35–46 / Std. p.35

q.en: Your project has competing constraints. If the client halves the schedule while keeping scope fixed, what is the most likely impact?
q.ar: مشروعك خاضع لقيود متنافسة. إذا قرر العميل تقليص الجدول الزمني للنصف مع بقاء النطاق ثابتًا، فما الأثر الأكثر ترجيحًا؟

en: Cost automatically decreases
Cost and/or risk increase to maintain the scope
No impact at all
Quality automatically improves
ar: ارتفاع التكلفة و/أو المخاطر للحفاظ على النطاق

x.ar:
القيود متشابكة: ضغط الجدول مع ثبات النطاق يتطلب موارد إضافية (تكلفة أعلى) أو يرفع المخاطر وقد يهدد الجودة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م2: تطوير نطاق المشروع وإدارته | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء النطاق (القسم 2.2) — المعيار ص 35–46 / Std. p.35

q.en: Your project stalled over an authority dispute between two departments and funding gaps for the next phase. A consultant told you: 'This battle isn't the PM's to win — it belongs to whoever defends the project before senior management, funds it, and approved its charter.' Who is he referring to?
q.ar: توقف مشروعك بسبب نزاع صلاحيات بين إدارتين ونقص تمويل للمرحلة القادمة. قال لك مستشار: «هذه معركة لا يحسمها مديرُ المشروع، بل مَن يملك الدفاع عن المشروع أمام الإدارة العليا ويوفر تمويله وقد اعتمد ميثاقه أصلًا». عمّن يتحدث؟

en: Project manager
Sponsor
Product owner
Program manager

x.ar:
الراعي هو من يوفر الموارد والدعم ويتحمل مساءلة نجاح المشروع على مستوى المؤسسة، ويصدر/يعتمد الميثاق ويمنح مدير المشروع سلطته.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 — الأشخاص م2: إدارة النزاعات | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء أصحاب المصلحة/الموارد + مبدأ بناء ثقافة ممكّنة

q.en: Your project delivered a new e-system (output), but management asks about the 40% reduction in transaction time (outcome). What distinction is management pointing to?
q.ar: سلّم مشروعك نظامًا إلكترونيًا جديدًا (مخرَج)، لكن الإدارة تسأل عن انخفاض زمن إنجاز المعاملات بنسبة 40% (نتيجة). ما الفرق الذي تشير إليه الإدارة؟

en: The difference between outputs and outcomes
The difference between quality and grade
The difference between scope and time
The difference between risks and issues
ar: الفرق بين المخرجات Outputs والنتائج Outcomes

x.ar:
المخرَج هو المنتج الملموس، بينما النتيجة هي الأثر والقيمة الناتجة عن استخدامه. التركيز الحديث في إدارة المشاريع على النتائج والقيمة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م3: ضمان التسليم القائم على القيمة | PMBOK® 8 — مبدأ «التركيز على القيمة» (3.4) — الدليل ص 40 / Guide p.40

q.en: Which PMBOK® project performance domain addresses building effective relationships with parties who influence or are affected by the project?
q.ar: أي مجال من مجالات أداء المشروع في PMBOK® يُعنى بأنشطة بناء علاقات فعالة مع الأطراف المؤثرة والمتأثرة بالمشروع؟

en: Team performance domain
Stakeholder performance domain
Measurement performance domain
Uncertainty performance domain

x.ar:
مجال أداء أصحاب المصلحة يركز على تحديدهم وفهمهم وإشراكهم بفعالية طوال المشروع لبناء علاقات إيجابية ومواءمة التوقعات.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — مجال العمليات | PMBOK® 8 — مناطق التركيز الخمس (4.5) — الدليل ص 70–72 / Guide p.70

q.en: You notice your project decisions require approval from a steering committee that defines authorities, accountability, and escalation paths. What is this framework called?
q.ar: لاحظت أن قرارات مشروعك تحتاج اعتمادًا من لجنة توجيهية تحدد الصلاحيات والمساءلة وآلية التصعيد. ما اسم هذا الإطار؟

en: Project governance
Organizational change management
Configuration management
Resource planning

x.ar:
حوكمة المشروع هي إطار الصلاحيات والمساءلة والرقابة واتخاذ القرار والتصعيد الذي يعمل المشروع ضمنه، وتتوافق مع حوكمة المؤسسة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م1: تحديد حوكمة المشروع وتأسيسها | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) وملحق X2 — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: At the project approval committee, a manager defended his project saying 'we will deliver a massive technical system.' The chair replied: 'We don't invest in outputs, but in what they return to the organization.' Which best expresses what the chair means by 'business value'?
q.ar: في لجنة اعتماد المشاريع، دافع مدير عن مشروعه بقوله «سنسلّم نظامًا تقنيًا ضخمًا»، فردّ رئيس اللجنة: «لا نستثمر في مخرجات، بل فيما تعود به على المنظمة». أي مما يلي أفضل تعبير عمّا يقصده الرئيس بـ«قيمة الأعمال»؟

en: Financial return only
The net quantifiable and intangible benefit (financial, reputation, customer satisfaction, new capabilities)
The number of deliverables produced
The size of the project team
ar: صافي المنفعة الملموسة وغير الملموسة (مالية، سمعة، رضا عملاء، قدرات جديدة)

x.ar:
قيمة الأعمال تشمل المنافع الملموسة (إيرادات، توفير) وغير الملموسة (سمعة، علامة تجارية، رضا) التي تعود على المؤسسة وأصحاب المصلحة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م1: تحديد حوكمة المشروع وتأسيسها | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) وملحق X2 — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: A new employee asks you to clarify the difference between the 'project team' and the 'project management team'. What is correct?
q.ar: طلب منك موظف جديد توضيح الفرق بين «فريق المشروع» و«فريق إدارة المشروع». ما الإجابة الصحيحة؟

en: There is no difference at all
The project management team is a subset of the project team performing management and leadership activities
The project team is a subset of the management team
The management team includes external stakeholders
ar: فريق إدارة المشروع جزء من فريق المشروع يتولى أنشطة الإدارة والقيادة
فريق المشروع جزء من فريق الإدارة
فريق الإدارة يضم أصحاب المصلحة الخارجيين

x.ar:
فريق المشروع يضم كل من يؤدي عمل المشروع، وفريق إدارة المشروع هو الجزء المسؤول عن أنشطة الإدارة (التخطيط، الرقابة، القيادة).
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 — الأشخاص م3: قيادة فريق المشروع | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الموارد + مبدأ «كن قائدًا خاضعًا للمساءلة»

q.en: In an app development project, requirements are vague, technology is new, and the client wants to see early working versions and give continuous feedback. Which approach fits best?
q.ar: في مشروع لتطوير تطبيق، المتطلبات غامضة والتقنية جديدة والعميل يريد رؤية نسخ عمل مبكرة وتقديم ملاحظات مستمرة. ما النهج الأنسب؟

en: Predictive
Adaptive (agile)
Strict waterfall
No approach needed

x.ar:
غموض المتطلبات وتغيرها المتوقع والحاجة لتغذية راجعة مبكرة ومستمرة مؤشرات قوية لاختيار النهج التكيفي القائم على التكرارات.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م2: تطوير نطاق المشروع وإدارته | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء النطاق (القسم 2.2) — المعيار ص 35–46 / Std. p.35

q.en: Two projects in your organization finished exactly on time and budget; users abandoned the first within months while the second raised revenue 15%. The CEO asked for a broader project success criterion that explains this gap. What is it per modern PMI thinking?
q.ar: سلّم مشروعان في مؤسستك في الوقت والميزانية المحددين تمامًا؛ الأول هجره المستخدمون خلال أشهر، والثاني رفع إيرادات المنظمة 15%. طلب الرئيس التنفيذي معيارًا أشمل للحكم على نجاح المشاريع يفسّر هذا الفارق. ما هذا المعيار وفق الفكر الحديث لـ PMI؟

en: Meeting time and cost only
Achieving intended value, outcomes, and stakeholder satisfaction in addition to performance objectives
Having no changes to the plan
Spending the entire budget
ar: تحقيق القيمة والنتائج المستهدفة ورضا أصحاب المصلحة إضافة إلى أهداف الأداء
عدم وجود أي تغييرات على الخطة

x.ar:
النجاح الحديث يقاس بتحقيق القيمة والنتائج المرجوة ورضا أصحاب المصلحة، وليس فقط بالالتزام بالقيود الثلاثية.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م3: ضمان التسليم القائم على القيمة | PMBOK® 8 — مبدأ «التركيز على القيمة» (3.4) — الدليل ص 40 / Guide p.40

q.en: The PMO noticed one PM of a small low-risk project applied every template and process of the full methodology literally, drowning the team in documentation, while another streamlined processes to fit his project's size. The PMO backed the second based on the 'Tailoring' principle, which means:
q.ar: لاحظ مكتب إدارة المشاريع أن مدير مشروع صغير منخفض المخاطر طبّق كل قوالب وعمليات المنهجية الكاملة حرفيًا فأغرق الفريق بالتوثيق، بينما بسّط آخر عملياته بما يناسب حجم مشروعه. أيّد المكتب الثاني استنادًا إلى مبدأ «التكييف Tailoring» الذي يعني:

en: Applying every process and tool to every project without exception
Selecting and adjusting the approach, processes, and tools to fit the project context, size, and organizational culture
Designing team uniforms
Copying a previous project's methodology as-is
ar: تطبيق كل العمليات والأدوات في كل مشروع دون استثناء
اختيار وتعديل النهج والعمليات والأدوات بما يناسب سياق المشروع وحجمه وثقافة المؤسسة
نسخ منهجية مشروع سابق كما هي

x.ar:
التكييف هو ملاءمة منهجية الإدارة (عمليات، أدوات، دورة حياة، حوكمة) لخصائص كل مشروع؛ فلا يوجد نهج واحد يناسب الجميع.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م5: تخطيط المخاطر وإدارتها | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء المخاطر (القسم 2.7) — المعيار ص 92–102 / Std. p.92

q.en: A startup operates in a projectized structure. Which is true?
q.ar: شركة ناشئة تعمل بهيكل تنظيمي مشاريعي (Projectized). أي مما يلي صحيح؟

en: The PM has high authority and the team is dedicated full-time
The functional manager controls the budget
There are no project managers
Staff report back to their departments daily
ar: مدير المشروع يملك سلطة عالية والفريق متفرغ له بالكامل

x.ar:
في الهيكل المشاريعي تتمحور المؤسسة حول المشاريع؛ فيتمتع مدير المشروع بسلطة شبه كاملة على الموارد والميزانية ويكون الفريق متفرغًا.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 11–12 / p.11–12) — بيئة الأعمال م2: تخطيط وإدارة الامتثال | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء الحوكمة (القسم 2.1) — المعيار ص 10–34 / Std. p.10

q.en: You discover a colleague is inflating progress reports sent to the client. Per PMI values (responsibility, respect, fairness, honesty), what is the most appropriate first action?
q.ar: اكتشفت أن زميلًا يضخّم تقارير نسب الإنجاز المقدمة للعميل. وفق قيم PMI (مسؤولية، احترام، إنصاف، أمانة)، ما أول تصرف مناسب؟

en: Ignore it since it is not your project
Address it with the colleague to correct the reports, then escalate through formal channels if it continues
Inform the client directly before any internal step
Spread the matter among colleagues
ar: مواجهة الزميل ومناقشة تصحيح التقارير، ثم التصعيد عبر القنوات الرسمية إن استمر
إبلاغ العميل مباشرة قبل أي خطوة داخلية

x.ar:
الأمانة والمسؤولية تقتضيان معالجة السلوك غير الأخلاقي؛ يبدأ ذلك بالمواجهة المهنية المباشرة ثم التصعيد الرسمي عند الحاجة.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 — الأشخاص م8: تخطيط وإدارة التواصل | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء أصحاب المصلحة/الموارد + مبدأ بناء ثقافة ممكّنة

q.en: Two teams presented product plans: the first builds a rough complete model then refines it cycle after cycle to maturity; the second delivers usable finished pieces that accumulate. The sponsor asked for a precise methodological distinction. Which correctly describes 'iterative' versus 'incremental' life cycles?
q.ar: عرض عليك فريقان خطتيهما لتطوير منتج: الأول يبني نموذجًا كاملًا مبدئيًا ثم يعيد صقله دورة بعد دورة حتى النضج، والثاني يسلّم أجزاء مكتملة قابلة للاستخدام تتراكم تباعًا. طلب الراعي توصيف الفارق المنهجي بدقة. أي وصف صحيح لدورة الحياة «التكرارية» مقارنة بـ«التزايدية»؟

en: Iterative refines the product through successive cycles to clarify it, while incremental delivers usable finished pieces successively
They are exactly the same concept
Incremental delivers nothing until the end
Iterative is used only in construction
ar: التكرارية تحسّن المنتج عبر دورات متتالية لتوضيح الفكرة، والتزايدية تسلّم أجزاء مكتملة قابلة للاستخدام تباعًا
التكرارية والتزايدية مصطلحان لنفس المفهوم تمامًا
التزايدية لا تسلّم شيئًا حتى النهاية

x.ar:
التكرار يعيد العمل على النسخة نفسها لتحسينها وتوضيح المتطلبات، بينما التزايد يضيف أجزاء مكتملة وظيفيًا تسلَّم تدريجيًا. الرشيق يجمع الاثنين.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 (ص 9–10 / p.9–10) — العمليات م2: تطوير نطاق المشروع وإدارته | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء النطاق (القسم 2.2) — المعيار ص 35–46 / Std. p.35

q.en: At the start of a sensitive project, your team identifies a highly influential person who opposes the project. What is the best timing and approach?
q.ar: في بداية مشروع حساس، حدد فريقك شخصًا مؤثرًا جدًا يعارض المشروع. ما أفضل توقيت وأسلوب للتعامل معه؟

en: Ignore them until they formally object
Engage them early, understand their concerns, and set an appropriate engagement plan
Remove them from communication lists
Assign a junior member to monitor them
ar: إشراكه مبكرًا وفهم مخاوفه ووضع خطة إشراك مناسبة

x.ar:
أصحاب المصلحة عالو التأثير المعارضون يُشرَكون مبكرًا وبشكل استباقي؛ فهم مخاوفهم قد يحوّلهم لداعمين ويقلل مخاطر المشروع.
📖 المرجع: ECO 2026 — الأشخاص م4: إشراك أصحاب المصلحة | PMBOK® 8 — مجال أداء أصحاب المصلحة (القسم 2.5 من المعيار)
